senses.title: Stuff used to build or make
senses.titleCN: 用来建造或制作的材料
senses.definition: the substance out of which something is made or built
senses.definitionCN: 用来制造或建造某物的物质
senses.example: Bricks and timber were the material of the old bridge.
senses.exampleCN: 砖与木料是这座老桥的材料。
senses.why: Late Latin materialis was simply the adjective of materia 'stuff', so the noun kept the plain sense of the stuff itself.
senses.whyCN: 晚期拉丁 materialis 就是 materia「材料」的形容词，名词义因此保留了「料本身」这层直白意思。

senses.title: Cloth for sewing
senses.definition: fabric used for making clothes or furnishings
senses.definitionCN: 用来做衣服或家居用品的布料
senses.example: The tailor spread the material and cut along the chalk line.
senses.exampleCN: 裁缝把布料铺开，沿粉线裁剪。
senses.why: cloth was the material a household handled most often, so the word narrowed to fabric in everyday speech.
senses.whyCN: 布料是家庭最常打交道的材料，于是这个词在日常口语中收窄为「织物」。

senses.title: Facts and sources for a work
senses.definition: information, notes or sources used for writing, research or a report
senses.definitionCN: 用于写作、研究或报道的信息、笔记与来源
senses.example: The reporter gathered material for the story over three weeks.
senses.exampleCN: 记者用三周时间为这篇报道收集素材。
senses.why: what clay is to a pot, notes are to an article, so the same word covers the raw stuff of a text.
senses.whyCN: 黏土之于陶罐，正如笔记之于文章，于是同一个词也指文本的原料。

senses.title: Supplies and equipment
senses.definition: the things needed for a particular activity, usually in the plural
senses.definitionCN: 某项活动所需的物品，通常用复数
senses.example: The laboratory ordered its materials for the autumn term.
senses.exampleCN: 实验室订购了秋季学期要用的用品。
senses.why: in the plural the word counts separate items rather than an uncountable stuff, a shift English makes freely with substances.
senses.whyCN: 复数把不可数的「料」转成一件件可数的东西，英语对物质名词常有这种转换。

senses.title: Physical rather than spiritual
senses.titleCN: 物质层面的，与精神相对
senses.definition: belonging to the physical world rather than to thought or spirit
senses.definitionCN: 属于物理世界，而非思想或精神世界
senses.example: The material world still obeys physical law.
senses.exampleCN: 物质世界依然服从物理规律。
senses.why: the adjective kept the old opposition of stuff to spirit, so it describes whatever can be touched.
senses.whyCN: 形容词保留了「材料对精神」的古老对举，因此描述一切摸得着的东西。

senses.title: Important to a decision
senses.definition: significant enough to affect a decision, a contract or a judgment
senses.definitionCN: 重要到足以影响决定、合同或判断的
senses.example: The delay was material to the terms of the contract.
senses.exampleCN: 这次延误对合同条款有实质影响。
senses.why: law and accounting borrowed the word because a fact with real stuff in it can change an outcome.
senses.whyCN: 法律与会计借用这个词，因为有实体内容的事实才足以改变结果。

senses.title: Concerned with wealth
senses.definition: interested in money and possessions rather than in higher aims
senses.definitionCN: 看重金钱与财物而非更高追求
senses.example: They chased material gain and ignored the damage.
senses.exampleCN: 他们追逐物质利益，无视造成的损害。
senses.why: if the material world is what can be touched, then gain in that world is money and goods.
senses.whyCN: 既然物质世界就是摸得着的那一面，那么那一面的收获自然就是钱与物。

senses.title: A person suited to a role
senses.definition: a person considered as suitable raw stuff for a particular post or task
senses.definitionCN: 被看作适合某项职位或任务的「生料」
senses.example: She is good material for the debate team.
senses.exampleCN: 她是辩论队的好苗子。
senses.why: a person is treated as raw stuff to be shaped by training, which keeps the oldest sense of material alive in a comic way.
senses.whyCN: 人被当成可被训练塑造的生料，这以略带戏谑的方式保留了 material 最古老的意思。

intro.en: Material is Late Latin materialis, the adjective of materia 'stuff', which passed through Old French into English. Its parent noun is the same source as matter.
intro.cn: material 是晚期拉丁 materialis，即 materia「材料」的形容词，经古法语进入英语；其母名词与 matter 同源。

items.en: Materia meant timber, stuff and subject matter; the adjective materialis was formed on it in later Latin.
items.cn: materia 指木料、材料与题材；形容词 materialis 是晚期拉丁语在它之上构成的。

items.en: Materialis meant 'of matter, physical' and was used in philosophy to contrast the physical with the spiritual.
items.cn: materialis 意为「物质的、物理的」，在哲学中用来与精神相对。

items.en: Old French material brought the adjective and noun into English in the thirteenth and fourteenth centuries.
items.cn: 古法语 material 在十三、十四世纪把这个形容词与名词带入英语。

items.en: By the sixteenth century material was the ordinary word for cloth in a household, a sense that still survives in tailoring.
items.cn: 到十六世纪，material 已是家庭里指布料的常用词，这一义至今留在裁缝行当。

items.en: Modern law and accounting use 'material' for facts that can shift a decision, an extension of the idea of having real substance.
items.cn: 现代法律与会计用 material 指能改变决定的事实，这是「有实质」这一想法的延伸。

items.en: First recorded dates for the cloth, legal and accounting senses are approximate; the core adjective is well attested from the fourteenth century.
items.cn: 布料义、法律义与会计义的最早记录年代为约数；核心形容词义在十四世纪已有充分书证。

note.en: The first group holds near-forms of material, some sharing its Latin stock and some not; the second group holds words that overlap in meaning.
note.cn: 第一组是与 material 形近的词，有的同出拉丁词源，有的不是；第二组是词义部分重叠的词。

entries.definition: The noun and verb built directly on materia; material is its learned adjective, so the two share a root but not a part of speech.
entries.definitionCN: 直接由 materia 构成的名词与动词；material 是它的书面形容词，二者同根而词性不同。

entries.definition: The same word borrowed a second time from French and narrowed to military stores; it is not a separate root.
entries.definitionCN: 同一个词第二次从法语借入，收窄为军用物资；并非另一个词根。

entries.definition: From mater 'mother', not materia; any family resemblance rests on the unproven mater-materia hypothesis.
entries.definitionCN: 出自 mater「母亲」而非 materia；所谓亲缘只建立在那条未获证实的假说上。

entries.definition: The adverb of material, used for 'to a significant degree'; it is a derived form, not a separate word.
entries.definitionCN: material 的副词，表示「达到显著程度」；它是派生形式，不是另一个词。

entries.definition: Material seen as the thing that underlies qualities; substance is more abstract and less countable.
entries.definitionCN: 被看作承载属性的材料；substance 更抽象、更不可数。

entries.definition: Cloth made by weaving; it covers only the textile sense of material.
entries.definitionCN: 织成的布；只覆盖 material 的织物义。

entries.definition: One of the substances combined in a mixture; material is the broader word for what anything is made of.
entries.definitionCN: 混合物中的一种成分；material 是更宽泛的「造物之料」。

entries.definition: Facts that support a conclusion; it overlaps the legal sense of material but not the sense of source material.
entries.definitionCN: 支持结论的事实；与 material 的法律义部分重叠，但不指写作素材。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real Latin source, the real word family and real fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的拉丁来源、真实的同族词与真实的固定搭配。

normal.en: Materialis is the Latin adjective of materia, so material is literally 'of stuff'.
normal.cn: materialis 是 materia 的拉丁形容词，因此 material 字面上就是「属于材料的」。

normal.en: The family runs material, materially, materiality, materialism and materialize.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 material、materially、materiality、materialism 与 materialize。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the physical sense: raw material, building material, material world.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出物质义：原材料、建筑材料、物质世界。

normal.en: In law, a material fact is one that can change the outcome.
normal.cn: 在法律里，具有实质性的关键事实才能改变结果。

normal.en: The same Latin stock gives matter, and material is its adjective.
normal.cn: 同一拉丁词源也给出 matter，而 material 是它的形容词。

abstract.en: Picture a cutting table where the cloth decides what the coat can become.
abstract.cn: 想象一张裁床，布料本身决定了这件外套能做成什么样。

abstract.en: Picture a potter's hands choosing clay before any shape is attempted.
abstract.cn: 想象陶匠在动手塑形之前先挑泥料。

abstract.en: Picture a folder of notes that a writer keeps beside the blank page.
abstract.cn: 想象作家把一叠笔记放在空白稿纸旁边。

examples.en: Recycled material now accounts for a third of the plant's input.
examples.cn: 回收材料现在占这家工厂投入的三分之一。

examples.en: The committee judged the omission material to the audit.
examples.cn: 委员会认定这处遗漏对审计有实质影响。

examples.en: Course material is posted online before each lecture.
examples.cn: 课程材料在每次讲课前发布到网上。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「买铁料」——盖房装修先买铁、买料，买的都是材料 → 材料、原料

root: 拉丁 materia「材料、木料」→ 晚期拉丁 materialis（materia 加形容词后缀）「物质的」→ 古法语 material → 英语 material；「布料」「重要」义由「做成东西的料」再引申。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all treat something as the stuff a thing is made from: bricks for a bridge, cloth for a coat, notes for a story, supplies for a term, the physical world for the spirit, facts for a decision, money for a life, and a person for a post.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都把某物当作「造物之料」：桥的砖、外套的布、报道的笔记、学期的用品、对抗精神的物质世界、影响决定的实据、支撑生活的钱财，以及适合某职位的人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: cloth on a cutting table, waiting to become something else.
core.cn: 核心意象：裁床上的一匹布，等着被做成别的什么。

branches.en: THE STOCK ITSELF: raw stuff in bulk, and the same stuff counted out as supplies for a term.
branches.cn: 原料本身：成批的生料，以及按学期点清的同一种用品。

branches.en: THE CLOTH ON THE TABLE: the material a household handles most often is fabric.
branches.cn: 桌上的那匹布：家庭最常打交道的材料就是织物。

branches.en: THE MATERIAL OF A TEXT: notes and sources are clay for a writer's pot.
branches.cn: 文本的料：笔记与来源是作家制陶的黏土。

branches.en: THE TOUCHABLE WORLD AND ITS GAINS: what can be touched, and what can be accumulated from it.
branches.cn: 可触摸的世界及其收获：摸得着的那一面，以及从那一面攒下的东西。

branches.en: STUFF THAT DECIDES: a fact with substance changes a contract, and a person with substance fills a post.
branches.cn: 起决定作用的料：有实质的事实能改动合同，有实质的人能补上职位。

intro.en: Material is one Latin root plus one adjective suffix, and both parts recur across a large English family.
intro.cn: material 由一个拉丁词根加一个形容词后缀构成，这两部分在英语的一大批词里反复出现。

latinIntro.en: Latin materia gives matter and material; the suffix -alis, through French -al, also shapes manual, editorial and commercial.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 materia 衍生 matter 与 material；后缀 -alis 经法语 -al 也构成 manual、editorial 与 commercial。

items.example: The root supplies the picture of raw stuff.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根提供「生料」的画面。

items.example: The suffix makes an adjective of stuff.
items.exampleCN: 后缀把「材料」变成形容词。

items.example: Material carries both the physical and the serious sense.
items.exampleCN: material 兼有物质与重要两义。

items.example: The same ending appears in manual and editorial.
items.exampleCN: 同一词尾出现在 manual 与 editorial 中。

items.meaning: the quality of being material or significant
items.example: Auditors test materiality before they test figures.
items.exampleCN: 审计师先判断重要性，再核对数字。

items.meaning: the belief that matter is all there is
items.meaningCN: 认为物质即一切的学说
items.example: The suffix turns a quality into a doctrine.
items.exampleCN: 后缀把一种性质变成一种主义。

items.example: The design materialized as a real bridge.
items.exampleCN: 设计落实成了一座真实的桥。

items.example: The prefix denies both the stuff and the weight.
items.exampleCN: 否定前缀同时否掉「实体」与「分量」。

items.example: A second borrowing narrowed to army stores.
items.exampleCN: 第二次借入的形收窄为军队物资。

definition_zh: 微不足道的；可忽略不计的；微小的；无关紧要的
definition_en: so small or unimportant that it can be ignored, especially in a calculation or judgement
core_image: 天平一端放着一整袋米，另一端只落了一粒芝麻，指针几乎没有动。
scene: 工程师盯着检测报告说，这点误差不会影响桥梁的承重判断。 The error is negligible and will not affect the bridge's load estimate.
sceneCN: 这里 negligible 是“小到可以忽略不计的”（第 1 个义项）；句意：这点误差微不足道，不会影响桥梁的承重估算。

pos.zh: 微不足道的；可忽略不计的；微小的；无关紧要的

疏忽；失职

senses.title: Small enough to ignore
senses.titleCN: 微不足道：小到不必理会
senses.definition: so slight or unimportant that it need not be considered
senses.definitionCN: 轻微或不重要到无须纳入考虑
senses.example: The dent in the door was negligible and could be left as it was.
senses.exampleCN: 门上的凹痕微不足道，可以保持原样。
senses.why: The word does not measure size by itself; it measures the size against a purpose, and finds it below the level where action is required.
senses.whyCN: 这个词本身不衡量大小，而是把大小放到某个目的旁边衡量，判定它低于需要采取行动的水平。

senses.title: A quantity too small to count
senses.titleCN: 数量微小：多它一个也不变结果
senses.definition: a quantity so small that adding or removing it changes nothing measurable
senses.definitionCN: 数量极小，增加或去掉都改变不了可测量的结果
senses.example: The impurity occurs in a negligible quantity, below one part per million.
senses.exampleCN: 这种杂质的含量微乎其微，低于百万分之一。
senses.why: In measurement the threshold of the instrument sets the line: below that line the quantity exists but cannot affect the reading.
senses.whyCN: 在测量中，仪器的阈值划出这条线：低于这条线的数量虽存在，却影响不了读数。

senses.title: A difference not worth arguing about
senses.titleCN: 差异可忽略：差一点点，不算差
senses.definition: a difference between two things that is too small to matter in practice
senses.definitionCN: 两事物之间的差异过小，在实践中无关紧要
senses.example: The two coatings differed by a negligible margin in wear tests.
senses.exampleCN: 两种涂层在磨损测试中的差距可忽略不计。
senses.why: Comparing two results invites the question 'does it matter?'; negligible answers no, and so closes the comparison without denying the difference.
senses.whyCN: 比较两个结果会引出“这要紧吗”的问题；negligible 回答“不要紧”，从而在不否认差异的前提下结束比较。

senses.title: A risk that can be accepted
senses.titleCN: 风险极低：可以接受，不必防范
senses.definition: a level of danger low enough that no further protection is thought necessary
senses.definitionCN: 危险程度低到被认为无须再采取额外防护
senses.example: Health officials called the exposure risk negligible for local residents.
senses.exampleCN: 卫生官员称当地居民面临的暴露风险极低。
senses.why: Risk language adds a decision: when a hazard is negligible, the cost of guarding against it is judged higher than the hazard itself.
senses.whyCN: 风险语言加入了一层决定：当危害 negligible 时，防范它的成本被判定为高于危害本身。

senses.title: Cost one barely notices
senses.titleCN: 成本可忽略：花了也像没花
senses.definition: an expense small in relation to the budget or benefit involved
senses.definitionCN: 相对于预算或收益而言小到几乎可以不计的开支
senses.example: The extra memory is a negligible cost compared with the processor.
senses.exampleCN: 与处理器相比，增加的内存成本可以忽略。
senses.why: Money becomes negligible only against a larger figure; the adjective always implies a scale that makes one item fade.
senses.whyCN: 只有对照更大的数字，金钱才显得 negligible；这个形容词总暗含一个让某项淡出的尺度。

senses.title: An effect too faint to detect
senses.titleCN: 作用微弱：发生了，却看不出
senses.definition: an influence so weak that its results cannot be distinguished from noise
senses.definitionCN: 影响弱到其结果无法与噪声区分
senses.example: The second variable had a negligible effect on the final score.
senses.exampleCN: 第二个变量对最终得分的影响微乎其微。
senses.why: An effect is judged against background variation; if it hides inside the noise, it is negligible even if it is real.
senses.whyCN: 作用是对照背景波动来判断的；如果它藏在噪声里，即使真实存在也算 negligible。

senses.title: Not statistically significant
senses.titleCN: 统计上不显著：样本里看不出来
senses.definition: too small, relative to variation, for a statistical test to call it significant
senses.definitionCN: 相对于数据波动太小，统计检验无法判为显著
senses.example: The difference in recovery rates was negligible at the chosen confidence level.
senses.exampleCN: 在所选的置信水平上，康复率的差异在统计上可忽略。
senses.why: Statistical judgement compares an effect with the spread of the data; a negligible difference is one the test cannot separate from chance.
senses.whyCN: 统计判断把效应与数据离散度相比；negligible 的差异就是检验无法与偶然区分开的差异。

senses.title: Safe to drop from a model
senses.titleCN: 可省略：近似计算里直接划掉
senses.definition: small enough in a model or approximation that the term containing it can be omitted
senses.definitionCN: 在模型或近似中足够小，可以删去含它的那一项
senses.example: For slow speeds, the relativistic correction is negligible.
senses.exampleCN: 在低速情况下，相对论修正项可忽略不计。
senses.why: Here the word is an instruction: drop the term, and the error introduced stays inside the tolerance the model already accepts.
senses.whyCN: 这里的词是一道指令：删掉该项，引入的误差仍落在模型本来就接受的容差之内。

intro.en: Negligible comes from French négligible, from the verb négliger, to neglect. That verb goes back to Latin neglegere, to disregard, literally 'not to pick up'.
intro.cn: negligible 来自法语 négligible，出自动词 négliger“忽视”。该动词上溯至拉丁语 neglegere“不理会”，字面意思是“不去捡起”。

items.en: Neglegere combined nec- 'not' with legere 'to pick up or choose'. To neglect was literally to leave something lying there, unpicked.
items.cn: neglegere 由 nec-“不”与 legere“捡起、选择”组合而成。忽视就是字面上让某物躺在那儿，不去捡。

items.en: The adjective meant that could be disregarded. Latin used it for things one was entitled to leave out of account.
items.cn: 形容词形式意为“可以被不理会”。拉丁语用它指那些有权不计入考虑范围的事物。

items.en: Old French négliger kept the sense of neglecting a duty or a thing, and added the idea of carelessness in appearance and dress.
items.cn: 古法语 négliger 保留了“疏于职责或事物”的意思，并增加了外表与衣着上的随意、不修边幅之义。

items.en: French formed négligible as 'that may be neglected'. English took the word over in the 18th century with the quantitative sense already attached.
items.cn: 法语造出 négligible，意为“可以忽略的”。英语在 18 世纪借入时，数量化的含义已经附着在词上。

items.en: English negligible first meant 'disregardable', then settled into the modern sense of a quantity or effect too small to matter.
items.cn: 英语 negligible 最初意为“可不予理会的”，随后固定为现代义：数量或作用小到无关紧要。

items.en: Statistics and engineering made the word a standard label for effects below a stated threshold, as in negligible risk and negligible error.
items.cn: 统计学与工程学使该词成为“低于既定阈值”的标准标签，如 negligible risk、negligible error。

note.en: The first group is the neglect family; the second compares words for smallness and unimportance, each with a different standard.
note.cn: 第一组是 neglect 词族；第二组比较表示“小”与“不重要”的词，各自标准不同。

entries.definition: to fail to care for or attend to something. It names the act of leaving it undone.
entries.definitionCN: 未能照料或处理某事；命名的是“放着不管”的行为。

entries.definition: a failure to take proper care, especially as a breach of duty. It carries responsibility.
entries.definitionCN: 未尽应有注意，尤指失职；带有责任意味。

entries.definition: careless about a duty or about safety. It describes a person or an act, not a size.
entries.definitionCN: 对职责或安全疏忽的；描述人或行为，而非大小。

entries.definition: lacking meaning, influence, or importance. It judges significance rather than size.
entries.definitionCN: 缺乏意义、影响或重要性；判断的是意义而非大小。

entries.definition: of little worth or consequence. It often carries a tone of dismissal.
entries.definitionCN: 价值或后果很小；常带轻视语气。

entries.definition: at the edge of what matters, or very slight. It suggests a border rather than a vanishing point.
entries.definitionCN: 处在重要性的边缘，或非常轻微；暗示边界而非消失点。

entries.definition: extremely small in size or amount. It states smallness without yet saying it can be ignored.
entries.definitionCN: 尺寸或数量极小；只陈述小，还未说可以忽略。

normalIntro.en: Real parts only: neglegere, to not pick up, plus -ible, 'able to be'. Negligible means 'able to be left lying there'.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实成分：neglegere“不去捡起”，加 -ible“可以被……”。negligible 就是“可以被搁在那儿不管的”。

normal.en: Negligible = neglect + able: small enough that neglect is allowed.
normal.cn: negligible 等于 neglect 加 able：小到“可以 neglect（不管）”。

normal.en: One sesame seed on one side of the scale moves the needle by almost nothing.
normal.cn: 天平一端只放一粒芝麻，指针几乎不动。

normal.en: Below the instrument's threshold, a quantity is real but negligible.
normal.cn: 低于仪器阈值时，数量真实存在，但可忽略。

normal.en: Negligible risk means the guard costs more than the danger.
normal.cn: 风险可忽略，意味着防护的成本高于危险本身。

normal.en: In a physics model, negligible is a permit to delete the term.
normal.cn: 在物理模型里，negligible 就是允许你删掉那一项的通行证。

abstract.en: Negligible is never a fact about the world alone; it is a fact about a purpose, a threshold, and a decision.
abstract.cn: negligible 从来不只是关于世界的事实；它关于一个目的、一条阈值和一次决定。

abstract.en: What is negligible to one observer is the whole signal to another with a finer instrument.
abstract.cn: 对一个观察者可忽略的东西，对另一个拿着更精细仪器的人可能就是全部信号。

abstract.en: The word quietly forgives neglect: it says the thing was not worth picking up in the first place.
abstract.cn: 这个词悄悄为“忽视”开脱：它说那东西本来就不值得弯腰去捡。

examples.en: The warming effect of the extra lamp was negligible beside the heat already in the room.
examples.cn: 与房间里已有的热量相比，那盏额外灯管的加热作用微不足道。

examples.en: The two drugs differ by a negligible margin in the trial, so cost becomes the deciding factor.
examples.cn: 两种药在试验中的差距可忽略，因此成本成了决定因素。

examples.en: For a first model, we treat the friction of the pulley as negligible and check the error later.
examples.cn: 在初版模型中，我们把滑轮的摩擦视为可忽略，事后再检验误差。

dict_mnemonic.text: negligible 里有 neglect（忽视）的影子——小到可以直接忽视，就是“微不足道”。

root: 源自法语 négligible，出自 négliger（忽视），上溯拉丁语 neglegere：nec-“不”+ legere“捡起、选择”，字面为“不去捡起”，故引申为“可不予理会、微不足道”。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of negligible. All say the same thing in different settings: whatever is being discussed falls below a threshold that would require attention. The threshold may be an instrument, a budget, a risk decision, a statistical test, or a model's tolerance.
sensesIntro.cn: negligible 的八个义项在不同场景里说着同一件事：所讨论之物低于需要关注的门槛。门槛可以是仪器精度、预算、风险决定、统计检验，或模型的容差。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a scale with a sack of rice on one side and a single sesame seed on the other; the pointer barely moves.
core.cn: 核心意象：天平一边一袋米，另一边一粒芝麻，指针几乎不动。

chain: LATIN LEGERE TO PICK UP, CHOOSE
LATIN NEGLEGIBILIS THAT MAY BE DISREGARDED
ENGLISH NEGLIGIBLE TOO SMALL TO MATTER

branches.en: BELOW ATTENTION: too slight to act on, and a difference too small to argue about.
branches.cn: 低于注意力线：轻微到无须行动，差异小到不必争论。

branches.en: BELOW SCALE: a quantity under the instrument's threshold and a cost under the budget's notice.
branches.cn: 低于尺度：数量在仪器阈值之下，成本在预算注意之外。

branches.en: BELOW ACCEPTABLE HARM: a risk cheaper to accept than to guard against.
branches.cn: 低于可接受的伤害：接受风险比防范更划算。

branches.en: BELOW NOISE: an effect hidden in variation, whether in the lab or in a statistical test.
branches.cn: 低于噪声：作用藏在波动里，无论在实验室还是统计检验中。

branches.en: BELOW TOLERANCE: a term that can be deleted from a model without breaking it.
branches.cn: 低于容差：可以从模型中删去而不使它失效的项。

intro.en: Negligible is Latin neglegere plus -ible, 'able to be'. The family keeps the legere root in neglect, negligence, and negligent, where the idea is failing to pick something up.
intro.cn: negligible 是拉丁语 neglegere 加 -ible“可以被……”。词族在 neglect、negligence、negligent 中保留 legere 词根，核心意象是“没去捡起”。

latinIntro.en: The base is legere, to pick up, read, or choose, negated by nec-. Legere also gives collect, select, elect, and lecture through related prefixes.
latinIntro.cn: 词基是 legere“捡起、阅读、选择”，由 nec- 否定。legere 还通过其他前缀给出 collect、select、elect、lecture。

items.structure: Latin neglegere (not pick up) through French neglect
items.meaning: to fail to care for or attend to
items.example: They neglected the roof until it leaked.
items.exampleCN: 他们一直没管屋顶，直到它漏水。

items.meaning: failure to take proper care, especially as a legal fault
items.meaningCN: 疏忽；尤指法律上的过失
items.example: The court found negligence in the maintenance of the lift.
items.exampleCN: 法院认定电梯维护存在过失。

items.example: A negligent driver failed to check the mirror.
items.exampleCN: 一位疏忽的司机没有看后视镜。

items.example: The delay was negligible for most passengers.
items.exampleCN: 对大多数乘客而言，这点延误微不足道。

items.meaning: to a degree that can be ignored
items.example: The new route is negligibly longer than the old one.
items.exampleCN: 新路线只比旧路线长一点点。

items.example: The survey collects responses from every district.
items.exampleCN: 这项调查从每个区收集反馈。

items.meaning: to pick out from a group
items.example: The panel selects ten applicants for interview.
items.exampleCN: 评审小组选出十名申请人参加面试。

items.example: Only full members are eligible to vote.
items.exampleCN: 只有正式成员有资格投票。

items.example: The signature was barely legible.
items.exampleCN: 那个签名几乎看不清。

latinEntries.meaning: to pick up, gather, read, choose

definition_zh: 观察的；观测的；观察性的；依据观察的
definition_en: relating to or based on observation, especially in research that watches without intervening
core_image: 一间教室的后排，研究者坐在椅子上不发一言，只在表格里勾画孩子们每一次举手。
scene: 论文的方法部分写明，这项研究不设对照组，也不干预受试者的日常活动。 The study is observational: there is no control group and no interference.
sceneCN: 这里 observational 是“以观察为方法、不施加干预的”（第 2 个义项）；句意：这项研究属于观察性研究，没有对照组，也不施加干预。

pos.zh: 观察的；观测的；观察性的；依据观察的

derivatives.zh: 观察；观测；观察结果
观察；注意到；遵守
观察者；观察员

senses.title: Belonging to watching
senses.titleCN: 观察的：与“看”这一活动有关
senses.definition: relating to the act of watching something carefully
senses.definitionCN: 与仔细观看某物的行为有关
senses.example: The study's observational phase lasted six months before any interviews began.
senses.exampleCN: 这项研究的观察阶段持续了六个月，之后才开始访谈。
senses.why: The suffix marks a domain: whatever the activity of watching produces or requires can be called observational.
senses.whyCN: 这个后缀标出领域：凡由“看”这一活动产生或所需的东西，都可以叫 observational。

senses.title: Research that does not intervene
senses.titleCN: 观察性研究：只看，不动手
senses.definition: describing a study in which researchers watch and record without controlling the conditions
senses.definitionCN: 指研究者只观察记录、不控制条件的研究
senses.example: The observational study followed thousands of smokers without asking any of them to change.
senses.exampleCN: 这项观察性研究跟踪了数千名吸烟者，却没有要求任何人改变习惯。
senses.why: The word contrasts with experimental: nothing is assigned or manipulated, so the researchers accept whatever conditions already exist.
senses.whyCN: 这个词与“实验性研究”相对：不分配、不操纵，研究者接受业已存在的条件。

senses.title: Data taken from watching
senses.titleCN: 观测数据：仪器和眼睛记下来的
senses.definition: describing measurements or records obtained by watching rather than by experiment
senses.definitionCN: 指通过观察而非实验获得的测量值或记录
senses.example: Observational data from the buoys showed a slow rise in water temperature.
senses.exampleCN: 浮标传来的观测数据显示水温在缓慢上升。
senses.why: Data is observational when its source is the world as it is, not a world the researcher arranged.
senses.whyCN: 当数据来源是“本来的世界”而不是研究者安排的世界时，它就是观测数据。

senses.title: Astronomy by detection
senses.titleCN: 观测天文学：靠接收光来研究天体
senses.definition: describing astronomy that studies celestial objects through detected radiation rather than theory alone
senses.definitionCN: 指通过探测辐射而非仅凭理论研究天体的天文学分支
senses.example: Observational astronomy confirmed the prediction with a new image of the nebula.
senses.exampleCN: 观测天文学用一张新的星云图像证实了这一预测。
senses.why: Astronomers cannot run experiments on stars; observation replaces manipulation, so the branch is named for its only available method.
senses.whyCN: 天文学家无法对恒星做实验；观察取代了操纵，因此这一分支以它唯一可用的方法命名。

senses.title: Learning by watching others
senses.titleCN: 观察学习：看别人做，自己学会
senses.definition: describing the acquisition of behaviour by watching others perform it
senses.definitionCN: 指通过观看他人行为而习得行为的过程
senses.example: Observational learning explains how a child copies a gesture never directly taught.
senses.exampleCN: 观察学习解释了孩子如何学会一个从未被直接教过的手势。
senses.why: Here the watching is the teaching: no instruction is given, yet the model's behaviour passes to the observer.
senses.whyCN: 这里的“看”就是“教”：没有指令，示范者的行为却传给了观察者。

senses.title: Evidence from what is seen
senses.titleCN: 观察证据：眼睛能作证的部分
senses.definition: describing evidence that comes from direct or recorded watching
senses.definitionCN: 指来自直接或记录下来的观察的证据
senses.example: Observational evidence supported the theory long before a test could be designed.
senses.exampleCN: 在设计出检验之前很久，观察证据就已支持这一理论。
senses.why: Evidence is observational when it can be pointed at: the argument rests on what was seen, not on what was assumed.
senses.whyCN: 当证据可以被指认时，它就是观察证据：论证依靠看见的东西，而不是假定的东西。

senses.title: Error introduced by watching
senses.titleCN: 观测误差：看的人也会看错
senses.definition: describing error that arises from the limits of the observer or the instrument
senses.definitionCN: 指由观察者或仪器的局限造成的误差
senses.example: Observational error was reduced by averaging many readings.
senses.exampleCN: 通过平均多次读数，观测误差被降低了。
senses.why: Since observation is a human or instrumental act, it carries its own kind of error, distinct from the error of the thing observed.
senses.whyCN: 既然观察是人或仪器的行为，它就带有自身的误差，与被观察物本身的误差不同。

senses.title: A trained capacity
senses.titleCN: 观察能力：看得出别人看不出的
senses.definition: describing the skills or habits involved in noticing details accurately
senses.definitionCN: 指准确注意细节所需的技能或习惯
senses.example: Good observational skills let the nurse notice a change in breathing.
senses.exampleCN: 良好的观察能力让护士注意到呼吸的变化。
senses.why: Practice turns watching into a competence: the trained observer sees distinctions that an untrained eye smooths over.
senses.whyCN: 练习把“看”变成一种能力：受过训练的眼睛能看出未经训练的眼睛会抹平的差别。

intro.en: Observational is observation plus -al. Behind observation is Latin observare, ob- 'over' plus servare 'to keep or guard'.
intro.cn: observational 是 observation 加 -al。observation 背后是拉丁语 observare：ob-“在上”加 servare“守护、保持”。

items.en: Servare meant to keep or guard. Watching and keeping were one act: one keeps what one watches over.
items.cn: servare 意为保持、守护。看与守曾是一个动作：人守着自己所看护的东西。

items.en: With ob-, the verb meant to watch over, to heed, and to comply with a rule or sign.
items.cn: 加上 ob- 后，动词意为看护、留意，并遵从规则或征兆。

items.en: The noun named the act of watching and the remark produced by it. Medieval science leaned on this noun for recorded attention.
items.cn: 该名词指看护行为及其产生的评论。中世纪科学倚重这个名词来表示有记录的注意。

items.en: English observation arrived through French in the 14th century and became a key term in navigation, medicine, and natural philosophy.
items.cn: 英语 observation 于 14 世纪经法语进入，成为航海、医学与自然哲学的关键术语。

items.en: The suffix -al turns the noun into an adjective meaning 'of or relating to'. Observational therefore means 'of observation'.
items.cn: 后缀 -al 把名词变成意为“与……有关的”形容词。因此 observational 就是“与观察有关的”。

items.en: In the 20th century, epidemiology and psychology standardised observational study and observational learning as named methods.
items.cn: 20 世纪，流行病学与心理学把 observational study 与 observational learning 固定为有名称的方法。

note.en: The first group is the observation family; the second compares research and evidence labels that differ in how much the researcher intervenes.
note.cn: 第一组是 observation 词族；第二组比较几个研究方法与证据标签，区别在于研究者干预的程度。

entries.definition: the act, result, or remark of watching. It is the noun that observational modifies.
entries.definitionCN: 观察的行为、结果或评论；是 observational 所修饰的名词。

entries.definition: able to be seen or noticed. It describes a quality of the object, not a method.
entries.definitionCN: 可被看见或注意到的；描述对象的性质，而非方法。

entries.definition: quick to notice things. It describes a person's habit.
entries.definitionCN: 善于察觉的；描述人的习性。

entries.definition: based on controlled tests in which conditions are changed. It is the direct opposite of observational.
entries.definitionCN: 基于改变条件的受控试验；与 observational 直接相对。

entries.definition: based on experience or data rather than theory. It can cover both observation and experiment.
entries.definitionCN: 依据经验或数据而非理论；可同时涵盖观察与实验。

entries.definition: describing a study that measures whether two variables move together, without changing either.
entries.definitionCN: 指测量两个变量是否同向变化、而不改变任一变量的研究。

entries.definition: based on isolated stories rather than systematic watching. It is the weakest cousin of observational.
entries.definitionCN: 基于零散个例而非系统观察；是 observational 最弱的表亲。

normalIntro.en: Real parts only: observation plus -al. No new root enters; the adjective simply means 'of observation'.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实成分：observation 加 -al。没有新词根进入；这个形容词只表示“属于观察的”。

normal.en: Observation + al: anything that belongs to watching is observational.
normal.cn: observation 加 al：凡属于“看”的东西都是 observational。

normal.en: An observational study sits at the back of the room and takes notes.
normal.cn: 观察性研究坐在教室后排做笔记。

normal.en: Experimental changes the room; observational records the room as it is.
normal.cn: 实验研究改变房间；观察研究记录房间本来的样子。

normal.en: Observational astronomy cannot touch a star, so it watches light instead.
normal.cn: 观测天文学碰不到恒星，于是改为看光。

normal.en: Observational error belongs to the watcher; the object may be perfectly steady.
normal.cn: 观测误差属于看的人；被看的东西可能完全稳定。

abstract.en: Observation without intervention is an ideal that no observer fully reaches; presence itself is a kind of touch.
abstract.cn: 不干预的观察是一种理想，没有观察者能完全达到；在场本身就是一种触碰。

abstract.en: An observational study can show that things travel together, never that one pushed the other.
abstract.cn: 观察性研究能显示事物同行，却不能显示是谁推了谁。

abstract.en: The adjective hides the instrument: 'observational' sounds neutral, yet every observation has a device behind it.
abstract.cn: 这个形容词把仪器藏了起来：observational 听起来中立，可每次观察背后都有一台装置。

examples.en: The observational study could not rule out that healthier people simply walked more.
examples.cn: 这项观察性研究无法排除“本来就更健康的人走得更多”这一可能。

examples.en: Observational astronomy relies on telescopes that record light far beyond the visible range.
examples.cn: 观测天文学依靠能记录可见范围之外光线的望远镜。

examples.en: Young animals acquire many skills through observational learning rather than direct practice.
examples.cn: 幼年动物通过观察学习而非直接练习获得许多技能。

dict_mnemonic.text: observation（观察）+ al（的）——凡跟“观察”有关的，就是观察性的。

root: 由 observation（观察，源自拉丁语 observare“看护、留意”）加形容词后缀 -al 构成，意为“与观察有关的”；在研究方法中指不施加干预、仅作记录的一类研究。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of observational, all variations on one adjective. It can name the activity of watching, a method that avoids interference, the data such a method yields, the error it introduces, or the skill it requires.
sensesIntro.cn: observational 的八个义项都是同一个形容词的变化。它可以指观看活动、避免干预的方法、该方法产生的数据、它带来的误差，或它所需的技能。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a researcher seated at the back of a classroom, silent, ticking each hand raised.
core.cn: 核心意象：研究者坐在教室后排，一言不发，每次有人举手就打一个勾。

branches.en: THE ACT AND THE SKILL: watching as an activity, and watching as a trained competence.
branches.cn: 行为与能力：作为活动的观看，以及作为训练有素的本领。

branches.en: METHOD AND DATA: a study without intervention, and the records it produces.
branches.cn: 方法与数据：不干预的研究，以及它产生的记录。

branches.en: ASTRONOMY'S ONLY METHOD: watching light because stars cannot be handled.
branches.cn: 天文学唯一的方法：恒星无法摆弄，只能看光。

branches.en: LEARNING BY IMITATION: behaviour passed on through watching a model.
branches.cn: 通过模仿学习：行为通过观看示范者而传递。

branches.en: EVIDENCE AND ITS COST: what the eye can support, and the error the eye adds.
branches.cn: 证据与代价：眼睛能支持的内容，以及眼睛附加的误差。

intro.en: Observational is observation plus -al. The family keeps -ation for the act, -er for the person, -ance for compliance, and -atory for the place.
intro.cn: observational 是 observation 加 -al。词族保留 -ation 表示行为，-er 表示人，-ance 表示遵从，-atory 表示场所。

latinIntro.en: The base is servare, to keep, with ob- adding attention. The same Latin verb yields preserve, reserve, conserve, and servant.
latinIntro.cn: 词基是 servare“保持”，ob- 增加“注意”的方向。同一拉丁动词给出 preserve、reserve、conserve、servant。

items.meaning: to watch, notice, or keep a rule
items.example: The team observed the site for three seasons.
items.exampleCN: 团队对该地点观察了三个季节。

items.meaning: the act or result of watching
items.example: The observation was repeated by a second team.
items.exampleCN: 这一观察由第二个团队重复了一次。

items.meaning: relating to watching as a method
items.meaningCN: 与作为方法的观察有关
items.example: The paper is observational rather than experimental.
items.exampleCN: 这篇论文属于观察性而非实验性研究。

items.example: The two sites are observationally similar but geologically distinct.

senses.title: The world-encircling body of salt water
senses.titleCN: 覆盖地球大部分表面的连片咸水
senses.definition: the great body of salt water that surrounds the continents and covers most of the planet
senses.definitionCN: 环绕各大陆、覆盖地球大部分表面的巨大咸水体
senses.example: A single ocean can hold more water than all the land it surrounds.
senses.exampleCN: 一个海洋能容纳的水量超过它周围全部陆地。
senses.why: Greek Okeanos named the stream believed to run all the way around the world, so the word began as one continuous encircling water, not as a list of separate seas.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 Okeanos 原本指绕世界一周的大河，所以这个词从诞生起就是「一圈连着的咸水」，而非若干彼此分开的海。

senses.title: One of the named divisions
senses.titleCN: 五大洋中一个有名字的洋
senses.definition: one of the five large divisions of this water, such as the Pacific, Atlantic or Indian ocean
senses.definitionCN: 这片水域被划分出的五大洋之一，如太平洋、大西洋或印度洋
senses.example: The Atlantic ocean narrows toward its northern end.
senses.exampleCN: 大西洋在它的北端变窄。
senses.why: once geographers divided the single world water into named basins, the same word served both the whole and each part, and context decides which is meant.
senses.whyCN: 地理学家把这一整片世界水域划分成有名字的海盆之后，同一个词既指整体也指其中一部分，靠上下文决定所指。

senses.title: The water as opposed to the land
senses.definition: the open salt water thought of as a place distinct from land, especially in travel and trade
senses.definitionCN: 与陆地相对的开阔咸水，尤用于航行与贸易语境
senses.example: They spent three weeks on the ocean before sighting land.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在海上待了三个星期才看见陆地。
senses.why: a voyage needs two settings, land and water; the word supplies the second one, so 'on the ocean' simply means out on the salt water.
senses.whyCN: 一次远航需要两个场景：陆地与水面；这个词提供后者，因此「在海洋上」就是身处开阔咸水之中。

senses.title: A very large amount
senses.definition: an immense quantity of something, especially something abstract such as words or work
senses.definitionCN: 某事物数量极大，尤指话语、工作等抽象事物
senses.example: An ocean of paperwork awaited the new clerk.
senses.exampleCN: 海量的文书工作等着这位新职员。
senses.why: the figurative step is simple: the largest thing most speakers know becomes the measure of anything too big to count, so an ocean of forms is just too many forms.
senses.whyCN: 比喻的跳跃很简单：把说话人知道的最大之物拿来度量多到数不清的东西，因此「一整个海洋的表格」就是表格多到数不清。

senses.title: A boundless expanse
senses.definition: a vast unbroken stretch of something that seems to have no edge, such as sand or grass
senses.definitionCN: 沙、草等铺展到看不见边界的广阔一片
senses.example: An ocean of sand stretched from the road to the horizon.
senses.exampleCN: 一片沙海从路边一直铺到地平线。
senses.why: the eye reads any surface without a visible edge the way it reads water, so desert and prairie borrow the word for the same feeling of no boundary.
senses.whyCN: 人眼看到没有可见边界的表面时，读法与看水面一样，因此沙漠与草原借这个词表达同样的「无边」之感。

senses.title: A depth of feeling
senses.definition: an overwhelming quantity of a feeling that seems to swallow a person up
senses.definitionCN: 铺天盖地、仿佛把人吞没的情感
senses.example: She sank into an ocean of grief after the funeral.
senses.exampleCN: 葬礼之后，她沉入一片悲痛的汪洋。
senses.why: deep water is the standing image for what cannot be crossed or controlled, so grief and doubt are described as oceans, with the person inside them rather than beside them.
senses.whyCN: 深水一直是无从跨越、无法掌控的意象，因此悲伤与疑虑被说成海洋，而人是在其中，不在其旁。

senses.title: The ocean as a climate system
senses.definition: the salt water regarded as a system that stores heat, moves currents and regulates the atmosphere
senses.definitionCN: 把咸水视为储存热量、驱动洋流并调节大气的一个系统
senses.example: The ocean absorbs much of the heat trapped by greenhouse gases.
senses.exampleCN: 海洋吸收了温室气体截留的大部分热量。
senses.why: twentieth-century earth science turned the place into a mechanism: the same water that sails are built for is now studied as a store and pump of heat.
senses.whyCN: 20 世纪的地球科学把这个地点变成了机制：原本造船航行的同一片水，如今被当作热量的储库与泵来研究。

senses.title: The high seas in law
senses.definition: open water beyond any state's coastal jurisdiction, belonging to no single country
senses.definitionCN: 超出任何国家沿海管辖范围、不属任何一国所有的开阔水域
senses.example: Beyond the twelve-mile limit lies the open ocean.
senses.exampleCN: 越过十二海里界限，就是开阔的公海。
senses.why: maritime law needed a term for water that no flag claims; the everyday word for the great water took that legal slot without changing shape.
senses.whyCN: 海商法需要一个词指没有任何国旗主张的水域，于是日常指大水的词原样填进了这个法律位置。

senses.title: Ocean as a shipping modifier
senses.definition: used before another noun to mean carried by, used on, or belonging to the open sea
senses.definitionCN: 置于名词前，表示由远洋承运、用于远洋或属于远洋的
senses.example: Ocean freight moves most goods between continents.
senses.exampleCN: 远洋货运承担了洲际间的大部分货物。
senses.why: when a noun is placed before another noun it stops naming a place and starts naming a route or a class, which is how ocean becomes the label on a shipping container.
senses.whyCN: 名词放到另一个名词前时，它不再指地点，而开始指一条路线或一个类别，海洋就是这样变成了集装箱上的运输标签。

intro.en: Ocean reaches English through Latin and Old French from Greek Okeanos, the name of the stream that was thought to run around the whole inhabited world. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: ocean 经拉丁语与古法语进入英语，源头是希腊语 Okeanos——古人想象中环绕整个已知世界的大河之名。年代均为约数。

items.en: Okeanos in Homer is the river that encircles the disc of the world and is never crossed; it is a proper name first, a common noun for the outer water later.
items.cn: 荷马笔下的 Okeanos 是环绕世界圆盘、无人能越的大河；它先是专名，后来才成为指外围水域的普通名词。

items.en: Later Greek writers, above all Herodotus, used okeanos for the open water outside the Mediterranean, and the word began to mean the sea itself rather than a river.
items.cn: 后来的希腊作者，尤其是希罗多德，用 okeanos 指地中海之外的开阔水域，这个词开始表示海本身而非一条河。

items.en: Latin took Oceanus as both a name and a common noun for the great sea; the adjective oceanicus 'of the ocean' follows the same stem.
items.cn: 拉丁语把 Oceanus 同时用作专名与指大海洋的普通名词；形容词 oceanicus「海洋的」沿用同一词干。

items.en: Old French occean passed the word to Middle English around the fourteenth century, where it first named the outer sea and only later any large body of salt water.
items.cn: 古法语 occean 在 14 世纪前后把这个词传给中古英语，最初指外围的大海，后来才泛指任何巨大咸水体。

items.en: From the age of exploration the single world water was mapped as named oceans, and the older 'stream around the world' image survives only in poetry and etymology.
items.cn: 从大航海时代起，这一整片世界水域被绘制成有名字的几个大洋，古老「绕世大河」的意象只留在诗歌与词源说明里。

items.en: Source uncertain (root origin, not first date): the deeper origin of Greek Okeanos is disputed, with some scholars treating it as a pre-Greek loan; any reconstructed Indo-European form for it is a hypothesis, not an established derivation.
items.cn: 来源不确定（指词根来源，不是首见年代）：希腊语 Okeanos 的更早来源有争议，有学者视之为前希腊语借词；为它构拟的任何印欧语形式都只是假说，不是已证实的派生。

note.en: Group one holds words that look like ocean or are built on the same stem; group two holds words for water that differ in size or register.
note.cn: 第一组是与 ocean 形近或同出同一词干的词；第二组是都指水域、但规模或语体不同的词。

entries.definition: the collective name for the Pacific islands and Australia; it adds -ia to the Oceanus stem, so it names a region, not a body of water.
entries.definitionCN: 太平洋岛屿与澳大利亚的合称；在 Oceanus 词干上加 -ia，指一个区域，而不是一片水域。

entries.definition: ocean plus -ic: relating to the ocean, or simply very large and open, as in oceanic distances.
entries.definitionCN: ocean 加 -ic：与海洋有关的，或形容极其辽阔开阔的，如「远洋般的距离」。

entries.definition: ocean plus -graphy 'writing, describing': the scientific study of the sea, not the sea itself.
entries.definitionCN: ocean 加 -graphy「书写、描述」：对海洋的科学研究，而不是海洋本身。

entries.definition: ocean plus front: land that faces the sea, so the compound names property rather than water.
entries.definitionCN: ocean 加 front：面朝大海的陆地，因此这个复合词指地产，而非水域。

entries.definition: a body of salt water smaller than an ocean and often partly enclosed by land; the everyday word for the water you can see from a shore.
entries.definitionCN: 比大洋小、常被陆地部分围住的咸水体；指岸边看得见的那片水的日常用词。

entries.definition: a plural used for a particular stretch of water, as in territorial waters; it is neutral in size and common in law and news.
entries.definitionCN: 复数形式，指某一片特定水域，如领海；不限定规模，常见于法律与新闻。

entries.definition: an old poetic word for the open sea, as in the Spanish Main; it survives mostly in verse and historical writing.
entries.definitionCN: 指开阔大海的古雅诗歌用词，如「西班牙海」；如今多存于诗歌与历史写作。

entries.definition: the deep is a literary name for the sea that stresses its depth rather than its width; it fits images of sinking and hiding.
entries.definitionCN: the deep 是海洋的文学称呼，强调深度而非广度；适合「沉没、隐藏」一类意象。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Greek Okeanos was the river around the world, so the word began as one continuous ring of water.
normal.cn: 希腊语 Okeanos 是绕世界的大河，因此这个词最初就是一圈连着的水。

normal.en: The family runs ocean, oceanic, oceanography, oceanographer, oceanarium, oceanfront.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 ocean、oceanic、oceanography、oceanographer、oceanarium、oceanfront。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the physical sense: ocean floor, ocean basin, deep ocean, open ocean.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出物理义：海底、海盆、深海、开阔洋面。

normal.en: Geography names five: the Pacific, Atlantic, Indian, Southern and Arctic oceans.
normal.cn: 地理学列出五个：太平洋、大西洋、印度洋、南大洋与北冰洋。

normal.en: The idiom an ocean of means a huge amount, as in an ocean of paperwork.
normal.cn: 短语 an ocean of 表示极多，如海量文书。

abstract.en: Picture a drop of water that cannot find a shore to belong to.
abstract.cn: 想象一滴水找不到可以归属的岸。

abstract.en: Picture a map where the blue is not a colour but a distance you cannot cross.
abstract.cn: 想象一张地图，上面的蓝色不是颜色，而是一段跨不过去的距离。

abstract.en: Picture a voice heard across water, arriving in layers like waves.
abstract.cn: 想象隔着水传来的人声，一层一层像浪一样抵达。

examples.en: The ocean covers about seventy percent of the earth's surface.
examples.cn: 海洋覆盖了地球表面约七成。

examples.en: Scientists track how the ocean moves heat from the tropics poleward.
examples.cn: 科学家追踪海洋如何把热量从热带向极地输送。

examples.en: From the cliff we watched an ocean of cloud roll inland.
examples.cn: 从崖上望去，我们看着一片云海向内陆翻滚。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「哦，深海」——看到望不到边的水，先「哦」一声，再想到深海大洋 → 海洋、大量

root: 希腊 Okeanos「环绕世界的大河」（专名转普通名词）→ 拉丁 Oceanus → 古法语 occean → 英语 ocean；Okeanos 的更早来源有争议，或为前希腊语借词，构拟的印欧形式均属假说。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses radiate from one picture: a ring of salt water around the land, then the named parts, the water seen from a ship, the same boundlessness borrowed for quantity and feeling, and finally the water studied as a machine and claimed in law.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项从同一个画面辐射出去：环绕陆地的咸水圈，然后是其中命名分区、船上所见的水面，同一份「无边」被借去指数量与情感，最后是当作机器研究的海洋与法律主张的海域。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one continuous ring of salt water holding the land inside it, too wide to see across.
core.cn: 核心意象：一整圈连着的咸水把陆地围在里面，宽到看不见对岸。

branches.en: THE PHYSICAL BODY: the same water is first a place on the map and later a heat store studied by climate science.
branches.cn: 物理水体：同一片水先是地图上的一个地点，后来成为气候科学研究的储热系统。

branches.en: DIVIDED AND CLAIMED: geography cuts the whole into named oceans, and law marks where national claims stop.
branches.cn: 被划分与被主张：地理学把整体切成有名字的洋，法律标出国家主张止于何处。

branches.en: SEEN FROM A SHIP: from deck the water is a setting for travel, and as a modifier it labels the freight that crosses it.
branches.cn: 从船上看见：在甲板上水是旅行的场景，作定语时则标注穿越它的货运。

branches.en: BORROWED SCALE: the widest thing a speaker knows measures paperwork, sand and grass.
branches.cn: 借来的尺度：说话人知道的最宽之物，被用来度量文书、沙与草。

branches.en: INWARD WATER: grief and doubt become oceans because the person is inside them, not beside them.
branches.cn: 向内的水：悲伤与疑虑变成海洋，因为人是在其中，而不是在其旁。

intro.en: Ocean is a borrowed proper name that became a common noun; its family is built with Greek and Latin suffixes added to the same stem.
intro.cn: ocean 是一个转为普通名词的外来专名；它的词族都是在同一词干上加希腊语与拉丁语后缀构成的。

latinIntro.en: Latin Oceanus keeps both the name and the common noun, and oceanicus supplies the adjective pattern behind oceanic.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 Oceanus 同时保留专名与普通名词用法，oceanicus 则提供了 oceanic 背后的形容词构词模式。

items.meaning: the island region of the Pacific

definition_zh: 理论的；理论上的；假设的；以理论推理为依据的
definition_en: based on general principles and reasoning rather than on practice, observation or direct experiment
core_image: 黑板上推演到一半的公式，与现实车间里尚未造出的机器隔着一段距离
scene: 理论组把公式钉满白板，实验组在旁摇头。 Theoretical physics often runs decades ahead of experiment.
sceneCN: 这里 theoretical 指「理论的」（第 1 个义项：依据原理与推理、而非实践与实验）；句意：理论物理学往往比实验领先数十年。图中可辨识物件：写满推演的黑板、尚未装配的仪器草图。

pos.zh: 理论的；理论上的；假设的（与 practical、experimental、applied 相对）

derivatives.zh: 理论；学说；原理
理论家；理论工作者
理论上；按理说
理论的（多见于 theoretic framework 等学术搭配）

senses.title: Based on Theory
senses.titleCN: 理论的：依据原理而非实践
senses.definition: based on ideas and general principles rather than on practice or experiment
senses.definitionCN: 依据观念与一般原理，而非实践或实验的
senses.example: Theoretical physics often runs decades ahead of experiment.
senses.exampleCN: 理论物理学往往比实验领先数十年。
senses.why: Greek theoria named looking and contemplating. The adjective marks knowledge reached by reasoning about principles, not by handling the thing itself.
senses.whyCN: 希腊 theoria 指观看与沉思。这个形容词标出的是通过对原理的推理而获得的知识，而不是亲手处理事物得来的知识。

senses.title: Hypothetical
senses.titleCN: 假设的：只为推理而设想
senses.definition: imagined or supposed for the purpose of reasoning, not actual
senses.definitionCN: 为推理而设想或假定，并非实际存在
senses.example: Let us take a theoretical case in which nobody pays tax.
senses.exampleCN: 让我们设想一个没人缴税的理论情形。
senses.why: A case built to test an argument is not observed anywhere. It exists only inside the reasoning, so the adjective shifts from 'about theory' to 'merely supposed'.
senses.whyCN: 为检验论证而构造的情形并不在任何地方被观察到，它只存在于推理之中；于是这个形容词从「关于理论的」滑向「仅仅假设的」。

senses.title: Predicted but Unseen
senses.titleCN: 理论预言的：尚未观测到
senses.definition: predicted by theory but not yet observed
senses.definitionCN: 由理论预言、但尚未被观测到的
senses.example: The theoretical particle would leave only a tiny trace in the detector.
senses.exampleCN: 这种理论粒子只会在探测器中留下极微小的痕迹。
senses.why: Theory can name something before any instrument sees it. The adjective marks that priority of reasoning over observation, which is common in particle physics.
senses.whyCN: 理论可以在任何仪器看见某物之前先给它命名；这个形容词标出的正是推理先于观测，这在粒子物理中很常见。

senses.title: Of the Theory Branch
senses.titleCN: 理论分支的：学科的理论侧
senses.definition: belonging to the branch of a subject that studies principles rather than applications
senses.definitionCN: 属于研究原理而非应用的那个学科分支
senses.example: She holds a chair in theoretical computer science.
senses.exampleCN: 她担任理论计算机科学方向的教授。
senses.why: Disciplines split into theory and application. The adjective labels the theory side, where the aim is to prove what is possible, not to ship a product.
senses.whyCN: 学科会分成理论与应用两侧；这个形容词标出理论一侧，其目标是证明什么在原理上可行，而不是交付产品。

senses.title: Idealized Model
senses.titleCN: 理想化模型的：删去复杂细节
senses.definition: belonging to an idealized model that leaves out complicating details
senses.definitionCN: 属于省略了复杂细节的理想化模型
senses.example: The theoretical model assumes a perfectly smooth sphere.
senses.exampleCN: 这个理论模型假定球体完全光滑。
senses.why: A model is made by leaving things out. The word marks that the object is a construction, so its predictions hold only as far as the omissions are harmless.
senses.whyCN: 模型是靠删减造出来的；这个词标出该对象是一种构造物，因此其预测只在删减无碍的范围内成立。

senses.title: Possible in Principle
senses.titleCN: 原则上可能的：逻辑容许
senses.definition: possible according to reasoning, whether or not it can be done in practice
senses.definitionCN: 按推理是可能的，不论实践中能否做到
senses.example: A theoretical solution exists, but nobody can build it yet.
senses.exampleCN: 理论上存在解法，但暂时没人能把它造出来。
senses.why: If the reasoning permits something, it is theoretically possible. The barrier lies in materials or cost, not in logic, which is why the two words 'theoretical' and 'practical' so often face each other.
senses.whyCN: 如果推理容许某件事，它就是理论上可能的；障碍在材料或成本，而不在逻辑，所以 theoretical 与 practical 常常成对出现。

senses.title: Abstract, Not Applied
senses.titleCN: 抽象的：带不务实的意味
senses.definition: concerned with abstract reasoning, often with a hint of impracticality
senses.definitionCN: 关心抽象推理，常暗示不切实际
senses.example: His answer was theoretical and ignored the cost of the plan.
senses.exampleCN: 他的回答是理论性的，忽略了该计划的成本。
senses.why: When reasoning ignores real conditions, the same word turns mildly critical: correct in the abstract and useless in this room. The tone comes from context, not from the root.
senses.whyCN: 当推理无视现实条件，同一个词就带上轻微批评：抽象上正确，在这间屋子里却没用。这一语气来自语境，而非词根。

senses.title: Consistent within a Theory
senses.titleCN: 理论体系内的：内部自洽
senses.definition: consistent with the definitions and assumptions of a given theory
senses.definitionCN: 与某一理论的定义和假定保持一致
senses.example: The objection is theoretical: the two claims cannot both hold.
senses.exampleCN: 这一反对是理论层面的：两项主张不能同时成立。
senses.why: Inside a theory, statements must fit its own rules. A theoretical objection attacks that fit rather than the data, so it can be settled by argument alone.
senses.whyCN: 在一个理论内部，陈述必须符合它自己的规则；理论性反对攻击的正是这种吻合，而不是数据，因此仅凭论证就能解决。

intro.en: Theoretical descends from Greek theōria 'a looking, contemplation', through Latin theoreticus. The Greek noun is usually traced to theoros 'spectator', but the details of the earliest formation are debated.
intro.cn: theoretical 经拉丁 theoreticus 上溯希腊 theōria「观看、沉思」。这个希腊名词通常追溯到 theoros「观看者」，但最早构词细节仍有争议。

items.en: The noun thea is generally taken to mean 'a view, a sight', and horan means 'to see'. Together they are thought to give theoros, 'one who looks on', especially a spectator at a festival or an envoy consulting an oracle.
items.cn: 名词 thea 一般认为是「景象、观看」，horan 意为「看见」；两者合成 theoros，即「观看的人」，尤指节庆上的观众或去求神谕的使者。此说一般认为是，细节并不完全确定。

items.en: From theoros came the noun theōria, 'the act of looking on, contemplation, a spectacle'. Philosophy borrowed it for the mind's disinterested viewing of truth, away from action.
items.cn: 由 theoros 产生名词 theōria，意为「观看的行为、沉思、景象」。哲学借它指心灵不带功利地观看真理，与行动保持距离。

items.en: Latin took the adjective theorēticus from Greek theoretikos, 'of contemplation'. The Latin form kept the philosophical sense of knowledge pursued for understanding rather than for use.
items.cn: 拉丁语从希腊 theoretikos 借入形容词 theorēticus，意为「沉思的」。拉丁形式保留了哲学含义：为理解而非为实用而追求的知识。

items.en: English theoretical appears in the seventeenth century beside the older theoretic. The -al form became the everyday adjective, while theoretic survived mainly in fixed academic phrases. The first citation is uncertain.
items.cn: 英语 theoretical 于十七世纪出现，与更早的 theoretic 并存。-al 形式成为日常形容词，theoretic 主要残留在固定的学术搭配中。确切首见书证不确定。

items.en: The modern contrast between theoretical and practical is older than English: Greek already opposed theōria to praxis. The pair therefore marks a division of labour, not a judgement that one side is useless.
items.cn: 现代 theoretical 与 practical 的对立比英语更古老：希腊语已用 theōria 对 praxis。因此这一对词标出的是分工，而不是判定某一侧无用。

note.en: The first group traces one Greek family whose members are easily confused. The second holds near-synonyms that sit at different distances from reality.
note.cn: 第一组梳理同一个希腊词族中容易混淆的成员；第二组是距现实远近不同的近义词。

entries.definition: A body of principles that explains a field. It is the thing a theoretical argument is built inside, not the adjective describing the argument.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，指解释某一领域的一套原理；理论论证是在它内部进行的，而它不是描述论证的形容词。

entries.definition: A person who builds or studies theory. It names the human agent, so it never replaces theoretical before a noun.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，指建构或研究理论的人；它命名的是人，因此不能替代名词前的 theoretical。

entries.definition: An older adjective of the same meaning, now mostly confined to phrases such as theoretic framework. It is not a different concept.
entries.definitionCN: 同义的较旧形容词形式，如今多限于 theoretic framework 一类搭配；它并非另一个概念。

entries.definition: Imagined as a premise. It stresses that the case is not real, while theoretical may still describe a well-founded body of reasoning.
entries.definitionCN: 作为前提被设想出来的；强调情形不真实，而 theoretical 仍可指有根据的推理体系。

entries.definition: Concerning concepts or mental categories. It says the work happens with ideas, not that it is unproven.
entries.definitionCN: 关于概念或心智范畴的；它说的是工作以观念为材料，并不表示未经证实。

entries.definition: General and detached from concrete cases. It can be neutral or critical, but it does not imply a formal theory.
entries.definitionCN: 一般性的、脱离具体个案的；可中性也可带批评，但不暗示存在形式化的理论。

entries.definition: Based on conjecture with little evidence. It is more negative than theoretical, which can be rigorous.
entries.definitionCN: 基于猜测而证据不足的；比 theoretical 更负面，因为 theoretical 可以是严谨的。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: theoria 'a looking' + -al: knowledge from viewing principles with the mind.
normal.cn: theoria「观看」+ -al：用心灵观看原理而得到的知识。

normal.en: The family runs theory, theorist, theorize, theoretic, theoretical, theorem.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 theory、theorist、theorize、theoretic、theoretical、theorem。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the use: theoretical framework, theoretical physics, theoretical model, theoretical possibility.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出用法：理论框架、理论物理学、理论模型、理论上的可能性。

normal.en: The opposite pair is theoretical and practical, or theoretical and experimental.
normal.cn: 对立搭配是 theoretical 与 practical，或 theoretical 与 experimental。

normal.en: theorem is a proved statement; theory is the whole system that contains it.
normal.cn: theorem 是被证明的命题；theory 是包含它的整个体系。

abstract.en: Picture a map drawn years before anyone walks the ground it describes.
abstract.cn: 想象一张地图，在任何人走过它所描述的地面之前许多年就已画好。

abstract.en: Picture a model ship in a bottle: exact in shape, unable to carry a single passenger.
abstract.cn: 想象瓶中船：形状精确，却载不了一位乘客。

abstract.en: Picture two people arguing about whether a door can open, without ever trying the handle.
abstract.cn: 想象两个人争论一扇门能不能开，却从不去拧门把手。

examples.en: The paper offers a theoretical explanation, but no experiment has tested it.
examples.cn: 这篇论文给出了一种理论解释，但尚无实验检验它。

examples.en: In theoretical terms the plan is sound; in practice it needs money nobody has.
examples.cn: 从理论上说这个计划是成立的；实践中它需要没人拿得出的资金。

examples.en: Students often find theoretical courses dry until they meet a real problem.
examples.cn: 学生常觉得理论课程枯燥，直到遇上一个真实问题。

dict_mnemonic.text: theory（理论）+ etical（形容词词尾）→ 属于理论的 → theoretical 理论的

root: 希腊 thea「景象」+ horan「看见」→ theoros「观看者」→ theōria「观看、沉思」→ 拉丁 theoreticus → 英语 theoretical。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses begin with reasoning rather than practice and fan out: a hypothetical case, an unobserved prediction, a branch of a discipline, an idealized model, a logical possibility, an abstract answer and an internal objection.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从「以推理而非实践为本」出发向外展开：假设情形、尚未观测的预言、学科分支、理想化模型、逻辑上的可能、抽象的回答与体系内部的反对。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a formula worked out on a board, separated from the machine it describes.
core.cn: 核心意象：黑板上推演出的公式，与它所描述的机器之间隔着距离。

branches.en: REASONING APART FROM PRACTICE: knowledge from principles, which can look either rigorous or useless depending on the room.
branches.cn: 与实践分离的推理：来自原理的知识，视场合可显得严谨，也可显得无用。

branches.en: THE SUPPOSED AND THE POSSIBLE: a case invented for argument and a solution the reasoning permits.
branches.cn: 假设与可能：为论证而虚构的情形，以及推理所容许的解法。

branches.en: THE UNSEEN: theory may name a particle before any detector records it.
branches.cn: 未见之物：理论可在任何探测器记录之前先为粒子命名。

branches.en: THE BRANCH: a discipline divides into a theory side and an application side.
branches.cn: 分支：一个学科分为理论侧与应用侧。

branches.en: CONSTRUCTION AND CONSISTENCY: a model built by omission must also stay coherent with its own assumptions.
branches.cn: 构造与自洽：靠省略建成的模型，还必须在自身假定内保持一致。

intro.en: Theoretical is a Greek noun of viewing turned into a Latin adjective and then an English one: root words for sight, a noun ending, and an adjective ending -al.
intro.cn: theoretical 是希腊语中表示「观看」的名词，先转为拉丁形容词，再进入英语：表示视觉的词根、名词词尾，以及形容词词尾 -al。

latinIntro.en: Greek theōria produced Latin theoreticus and English theory, theoretical, theorist, theorize and theorem. The same sight-root appears in theater, a place for viewing, though that word reached English by a different route.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊 theōria 产生拉丁 theoreticus，以及英语 theory、theoretical、theorist、theorize、theorem。同一个「观看」词根也出现在 theater（观看的场所）中，但那个词走的是另一条路径。

items.example: The theoretical part of the course comes first.
items.exampleCN: 课程的理论部分排在前面。

items.meaning: an organized body of explanatory principles
items.meaningCN: 有组织的解释性原理体系
items.example: The theory predicts a slow rise in sea level.
items.exampleCN: 该理论预测海平面会缓慢上升。

items.meaning: one who builds or studies theory
items.example: The theorist never visited the site she wrote about.
items.exampleCN: 这位理论家从未到过她所写的那处遗址。

items.meaning: to form or reason with theories
items.example: They theorized about the cause for years.
items.exampleCN: 他们多年来就成因进行理论推测。

items.meaningCN: theory 的较旧形容词形式
items.example: Theoretic work preceded any measurement.
items.exampleCN: 理论研究先于任何测量。

items.structure: theōrēma (a thing viewed, a proposition) + English form
items.example: The theorem holds for every triangle.
items.exampleCN: 该定理对一切三角形都成立。

items.meaning: of the stage; exaggerated as if acted
items.meaningCN: 戏剧的；如表演般夸张的
items.example: His grief was real but theatrical.
items.exampleCN: 他的悲伤是真的，却很戏剧化。

items.example: Theoretically, the bridge can hold twice that load.
items.exampleCN: 理论上，这座桥能承受两倍的荷载。

latinEntries.structure: theōria, -ae (f., first declension, Greek loan in Latin)

latinEntries.meaning: a spectacle; a proposition to be proved
latinEntries.meaningCN: 所见之物；待证明的命题

definition_zh: 恶化；变坏；退化；变质；衰减
definition_en: to become progressively worse in quality, condition or state
core_image: 一面旧墙的抹灰从角上起皮，裂缝一天比一天宽，落下的粉末堆在墙脚
scene: 这栋楼长期没人维护，墙面起皮，管道也开始漏。 Without maintenance the building will deteriorate within a few years.
sceneCN: 这里指建筑物状况逐渐变坏（第 3 个义项：环境或设施条件退化）；句意为若不维护，这栋楼几年内就会衰败。图中可辨识物件：起皮的墙面、裂缝、墙脚的粉末。

pos.zh: 恶化；变坏；退化；变质

derivatives.zh: 由该动词加表示动作结果的名词尾构成，义为「恶化；退化；变质」
由该动词加形容词后缀构成，义为「不断恶化的」
由该动词加已然词尾构成，义为「已恶化的」
由该动词加表示倾向的形容词尾构成，义为「趋于恶化的」（少用）

senses.title: For health to worsen
senses.definition: for a person's physical or mental condition to decline steadily
senses.definitionCN: 人的身体或精神状况持续下滑
senses.example: His hearing deteriorated after years of noise exposure.
senses.exampleCN: 多年暴露在噪声中之后，他的听力变差了。
senses.why: The word describes a slide down a scale, and health is read on such a scale.
senses.whyCN: 这个词描述的是一路下滑，而健康状况正是按这样的刻度来读的。

senses.title: For relations to sour
senses.definition: for ties between people, groups or states to become less friendly over time
senses.definitionCN: 人与人、群体与群体或国与国之间的关系随时间变得不友好
senses.example: Relations between the two offices deteriorated after the dispute.
senses.exampleCN: 争执之后，两个办事处的关系变差了。
senses.why: A relationship is a standing structure, and deteriorate records its slow loss of strength.
senses.whyCN: 关系是一种立着的结构，这个词记录它缓慢失去强度。

senses.title: For conditions to degrade
senses.definition: for the physical state of a place, building or system to get progressively worse
senses.definitionCN: 场所、建筑或系统的物理状态逐步变差
senses.example: The housing stock deteriorated faster than the city could repair it.
senses.exampleCN: 住房状况恶化的速度超过了城市的修缮能力。
senses.why: Materials and places wear down in one direction, and the verb names that one-way drift.
senses.whyCN: 材料与场所只朝一个方向磨损，这个词命名那种单向漂移。

senses.title: For quality to decline
senses.definition: for the quality of a product or material to fall below an earlier standard
senses.definitionCN: 产品或材料的质量降到早先标准之下
senses.example: The stored grain deteriorated because the silo was damp.
senses.exampleCN: 因为粮仓潮湿，储存的谷物变质了。
senses.why: Quality is a level, and the verb says the level keeps dropping.
senses.whyCN: 质量是一个水平线，这个词说这条线一直在往下掉。

senses.title: For performance to decay
senses.definition: for a machine or system to work less well than before
senses.definitionCN: 机器或系统的运转效果不如从前
senses.example: Battery performance deteriorates in freezing weather.
senses.exampleCN: 电池性能在严寒天气里会衰减。
senses.why: Engineering treats wear as a predictable curve, and deteriorate is the verb for the downward part.
senses.whyCN: 工程把磨损看作一条可预测的曲线，这个词专指向下的那一段。

senses.title: For economic indicators to weaken
senses.definition: for trade, output or confidence to move towards a worse position
senses.definitionCN: 贸易、产出或信心朝更差的方向移动
senses.example: The trade balance deteriorated for the third quarter running.
senses.exampleCN: 贸易差额连续第三个季度恶化。
senses.why: Economists read a falling line as a worsening, and the verb carries no other emotion.
senses.whyCN: 经济学家把下行的曲线读作恶化，这个词不带别的情绪。

senses.title: For a medical condition to progress badly
senses.definition: for a disease or a patient's state to move towards a worse stage
senses.definitionCN: 疾病或病人的状态走向更差的阶段
senses.example: The patient deteriorated overnight and was moved to intensive care.
senses.exampleCN: 病人一夜之间恶化，被转入重症监护。
senses.why: Clinical writing uses the verb for the direction of a course, not for its speed.
senses.whyCN: 临床记录用这个动词说明病程方向，而不说明速度。

senses.title: For order or safety to decline
senses.definition: for public order, security or discipline to become weaker or more dangerous
senses.definitionCN: 公共秩序、安全或纪律变得薄弱或更危险
senses.example: Security in the district deteriorated after the patrols stopped.
senses.exampleCN: 巡逻停止后，该区的治安恶化了。
senses.why: Order is a structure held by many hands, and the verb marks the strain that loosens it.
senses.whyCN: 秩序是许多只手撑着的结构，这个词标出把它松开的那些拉力。

intro.en: Deteriorate comes from Late Latin deteriorare, to make worse, from deterior, worse, a comparative whose positive form is not attested. French and English adopted the verb in the sixteenth century.
intro.cn: 这个词来自晚期拉丁语 deteriorare「使变坏」，出自比较级 deterior「更坏」，而其原级形式并无记录；法语与英语在十六世纪采用它。

items.en: Deterior was the comparative of an older adjective meaning lower or inferior, and that positive form survives only as a reconstruction.
items.cn: 这是较古形容词「较低、较差」的比较级，而那个原级只以重构形式存在，没有实际记录。

items.en: The verb meant to make worse or to become worse, and it appears mainly in later technical and medical writing.
items.cn: 这个动词意为使变坏或变坏，主要见于较晚的技术与医学文献。

items.en: French formed its own verb from the same Latin comparative and passed it to English.
items.cn: 法语由同一拉丁比较级造出自己的动词，再传给英语。

items.en: English records the verb from the sixteenth century; the exact first date is uncertain.
items.cn: 英语自十六世纪有记录，确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: The base adjective behind deterior cannot be recovered from any surviving text, so its source is uncertain.
items.cn: deterior 背后的原级形容词无法从任何传世文本中复原，因此标记为来源不确定。

items.en: Medicine and economics gave the verb fixed subjects such as condition, patient and balance.
items.cn: 医学与经济学给这个动词添了固定主语，如状况、病人与收支。

note.en: The first group looks close or shares the deteriorating stem; the second group names neighbouring ideas of decline.
note.cn: 第一组与「deteriorate」形近或共享「恶化」词干；第二组是与「下滑」意思相邻的说法。

entries.definition: The noun for the process of becoming worse.
entries.definitionCN: 指变坏这一过程的名词。

entries.definition: The adjective for something in the middle of getting worse.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，指正处在恶化过程中的。

entries.definition: To settle or decide, from terminus, a boundary; it looks close but is unrelated.
entries.definitionCN: 指确定、决定，出自「边界」；形近但无亲缘。

entries.definition: Something that discourages an action, from a verb meaning to frighten away.
entries.definitionCN: 指起威慑作用的事物，出自「吓退」的动词。

entries.definition: Harm or damage, from a different Latin stem.
entries.definitionCN: 指损害，出自另一拉丁词干。

entries.definition: To become or make worse, the plainest verb of the group.
entries.definitionCN: 指变坏或使变坏，是本组最朴素的说法。

entries.definition: To go down in amount or quality, often neutral in tone.
entries.definitionCN: 指数量或质量下降，语气常较中性。

entries.definition: To lower in quality, rank or condition.
entries.definitionCN: 指质量、等级或状况降低。

entries.definition: To rot or break down slowly through natural processes.
entries.definitionCN: 指经自然过程缓慢腐烂或分解。

entries.definition: To wear away gradually, literally by wind or water.
entries.definitionCN: 指逐渐磨损，字面多指风水侵蚀。

entries.definition: To fall suddenly in value or performance.
entries.definitionCN: 指价值或表现突然下跌。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the worse comparative, its missing base, and the fixed subjects medicine and economics give it.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用「更坏」这一比较级、它缺失的原级，以及医学与经济学给它的固定主语。

normal.en: Deterior is already a comparative, so the word starts from the idea of worse, not bad.
normal.cn: deterior 本身是比较级，所以这个词从「更坏」而不是「坏」起步。

normal.en: The positive adjective behind it never survived, which is the honest reason for marking its origin uncertain.
normal.cn: 它背后的原级形容词没有传下来，这正是把来源标为存疑的诚实理由。

normal.en: Doctors write that a patient deteriorated overnight.
normal.cn: 医生会写病人一夜之间恶化。

normal.en: Economists write that the trade balance deteriorated.
normal.cn: 经济学家会写贸易差额恶化。

normal.en: Deterioration is the noun, and deteriorating is the adjective used before situation.
normal.cn: 名词是 deterioration，形容词 deteriorating 常用于 situation 之前。

abstract.en: To deteriorate is to lose strength without any single blow, which is the hardest kind of damage to notice.
abstract.cn: 恶化是没有一次重击却不断失去强度，这是最难察觉的一种损坏。

abstract.en: Every system has a downward curve, and the word simply names the slope.
abstract.cn: 每个系统都有一条下行曲线，这个词只是给那道坡命名。

abstract.en: Things do not usually collapse; they first become slightly worse than yesterday.
abstract.cn: 事物通常不是突然崩塌的，而是先比昨天差一点。

examples.en: The road surface deteriorated quickly after the winter frosts.
examples.cn: 冬季霜冻之后，路面很快恶化了。

examples.en: Their working relationship deteriorated after the failed merger.
examples.cn: 合并失败后，他们的工作关系变差了。

examples.en: Air quality deteriorates whenever the wind drops.
examples.cn: 风一停，空气质量就恶化。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「迪提里奥瑞特」——旧墙起皮，裂缝一天比一天宽：恶化、变坏

root: 拉丁语 deterior「更坏」（比较级，原级无传世记录，直接来源不确定）→ 晚期拉丁语 deteriorare「使变坏」→ 法语 détériorer；英语十六世纪引入。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one downward slope through health, relations, places, quality, machinery, economy, illness and public order.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一条下坡走过健康、关系、场所、质量、机器、经济、病情与治安。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: plaster flakes off an old wall and the crack widens a little every day.
core.cn: 核心意象：旧墙抹灰一片片起皮，裂缝每天宽一点。

branches.en: THE BODY SLIDES: a person's condition or a disease course moves to a worse stage.
branches.cn: 身体下滑：人的状况或病程走向更差的阶段。

branches.en: THE TIE LOOSENS: relations lose their friendliness without any single break.
branches.cn: 纽带松了：关系失去友好，却不是一次断裂。

branches.en: THE MATERIAL WEARS: buildings and stored goods fall below an earlier standard.
branches.cn: 材料磨损：建筑与存粮降到早先标准之下。

branches.en: THE MACHINE LOSES EDGE: output falls as parts age or conditions harden.
branches.cn: 机器失锋：部件老化或条件变严，输出随之下降。

branches.en: THE SYSTEM SAGS: balances weaken and public order grows more dangerous.
branches.cn: 系统下沉：收支走弱，治安变得更危险。

intro.en: Deteriorate is a Late Latin verb built on a comparative adjective, so its affixes are the endings of comparison and of verb formation.
intro.cn: 这是一个建立在比较级形容词上的晚期拉丁动词，其词缀是比较级与动词构成用的词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplies deterior and deteriorare; the positive adjective behind deterior is not attested, so the base is marked uncertain rather than invented.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语提供了 deterior 与 deteriorare；deterior 背后的原级形容词没有记录，因此只标存疑，不作编造。

items.exampleCN: 这个比较级已经带上了这个词的方向。

items.example: It marks the form as a comparison, not a positive quality.
items.exampleCN: 它标明该形式是比较级，而非原级性质。

items.example: The verb turns the comparison into a process.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词把比较变成过程。

items.example: It marks the English verb.
items.exampleCN: 它标明英语动词。

items.example: It forms deterioration.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 deterioration。

items.example: It forms deteriorating.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 deteriorating。

items.example: It forms the rare deteriorative.
items.exampleCN: 它构成少用的 deteriorative。

items.example: It forms the adjective for what has already worsened.
items.exampleCN: 它构成表示「已恶化」的形容词。

由该动词加形容词后缀构成，义为「不断恶化的」
由该动词加表示倾向的形容词尾构成，义为「趋于恶化的」（少用）
由该动词加已然词尾构成，义为「已恶化的」

definition_zh: 持有人；持有者；支架；托架；夹具
definition_en: a person who owns or has something such as a ticket or a title, or an object used to hold something in place
core_image: 握住不放的手：证件、头衔被握在手里，笔被卡在托架上
scene: 图书馆的借阅台上，管理员把卡片递还给他，说了一句。 The library clerk handed back the card and said, "Show it to the holder at the front desk."
sceneCN: 这里 holder 是「持有人」（第 1 个义项：合法持有某物的人）；句意是管理员让他把卡片出示给前台那位持有它的人，核心画面是把东西握在手里的人。

pos.zh: 持有人；持有者（证件、头衔、职务等）
支架；托架；夹具（固定物品的器具）

derivatives.zh: 基础动词，握住；持有；容纳，holder 由它加施动者后缀构成
hold 加 -ing 构成，义为「持有；持有的股份或产业」
house 与 hold 复合，义为「家庭；一家人」
古英语复合词，义为「门槛；起点」，词源与 hold 无关

senses.title: A person who legally has something
senses.definition: a person who owns, possesses, or officially has something such as a ticket, a card, or an account
senses.definitionCN: 合法拥有或持有票证、卡片、账户等东西的人
senses.example: Ticket holders should arrive thirty minutes early.
senses.exampleCN: 持票人应提前三十分钟到场。
senses.why: The verb hold means to keep something in your hands, so a holder is simply the person on the other side of that hand.
senses.whyCN: 动词 hold 表示「握住」，holder 就是「握着它的人」，从手上的动作落到人的身份上。

senses.title: A person who holds a title, record, or position
senses.definition: a person who has a title, a record, an office, or a position
senses.definitionCN: 拥有头衔、保持纪录或担任某一职务的人
senses.example: She is the world record holder in the marathon.
senses.exampleCN: 她是马拉松世界纪录保持者。
senses.why: A title or record is imagined as something grasped and not let go, so the person keeping it is the holder.
senses.whyCN: 头衔和纪录被想象成「握在手里不放」的东西，谁握着谁就是 holder。

senses.title: An object used to hold something in place
senses.definition: a device or container designed to keep an object steady or in position
senses.definitionCN: 用来固定或安放物品的器具，使其稳定不动
senses.example: There is a cup holder beside each seat in the car.
senses.exampleCN: 车内每个座位旁边都有一个杯架。
senses.why: The core image of holding extends from people to tools: the device literally holds the object for you.
senses.whyCN: 「握住」的意象从人扩展到器具：这种装置替你「握住」物品，于是也叫 holder。

intro.en: Holder is a transparent English formation: the verb hold plus the agent suffix -er.
intro.cn: holder 是一个构成透明的英语词：动词 hold 加上表「人／物」的后缀 -er。

items.en: The verb goes back to the reconstructed Proto-Germanic root *haldan or *huldan, meaning to keep or to grasp.
items.cn: 动词可追溯至重构的原始日耳曼语词根 *haldan／*huldan，意为「保存；抓住」。

items.en: In Old English it appears as healdan, meaning to contain, to keep, or to guard.
items.cn: 古英语写作 healdan，表示「容纳；保有；守护」。

items.en: The verb settles as holden, and the agent noun holder emerges with the -er suffix.
items.cn: 中古英语定型为 holden，带 -er 后缀的施动名词 holder 随之出现。

items.en: The personal sense, one who has a title or a document, becomes common in legal and commercial writing.
items.cn: 表示「持有文件、头衔之人」的用法在十六至十七世纪的法律与商业文书中普及。

items.en: The object sense, a device that holds something, spreads with everyday inventions such as pen holders and match holders.
items.cn: 十九世纪随笔架、火柴座等日常小物件的普及，「固定物品的器具」一义广泛使用。

items.en: Today holder freely combines with other nouns: ticket holder, account holder, cup holder.
items.cn: 如今 holder 可自由与名词组合：ticket holder 持票人、account holder 账户持有人、cup holder 杯架。

note.en: Holder looks plain, but it hides two near neighbours with different suffixes and a small family of look-alikes.
note.cn: holder 看似简单，但它有两个后缀相近的邻居，还有一小群拼写相像的词。

entries.definition: the base verb meaning to keep, grasp, or contain
entries.definitionCN: 基础动词：握住；持有；容纳，holder 的直接来源

entries.definition: property or shares that someone holds; the act of holding
entries.definitionCN: 持有的产业或股份；持有行为，hold 加 -ing 构成

entries.definition: all the people living together in one home
entries.definitionCN: 家庭；一家人，由 house 与 hold 复合而成

entries.definition: brave and confident; also describing heavy printed type
entries.definitionCN: 大胆的；粗体的，只是拼写相近，词源与 hold 不同

entries.definition: comparative of old, meaning of greater age
entries.definitionCN: old 的比较级：年纪更大的，发音接近 holder，词源无关

entries.definition: a person who owns something, especially property or a business
entries.definitionCN: 所有者；物主，强调所有权而非 merely 持有

entries.definition: a person who has or owns something, often in legal contexts
entries.definitionCN: 占有人；持有人，正式用语，常见于法律语境

entries.definition: a person who takes care of or guards something
entries.definitionCN: 保管人；看守人，侧重「看管」而非「持有」

entries.definition: a device attached to a wall to hold or support something
entries.definitionCN: 托架；支架，与 holder 第 3 义项相近

entries.definition: a person who holds property or land by renting it
entries.definitionCN: 租户；承租人，以租借方式「持有」的人

normalIntro.en: Five anchors built from the real root hold and its real combinations.
normalIntro.cn: 五条锚点，全部基于真实的词根 hold 及其真实组合。

normal.en: hold + -er: the one who holds is the holder.
normal.cn: hold 加 -er：握着的人就是「持有者」。

normal.en: Ticket holder: the ticket is in that person's hand.
normal.cn: 持票人：票就攥在那个人手里。

normal.en: Record holder: the record has never been let go.
normal.cn: 纪录保持者：纪录一直被「握住」没被打破。

normal.en: Cup holder: the little device holds your cup steady.
normal.cn: 杯架：替你「握住」水杯的小装置。

normal.en: Account holder: the bank account belongs to this person.
normal.cn: 账户持有人：银行账户就记在这人名下。

abstract.en: Picture a hand that never opens: whatever it grips makes its owner a holder.
abstract.cn: 想象一只永不松开的手：握住什么，它主人就是什么 holder。

abstract.en: A trophy on a shelf is held by a bracket, just as a title is held by a person.
abstract.cn: 架上的奖杯被托架「握」着，头衔被人在「握」着，画面相通。

abstract.en: From gripping hands to gripping tools, the idea of steady holding never changes.
abstract.cn: 从握紧的手到咬合的卡扣，「稳稳握住」这一个意象贯穿所有义项。

examples.en: The account holder must sign the form in person.
examples.cn: 账户持有人必须亲自在这份表格上签字。

examples.en: Every seat in the new car has a cup holder.
examples.cn: 新车的每个座位都配有杯架。

examples.en: She became the record holder after swimming the fastest lap.
examples.cn: 游出最快一圈之后，她成了纪录保持者。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「厚的」——想象一张很厚的大存折，握在谁手里，谁就是持有人（holder）。

root: holder 由动词 hold（握住；持有）加施动者后缀 -er 构成，属古英语本族词。hold 可追溯至重构的原始日耳曼语词根 *haldan／*huldan，一般认为与「看守、容纳」义相关；与拉丁词根无亲缘关系。

sensesIntro.en: The core image is a hand that does not let go: it points to a person holding a document or title, and then to a device holding an object.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心意象是一只不松开的手：先指向握着证件或头衔的人，再延伸到固定物品的器具。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a steady grip, held by a person or by a device
core.cn: 核心意象：一次稳定的握持，可以出自人手，也可以出自器具

branches.en: the hand on a ticket or card makes that person the holder
branches.cn: 握着票证的那只手，让人成为持有人

branches.en: a title or record is imagined as something gripped and never released
branches.cn: 头衔与纪录被想象成握住不放的东西

branches.en: both personal senses share the idea of lawful keeping
branches.cn: 两个「人」的义项共享「合法保有」的观念

branches.en: the device sense appears when the holder is a bracket or tray
branches.cn: 当握持者变成托架或卡座，就长出器具义

branches.en: keeping a title and fixing an object both rest on the same steady grip
branches.cn: 保持头衔与固定物品，都立足于同一次稳定的握持

intro.en: Holder is built from a native English verb plus the most productive agent suffix in the language.
intro.cn: holder 由英语本族动词加英语里最高产的施动者后缀构成。

latinIntro.en: The suffix -er is Germanic, not Latin, but Latin uses -or for the same job; the pairs below show the parallel.
