驯化（domesticate 加名词后缀，指归作家养的过程）
家庭生活；居家性（domestic 加名词后缀，指家庭生活的性质）
在国内（domestic 加副词后缀，指以本国为范围）
市场；推销（短语的另一半，语义为交易场所或交易行为）

senses.title: The market inside one's own country
senses.definition: the market contained within a country's borders, viewed in contrast to foreign markets
senses.definitionCN: 位于一国边界之内的市场，与外国市场相对而言
senses.example: The firm expects its domestic market to grow before it expands abroad.
senses.exampleCN: 公司预计先在国内市场取得增长，再向海外扩张。
senses.why: Domestic comes from Latin domesticus 'of the household', and a nation is often imagined as one large household, so the word marks what is inside the national walls.
senses.whyCN: domestic 出自拉丁 domesticus「家里的」，而国家常被想象成一个大家庭，因此这个词标出国家院墙之内的事物。

senses.title: Home-country buyers as demand
senses.definition: the total demand from buyers inside the country
senses.definitionCN: 一国之内买方形成的需求总和
senses.example: Domestic market demand absorbed most of the new output.
senses.exampleCN: 国内市场需求吸收了大部分新增产量。
senses.why: Market also names the buyers, so the domestic market can mean the sum of home customers rather than a place.
senses.whyCN: market 也指买方，因此国内市场可以指本国客户的总和，而不是一个地点。

senses.title: The home market for one product
senses.definition: the supply and demand inside the country for a single product or service
senses.definitionCN: 某单一产品或服务在一国之内的供给与需求
senses.example: The domestic market for electric cars doubled in three years.
senses.exampleCN: 电动汽车的国内市场三年内翻了一番。
senses.why: Naming the product narrows the national arena to one trade, as in the domestic steel market.
senses.whyCN: 点明产品就把国家范围收窄到一桩生意，如国内钢铁市场。

senses.title: Share held at home
senses.titleCN: 在本国市场所占的份额
senses.definition: the portion of national sales held by a firm or brand
senses.definitionCN: 某企业或品牌在本国销售中所占的部分
senses.example: The group controls half of the domestic market in cement.
senses.exampleCN: 该集团控制国内水泥市场的一半。
senses.why: Share language turns the national arena into a pie, and domestic says which pie is being cut.
senses.whyCN: 份额说法把本国竞技场变成一块饼，domestic 说明被切的是哪一块饼。

senses.title: Prices set inside the country
senses.titleCN: 由国内供求形成的价格
senses.definition: the price level within the country, affected by local costs and tariffs
senses.definitionCN: 一国之内的价格水平，受本地成本与关税影响
senses.example: Domestic market prices rose after the import duty was raised.
senses.exampleCN: 进口关税上调后，国内市场价格上涨。
senses.why: Protected by a border, home prices can drift away from world prices, so the phrase often marks that gap.
senses.whyCN: 在边界的保护下，国内价格可以偏离世界价格，因此这个短语常用来标出这道差距。

senses.title: The domestic market as a policy object
senses.titleCN: 作为政策对象的国内市场
senses.definition: the home market considered as something to be protected, regulated or opened
senses.definitionCN: 被视为需要保护、监管或开放的本国市场
senses.example: Quotas were meant to shield the domestic market from cheap imports.
senses.exampleCN: 配额意在保护国内市场免受廉价进口冲击。
senses.why: Once a state acts on the market, the phrase becomes a shorthand for a policy goal rather than a trading place.
senses.whyCN: 一旦国家对市场施以行动，这个短语就成为政策目标的代称，而不是交易场所。

senses.title: The size or capacity of the home market
senses.titleCN: 国内市场的规模与容量
senses.definition: the number of buyers and the purchasing capacity available inside the country
senses.definitionCN: 一国之内可用的买方数量与购买能力
senses.example: A small domestic market limits how far factories can grow.
senses.exampleCN: 国内市场狭小限制了工厂的扩张空间。
senses.why: Economists speak of market size, so the phrase can name capacity rather than activity.
senses.whyCN: 经济学家谈论市场容量，因此这个短语也可以指承载能力而非活动。

senses.title: Any internal arena of one's own group
senses.titleCN: 抽象义：自己圈子内部的场域
senses.definition: an internal setting within one's own community, field or institution
senses.definitionCN: 自己所属社群、领域或机构内部的场域
senses.example: For a regional paper, the province was a comfortable domestic market.
senses.exampleCN: 对一家地区性报纸来说，本省就是一个熟悉的内需市场。
senses.why: The abstract sense keeps the inside-outside contrast and drops the national border: any group can have an internal market.
senses.whyCN: 抽象义保留内外对比而去掉国界：任何群体都可以有自己的内部市场。

intro.en: Domestic market joins domestic, from Latin domesticus 'of the household', with market, from Latin mercatus 'trade'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: domestic market 把出自拉丁 domesticus「家里的」的 domestic，与出自拉丁 mercatus「交易」的 market 组合起来。年代均为约数。

items.en: Domus meant a house or household, and it built a large family of words about the home.
items.cn: domus 意为房屋或家庭，构成一大批关于家的词。

items.en: Domesticus meant belonging to the household; it described household affairs and, later, what is internal to a group.
items.cn: domesticus 意为属于家庭的，描述家务，后来也指某群体内部的事物。

items.en: English adopted domestic in the sixteenth century for household matters, then extended it to the internal affairs of a country.
items.cn: 英语在 16 世纪吸收 domestic 指家务，随后扩展到一国的内部事务。

items.en: Mercatus meant trade or a marketplace, from mercari 'to trade' and merx 'merchandise'.
items.cn: mercatus 意为交易或市场，出自 mercari「做买卖」与 merx「货物」。

items.en: Domestic market became standard in economics and business once national accounts separated home sales from exports.
items.cn: 一旦国民核算把国内销售与出口分开，domestic market 就成了经济与商业中的标准说法。

note.en: The first group shares the household root but has moved into other senses; the second group names markets that differ by the viewpoint taken.
note.cn: 第一组共享「家宅」词根但语义已转移；第二组是按立场区分的不同市场。

entries.definition: Of the household or of one's own country; alone it does not say what is being traded.
entries.definitionCN: 家庭的或本国的；单独使用时不说交易的对象是什么。

entries.definition: To bring a wild plant or animal into household use; the root is the same but the action is taming, not trading.
entries.definitionCN: 把野生植物或动物带入家养；词根相同，但动作是驯化，不是交易。

entries.definition: A person's legal place of residence, from domus 'house'; it names a dwelling, never a market.
entries.definitionCN: 个人的法定居住地，出自 domus「房屋」；它指住所，从不指市场。

entries.definition: The quality of home life; it shares the household root but describes private life, not national trade.
entries.definitionCN: 家庭生活的性质；共享「家宅」词根，却描述私人生活，不是国家贸易。

entries.definition: The market of one's own country; home is the native English word and domestic the Latin-derived formal variant.
entries.definitionCN: 本国市场；home 是英语本族词，domestic 是拉丁来源的正式变体。

entries.definition: A market inside a group of countries or a single organization; it stresses internal freedom of movement rather than nationality.
entries.definitionCN: 国家集团或单一组织内部的市场；它强调内部自由流动，而不强调国籍。

entries.definition: The market of a nation state; it overlaps with domestic market but treats the nation as the unit rather than the household image.
entries.definitionCN: 民族国家的市场；它与 domestic market 重叠，但以民族为单位，而不是以家宅为喻。

entries.definition: A market in a town or district; domestic market covers the whole country, which may contain many local markets.
entries.definitionCN: 城镇或区域的市场；国内市场覆盖全国，其中可能包含许多本地市场。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the household root, the trade root and real business phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：家宅词根、交易词根与真实商业搭配。

normal.en: Domestic means of the household, and a country is imagined as one household, so the phrase is trade inside the national house.
normal.cn: domestic 意为家里的，而国家被想象成一个大家庭，所以这个短语指国家这所房子内部的交易。

normal.en: The two halves have separate Latin sources: domus for the house, mercatus for trade.
normal.cn: 两半各有拉丁来源：domus 表房屋，mercatus 表交易。

normal.en: Fixed phrases show the uses: domestic market share, domestic market demand, domestic market prices.
normal.cn: 固定搭配显示用法：国内市场份额、国内市场需求、国内市场价格。

normal.en: It is the standard opposite of foreign market, and the two are often used in the same sentence.
normal.cn: 它是 foreign market 的标准反义说法，两者常出现在同一句中。

normal.en: Do not confuse domestic meaning household with domestic meaning national: context decides which house is meant.
normal.cn: 不要把「家庭的」与「国家的」两种 domestic 混淆：语境决定指的是哪个家。

abstract.en: Picture a walled courtyard where prices are posted inside and a different price list hangs outside.
abstract.cn: 想象一座有围墙的院子，院内挂着价目表，院外挂着另一份价目表。

abstract.en: Picture one large family whose kitchen, garden and storeroom form a closed circle of exchange.
abstract.cn: 想象一个大家庭，厨房、菜园与储藏室构成一个封闭的交换圈。

abstract.en: Picture a club where members trade favours among themselves and outsiders are not quoted a price.
abstract.cn: 想象一个俱乐部，成员在内部交换人情，对外人不报价。

examples.en: The company sells mostly to the domestic market.
examples.cn: 这家公司主要面向国内市场销售。

examples.en: Domestic market growth slowed as the population aged.
examples.cn: 随着人口老龄化，国内市场增长放缓。

examples.en: Tariffs raised domestic market prices above world levels.
examples.cn: 关税把国内市场价格抬到世界水平之上。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「自己家里的集市」——domus 是家，market 是集市，家里这一片的买卖就是国内市场

root: domestic 出自拉丁 domesticus「家里的」，源 domus「房屋」；market 出自拉丁 mercatus「交易」。合指「一国边界之内的市场」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all stay inside one boundary: the market within the country, its buyers, one product's home trade, a share of it, its prices, its policy role, its size and finally any internal arena.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都留在同一道边界之内：国内的市场、它的买方、单一产品的国内贸易、其份额、其价格、其政策角色、其规模，最后是任何内部场域。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a walled courtyard with one price list inside and another outside.
core.cn: 核心意象：一座有围墙的院子，院内院外各挂一份价目表。

branches.en: BASE INSIDENESS: the market lies within the national walls.
branches.cn: 基础的内在性：市场位于国家院墙之内。

branches.en: BUYERS AND PRODUCT: the arena sums to home demand, or narrows to one trade.
branches.cn: 买方与产品：竞技场可汇成国内需求，也可收窄到一桩生意。

branches.en: MEASURED AND PRICED: the home pie is divided by share and priced by local cost.
branches.cn: 计量与定价：本国的饼按份额分割，按本地成本定价。

branches.en: STATE VIEW: the market is shielded by policy and measured by capacity.
branches.cn: 国家视角：市场被政策护住，并用容量衡量。

branches.en: METAPHOR: any group can have an internal market of its own.
branches.cn: 比喻：任何群体都可以有自己的内部市场。

intro.en: Domestic market joins two free words, one built on the Latin word for house and one on the Latin word for trade.
intro.cn: domestic market 由两个自由词构成，一个建立在拉丁语「房屋」之上，一个建立在拉丁语「交易」之上。

latinIntro.en: Latin domus 'house' gives domestic, domesticate, domicile and domesticity; Latin mercatus 'trade' gives market, marketing, marketplace and merchant.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 domus「房屋」衍生 domestic、domesticate、domicile 与 domesticity；拉丁 mercatus「交易」衍生 market、marketing、marketplace 与 merchant。

items.example: The element builds words about the home.
items.exampleCN: 这个成分构成一批关于家的词。

items.meaning: of the household or home country
items.example: Domestic demand stayed strong.
items.exampleCN: 国内需求保持强劲。

items.example: People domesticated wheat early.
items.exampleCN: 人类很早驯化了小麦。

items.example: Domestication changed the grain.
items.exampleCN: 驯化改变了谷物。

items.example: The novel praised domesticity.
items.exampleCN: 这部小说赞美家庭生活。

items.example: Their domicile is in the capital.
items.exampleCN: 他们的法定住所在首都。

items.meaning: a place or system of trade
items.example: The market fell sharply.
items.exampleCN: 市场大幅下跌。

items.example: Marketing drove the growth.
items.exampleCN: 营销推动了增长。

items.example: The marketplace opened online.
items.exampleCN: 这个市场在线上开张。

items.example: They lead the domestic market.
items.exampleCN: 他们在国内市场领先。

definition_zh: 干旱；旱灾；长期缺雨；（资源、机会的）长期匮乏
definition_en: a prolonged period of abnormally low rainfall that causes water shortage; also a long scarcity of anything
core_image: 水库退成一片龟裂的泥滩，旧船坞悬在干岸上方，远处只剩一条细水
scene: 连续第三年缺雨，水库退成一片龟裂的泥滩。 The reservoir shrank to cracked mud after the third year of drought.
sceneCN: 这里 drought 指「持续异常少雨、造成缺水的时期」（第 1 个义项：气象干旱）；句意为连续第三年干旱之后，水库缩成龟裂泥滩。图中可辨识物件：泥滩裂缝、悬空的旧船坞、细水线、岸边枯草。

pos.zh: 干旱；旱灾；长期匮乏（可数或不可数）

derivatives.zh: 干旱的；易旱的
抗干旱的
耐干旱的
遭受旱灾的

senses.title: A long period of low rainfall
senses.definition: a prolonged period in which rainfall falls well below the normal for that place and season
senses.definitionCN: 降水明显低于该地与季节常值的持续时期
senses.example: The reservoir shrank to cracked mud after the third year of drought.
senses.exampleCN: 连续第三年干旱之后，水库缩成龟裂的泥滩。
senses.why: drought is defined against a local normal, so the same rainfall can be a drought in one place and a wet year in another.
senses.whyCN: 干旱是相对于当地常值定义的，同样的雨在一地算旱，在另一地算湿年。

senses.title: Agricultural drought
senses.definition: the soil-moisture shortfall that harms crops at their sensitive growth stages
senses.definitionCN: 在作物敏感生长期造成损害的土壤水分亏缺
senses.example: Rain fell in June, but an agricultural drought had already ruined the maize.
senses.exampleCN: 六月下了雨，但农业干旱早已毁掉玉米。
senses.why: rain that arrives after the critical stage does not undo the damage, so farms experience drought differently from weather stations.
senses.whyCN: 关键期之后才来的雨挽不回损失，因此农田所经历的干旱与气象站不同。

senses.title: Hydrological drought
senses.definition: the lagged shortage of streamflow, groundwater and reservoir storage after rainfall deficits
senses.definitionCN: 降水亏缺之后，河流流量、地下水与水库蓄水滞后出现的不足
senses.example: Hydrological drought persisted for two years after the rains returned.
senses.exampleCN: 雨回来后，水文干旱仍持续了两年。
senses.why: catchments store water, so rivers and wells record drought later and recover more slowly than the sky does.
senses.whyCN: 流域会蓄水，因此河流与水井记录干旱更晚，恢复也比天空更慢。

senses.title: Socioeconomic drought
senses.definition: the shortfall that appears when demand for water, food or power exceeds supply under dry conditions
senses.definitionCN: 干旱条件下，对水、食物或电力的需求超过供给所出现的短缺
senses.example: The city's socioeconomic drought hit when reservoirs failed and demand kept rising.
senses.exampleCN: 水库见底而需求仍在上升时，城市的社会经济干旱爆发。
senses.why: the shortage is produced by the balance of supply and demand, not by rainfall alone.
senses.whyCN: 短缺由供给与需求的平衡造成，而非仅由降水造成。

senses.title: A seasonal dry spell
senses.definition: the predictable dry season of a monsoon or Mediterranean climate, which farmers plan around
senses.definitionCN: 季风或地中海气候中可预期的旱季，农民据此安排耕作
senses.example: The seasonal drought lasts from November to April here.
senses.exampleCN: 这里的季节性干旱从十一月持续到四月。
senses.why: a dry season is normal, so drought becomes a question of degree: longer or harder than the usual dry spell.
senses.whyCN: 旱季本身正常，因此干旱变成程度问题：比通常的旱段更长或更烈。

senses.title: A figurative scarcity of anything
senses.definition: a prolonged shortage of something other than water, such as goals, funding or talent
senses.definitionCN: 水以外事物的长期短缺，如进球、资金或人才
senses.example: The club ended a ten-year drought without a title.
senses.exampleCN: 俱乐部结束了十年无冠的荒。
senses.why: the metaphor transfers 'no rain for too long' to any supply that has dried up.
senses.whyCN: 这一比喻把「太久没下雨」移到任何已干涸的供给上。

senses.title: Classifying drought severity
senses.definition: the grading of drought by indices such as the Palmer index or the standardised precipitation index
senses.definitionCN: 用帕尔默指数或标准化降水指数等指标对干旱分等
senses.example: The state declared drought stage three after the index fell for six months.
senses.exampleCN: 指数连续六个月下降后，州里宣布三级干旱。
senses.why: management needs thresholds, so a continuous deficit is divided into discrete stages that trigger rules.
senses.whyCN: 管理需要阈值，于是连续的亏缺被分成可触发规则的离散阶段。

senses.title: Drought as a slow disaster
senses.definition: a natural hazard that develops slowly, spreads widely and does most of its damage through food and water systems
senses.definitionCN: 发展缓慢、范围广、主要经食物与水系统造成损害的自然灾害
senses.example: Drought kills more livestock than any single storm.
senses.exampleCN: 干旱杀死的牲畜多过任何一场单独的风暴。
senses.why: unlike a flood, drought has no clear start, which is exactly why it is under-reported as a disaster.
senses.whyCN: 与洪水不同，干旱没有明确起点，这正是它作为灾害被少报的原因。

intro.en: Drought is a native English word from Old English drugað 'dryness', built on a verb for drying, and related to dry.
intro.cn: drought 是英语本族词，来自古英语 drugað「干燥」，由表示「使干」的动词构成，并与 dry 同族。

items.en: Drugað meant 'dryness' and was formed from drugian 'to dry', a Germanic verb of uncertain deeper origin.
items.cn: drugað 意为「干燥」，由 drugian「使干」构成，后者是更深来源不确定的日耳曼动词。

items.en: The stock behind both drought and dry is usually reconstructed as *draugiz 'dry', a form not directly attested.
items.cn: drought 与 dry 背后的共同词干通常重构为 *draugiz「干燥」，这一形式没有直接书证。

items.en: Middle English kept the word with the -ght ending that also appears in daughter and night, and fixed it as the noun for dry weather.
items.cn: 中古英语保留这个词，并带上也见于 daughter、night 的 -ght 词尾，固定为指干旱天气的名词。

items.en: From the nineteenth century drought extended figuratively to any long shortage, as in a scoring drought.
items.cn: 从 19 世纪起，drought 比喻性地扩展到任何长期短缺，如「进球荒」。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper root): the relation to dry is accepted, but the pre-Germanic root is a reconstruction; the exact first citation of the figurative sense is not securely dated.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词根）：与 dry 的关系被接受，但其日耳曼语之前词根属重构；比喻义的最早书证年代不可靠。

note.en: Group one separates the drought family and near spellings; group two separates the shortage words that are not a period of low rain.
note.cn: 第一组区分 drought 词族与相近拼写；第二组区分并非「少雨时期」的短缺词。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning prone to drought, used of soils or regions; it is rare in modern prose.
entries.definitionCN: 意为易旱的形容词，用于土壤或地区；现代书面语中少见。

entries.definition: The everyday adjective for lacking moisture; it shares the same Germanic stock as drought.
entries.definitionCN: 表示缺水的日常形容词；与 drought 共享同一日耳曼词干。

entries.definition: Describing a plant or variety that can resist drought damage, a compound built on the noun.
entries.definitionCN: 形容能抵抗干旱损害的植物或品种，由该名词构成的复合词。

entries.definition: Land degradation to desert; drought can trigger it, but it is a lasting change of land, not a period.
entries.definitionCN: 土地退化为荒漠；干旱可触发它，但它是土地的持久变化，不是一段时期。

entries.definition: A short run of dry weather; drought is longer and is measured against a local normal.
entries.definitionCN: 一段较短的干燥天气；干旱更长，并要对照当地常值。

entries.definition: The resulting lack of usable water; a drought is one of its causes, along with demand and leakage.
entries.definitionCN: 由此产生的可用水不足；干旱是原因之一，需求与漏损也会造成。

entries.definition: The long-term climatic dryness of a place; drought is a departure from that place's normal.
entries.definitionCN: 某地长期的气候干燥；干旱是对该地常值的偏离。

entries.definition: A general shortage of any resource; it is the wider category to which figurative drought belongs.
entries.definitionCN: 任何资源的普遍短缺；是比喻性 drought 所属的更大类别。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Old English drugað 'dryness' is the direct ancestor.
normal.cn: 古英语 drugað「干燥」是直接祖先。

normal.en: The family runs drought, droughty, drought-resistant, drought-stricken.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 drought、droughty、drought-resistant、drought-stricken。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: severe drought, prolonged drought, drought relief, break the drought.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：严重干旱、长期干旱、抗旱救济、结束干旱。

normal.en: Four kinds: meteorological, agricultural, hydrological, socioeconomic.
normal.cn: 四种类型：气象、农业、水文、社会经济。

normal.en: The image is a reservoir turned to cracked mud with an stranded jetty.
normal.cn: 意象是水库变成龟裂泥滩，船坞搁在干岸上。

abstract.en: Think of a clock that has stopped but nobody can say when.
abstract.cn: 想象一只停了的钟，谁也说不出是哪一刻停的。

abstract.en: Think of a team scoring no goals for a decade, and the word borrowed from weather.
abstract.cn: 想象一支球队十年不进球，于是借用了天气的词。

abstract.en: Think of a debt that grows while the rain is absent.
abstract.cn: 想象一笔在无雨时不断增长的债。

examples.en: The drought lasted four years and emptied every farm dam.
examples.cn: 这场干旱持续四年，抽干了每个农用蓄水池。

examples.en: Drought relief reached the district only in the second year.
examples.cn: 抗旱救济到第二年才抵达该区。

examples.en: The orchestra ended its drought of recordings with a new album.
examples.cn: 乐团以一张新专辑结束了长期的录音空白。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「drought」读音近「照特」——太阳特别照，雨一直不来 → 干旱

root: 古英语 drugað「干燥」← drugian「使干」，与 dry 同出日耳曼词干 *draugiz（重构形式）。更深词源不确定，无拉丁同族。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses separate the weather period from its soil, river, demand and seasonal forms, then extend it to any long scarcity and to disaster management.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项把天气时期与其土壤、河流、需求、季节形式分开，再扩展到任何长期匮乏与灾害管理。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a water body withdrawing and leaving its old shoreline exposed.
core.cn: 核心意象：水体退去，露出旧日的岸线。

branches.en: WEATHER: a deficit against local normal, whether unexpected or seasonal.
branches.cn: 天气：对当地常值的亏缺，无论突发还是季节性。

branches.en: DELAY: soil dries first, then rivers and wells record the loss later.
branches.cn: 延迟：土壤先干，河流与水井更晚记录损失。

branches.en: DEMAND: shortage appears where supply and use no longer balance.
branches.cn: 需求：供给与使用不再平衡之处，短缺才出现。

branches.en: METAPHOR: any supply can be said to have gone without rain.
branches.cn: 比喻：任何供给都可被说成「久未下雨」。

branches.en: GOVERNANCE: thresholds turn a slow process into stages, warnings and relief.
branches.cn: 治理：阈值把缓慢过程变成阶段、警报与救济。

intro.en: Drought is a native noun that forms compounds freely, especially with resistant and tolerant for plant breeding.
intro.cn: drought 是本族名词，可自由构成复合词，尤其与 resistant、tolerant 组合用于植物育种。

latinIntro.en: Drought has no Latin element; the -ant in resistant and tolerant is Latin-derived, but it belongs to those adjectives, not to drought.
latinIntro.cn: drought 没有拉丁成分；resistant 与 tolerant 中的 -ant 虽源自拉丁，却属于那两个形容词，而非 drought。

items.example: The drought broke in early autumn.
items.exampleCN: 干旱在初秋结束。

items.example: Droughty soils hold little water.
items.exampleCN: 易旱土壤蓄水少。

items.example: Drought-resistant millet survives on little rain.
items.exampleCN: 抗旱黍靠少量雨水存活。

items.example: Drought-tolerant shrubs suit dry gardens.
items.exampleCN: 耐旱灌木适合干旱庭园。

items.example: Drought-stricken villages relied on tankers.
items.exampleCN: 受旱村庄依靠运水车。

items.example: Drought-prone districts store fodder early.
items.exampleCN: 易旱区早早储备饲草。

items.example: In a drought year the wells fail first.
items.exampleCN: 干旱年里水井最先枯。

items.meaning: end a dry period or a long failure
items.example: The storm broke the drought at last.
items.exampleCN: 这场风暴终于结束了干旱。

definition_zh: 财产；所有物；房产；不动产；性质；特性
definition_en: something owned, especially land or buildings, or a quality that belongs to a thing
core_image: 一块地界石立在草地边缘，石面刻着主人的记号，旁边摆着屋内可搬动的器物
scene: 遗产清册上，房子、田地与家具都列在同一栏，标明归谁所有。 The estate inventory listed the house, the land and the furniture in one column, each item marked as property belonging to a named heir.
sceneCN: 这里指「归某人所有的财物与地产」，对应第 1 个义项：被拥有、可被继承的物；句意为清册把房子、田地和家具列在同一栏并注明归属。画面要点：地界石、主人的记号、并列的器物；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 财产；所有物；房产（不可数，指财物总体；表示一件件具体物品时可用复数）
性质；特性（可数，常用于科学语境，指某物固有的属性）

derivatives.zh: 所有人；业主（表示「自己的」词根加表施事的名词后缀，指对某物享有所有权的人）
专有的；所有权的（名词加形容词后缀，指由某一所有人独占或与其所有权相关）
所有权；业主身份（名词加表身份或状态的名词后缀，指作为所有人的地位）
恰当的；本身的（由拉丁语中表示「自己的」形容词经法语传入，语义由「属于自己的」转为「合乎其本性的」）

senses.title: Things that belong to someone
senses.definition: the things a person owns, taken as a whole, including goods, money and rights
senses.definitionCN: 一个人所拥有的东西的总和，包括货物、金钱与权利
senses.example: The estate inventory listed the house, the land and the furniture in one column, each item marked as property belonging to a named heir.
senses.exampleCN: 遗产清册把房子、田地和家具列在同一栏，每件都注明属于某位继承人的财产。
senses.why: The Latin source means 'one's own', so the word begins as a label for whatever answers the question 'whose is it'.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语来源意为「自己的」，因此这个词起初就是给「这是谁的」这一问题的答案贴标签。

senses.title: Land and buildings
senses.definition: real estate, especially a house or plot that can be bought, sold or rented
senses.definitionCN: 不动产，尤指可买卖或出租的房屋或地块
senses.example: Property prices rose along the new railway.
senses.exampleCN: 新铁路沿线的房价上涨了。
senses.why: Land is the one thing that cannot be carried away, so it became the clearest test of who owns what.
senses.whyCN: 土地是唯一搬不走的东西，因此它成为「谁拥有什么」最清楚的检验。

senses.title: The right of ownership itself
senses.definition: the legal power to use, exclude others from, sell or give away a thing
senses.definitionCN: 使用某物、排除他人、出售或赠予该物的法律权力
senses.example: Property is a bundle of rights, not merely the object held.
senses.exampleCN: 所有权是一束权利，而不只是手中所持之物。
senses.why: Lawyers separate the object from the right over it, and the word covers both, which is why one can own property in property.
senses.whyCN: 法学家把物与对物的权利分开，而这个词同时覆盖两者，所以人可以对财产享有财产权。

senses.title: A quality belonging to a thing
senses.definition: a characteristic that a substance or object has, such as colour, hardness or conductivity
senses.definitionCN: 某物质或物体所具有的特征，如颜色、硬度或导电性
senses.example: The property that makes the alloy useful is its resistance to heat.
senses.exampleCN: 使这种合金有用的性质是它的耐热性。
senses.why: What belongs to a thing in the oldest sense includes not only goods but traits, because a trait is also something 'its own'.
senses.whyCN: 最古老意义上的「属于」不只包括财物，也包括特征，因为特征同样是某物「自己的」东西。

senses.title: Property in intangible things
senses.definition: ownership of ideas, marks, designs or other intangibles protected by law
senses.definitionCN: 对思想、标记、设计或其他受法律保护的无形之物的所有权
senses.example: A song can be property even though nothing physical is held.
senses.exampleCN: 一首歌可以是财产，尽管手中并未握着任何实体。
senses.why: If ownership is a legal relation rather than a physical grip, it can attach to what cannot be touched.
senses.whyCN: 如果所有权是一种法律关系而不是一把握持，它就能附着在摸不到的东西上。

senses.title: Objects used on a stage
senses.definition: the movable articles that an actor handles in a play or film
senses.definitionCN: 演员在戏剧或影片中操作的可移动物件
senses.example: The props master checks every property before the curtain rises.
senses.exampleCN: 道具管理员在幕启前检查每一件道具。
senses.why: The theatre borrowed the legal word for 'things owned by the company', shortened it, and kept the sense of objects that belong to a production.
senses.whyCN: 剧院借用了「剧团所有的物件」这一法律说法，把它缩短，保留了「属于某场演出之物」的意思。

senses.title: An attribute in logic and mathematics
senses.definition: a feature that may be predicated of an object, or a rule that a mathematical structure satisfies
senses.definitionCN: 可以述说某一对象的特征，或某一数学结构所满足的规则
senses.example: The proof uses a property shared by all prime numbers.
senses.exampleCN: 该证明用到所有素数共有的一个属性。
senses.why: The quality sense, pushed to its most abstract, becomes whatever can be said to belong to a class of objects.
senses.whyCN: 「性质」义被推到最抽象处，就成为一切可以说属于某类对象的特征。

senses.title: An estate or domain in older use
senses.definition: a landed estate with its house and lands, especially in historical and literary descriptions
senses.definitionCN: 连同宅邸与土地在内的地产，尤见于历史与文学描写
senses.example: The old property passed to the younger son.
senses.exampleCN: 那座旧庄园传给了小儿子。
senses.why: Before land became a commodity it was an inherited domain, and that older meaning survives in descriptions of country estates.
senses.whyCN: 在土地成为商品之前，它是承袭而来的领地，这一较早的含义仍保留在对乡间地产的描写中。

intro.en: Property comes from Latin proprietas 'ownership, quality', from proprius 'one's own'. The deeper origin of proprius is uncertain, and a derivation from a phrase meaning 'for the individual' has been suggested but not settled. English took the word through Old French.
intro.cn: property 出自拉丁语 proprietas「所有权、性质」，源头为 proprius「自己的」。proprius 的更深来源不确定，有人认为它出自一个意为「为个体所有」的短语，但未成定论。英语经古法语吸收此词。

items.en: Proprius meant 'one's own, particular, not shared'; its own origin is uncertain, and a derivation from a phrase meaning 'for the individual' has been proposed rather than proved.
items.cn: proprius 意为「自己的、特有的、不共享的」；它本身的来源不确定，有人认为它出自一个意为「为个体所有」的短语，但这只是提出而非证实。

items.en: Proprietas named both ownership and the quality that belongs to a thing, so the two later English senses were present from the start.
items.cn: proprietas 同时指所有权与某物固有的性质，因此后来英语中的两个义项从一开始就已存在。

items.en: Old French proprete carried both senses into English, where the legal and material side soon became dominant.
items.cn: 古法语 proprete 把两个义项都带入英语，其中法律与财物的一面很快占据主导。

items.en: In Middle English the word could still mean a quality, but land, goods and the right over them increasingly answered to it.
items.cn: 在中古英语中，这个词仍可指性质，但土地、货物以及对它们的权利越来越多地用它来表达。

items.en: In modern usage the material sense dominates law and everyday speech, while the quality sense survives mainly in science and logic. The date of this separation is approximate.
items.cn: 在现代用法中，财物义主导法律与日常表达，而性质义主要保存在科学与逻辑中。这一分家的年代为约数。

note.en: The first group is built on the same Latin adjective for 'one's own' but has drifted into fitness, decorum and exclusivity; the second group gives near alternatives for belongings and for qualities.
note.cn: 第一组由同一个表示「自己的」拉丁形容词构成，但已漂向合适、得体与独占；第二组是「财物」与「性质」两个方向的近义替代。

entries.definition: Correct or suitable, and in some phrases meaning 'itself'; the sense moved from 'belonging to a thing' to 'fitting that thing'.
entries.definitionCN: 正确的、合适的，在某些短语中意为「本身」；语义由「属于某物」转为「合乎某物」。

entries.definition: Correctness of behaviour or of usage; it comes from the same source but describes what is fitting rather than what is owned.
entries.definitionCN: 行为或用语得体；它出自同一来源，但描述合乎礼仪之事，而不是被拥有之物。

entries.definition: Owned by a particular person or firm, or sold under an exclusive name; it is the adjective built on the ownership sense.
entries.definitionCN: 由特定个人或公司所有的，或以独占名称销售的；它是建立在所有权义上的形容词。

entries.definition: The plural means several pieces of real estate or several qualities; the theatre shortening props belongs here too.
entries.definitionCN: 复数形式可指数处房产或数种性质；剧院用语中的缩略形式也归在这里。

entries.definition: The fact of having something in one's control; it can exist without legal ownership, which is why the two are distinguished in law.
entries.definitionCN: 某物处于某人控制之下的事实；它可以没有法律上的所有权而存在，因此法律上把两者区分开。

entries.definition: Anything of value owned, seen from the balance sheet; it is a financial category rather than a legal relation.
entries.definitionCN: 所拥有的任何有价值之物，从资产负债表的角度看；它是一个财务类别，而不是法律关系。

entries.definition: A large area of land with a house, or the total property a person leaves at death; it is narrower than the entry word.
entries.definitionCN: 带有宅邸的大片土地，或某人去世时留下的全部财产；它比本词窄。

entries.definition: A characteristic regarded as belonging to a person or thing; it covers the quality sense of the entry word but never the ownership sense.
entries.definitionCN: 被认为属于某人或某物的特征；它覆盖本词的性质义，却从不覆盖所有权义。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the Latin adjective for 'one's own', real derived words and real legal phrases, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：拉丁语中表示「自己的」形容词、真实派生词与真实法律用语，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Everything starts from the question 'whose is it', which is what 'one's own' answers.
normal.cn: 一切都从「这是谁的」这个问题开始，而「自己的」正是它的答案。

normal.en: The family runs proper, propriety, proprietor, proprietary and proprietorship.
normal.cn: 同族词包括恰当的、得体、所有人、专有的与所有权。

normal.en: The same word covers the object and the right over it, so lawyers speak of property in property.
normal.cn: 同一个词既覆盖物，也覆盖对物的权利，因此法学家会说对财产享有财产权。

normal.en: Land is the clearest property because it cannot be carried away.
normal.cn: 土地是最清楚的财产，因为它搬不走。

normal.en: The theatre shortened the word to props, and the stage sense is still alive.
normal.cn: 剧院把这个词缩短为「道具」，舞台义至今仍活在使用中。

abstract.en: Picture a stone at the edge of a field with a name cut into it, and a chair, a cup and a coat laid beside it.
abstract.cn: 想象田野边缘一块刻着名字的石头，旁边摆着一把椅子、一只杯子和一件外套。

abstract.en: Picture a transparent box around an idea, marked with the same seal as the house.
abstract.cn: 想象一个透明的盒子罩住一个想法，盒上盖着与房屋相同的印章。

abstract.en: Picture a substance whose label reads not 'mine' but 'this is what I am like'.
abstract.cn: 想象一种物质的标签上写的不是「我的」，而是「我本来就是这样」。

examples.en: The firm owns property in three cities.
examples.cn: 这家公司在三座城市拥有房产。

examples.en: Hardness is a property that the alloy keeps at high temperature.
examples.cn: 硬度是这种合金在高温下仍保持的一种性质。

examples.en: The lease set out who was responsible for repairs to the property.
examples.cn: 租约列明了谁负责该房产的修缮。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「破坡地」——坡上那块地也是家产；再记住同一词还能指物之本性，就像地有坡、铁有硬。

root: 拉丁语 proprius「自己的、特有的」→ proprietas「所有权、性质」→ 经古法语 proprete 进入英语。proprius 的更深来源不确定，出自「为个体所有」短语的说法属假说；同根词包括 proper、propriety、proprietor。

sensesIntro.en: Eight readings grow from what answers 'whose is it'. The owned things come first, with land and buildings as the clearest case; then the right of ownership itself, which can attach even to untouchable things; then the quality that belongs to a thing, at home in science and logic; and finally the stage objects and the older landed estate.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都从「这是谁的」这一答案长出。先是被拥有的东西，其中土地与房屋最清楚；其次是对物享有所有权的权利，它甚至可以附着在摸不到的东西上；再其次是某物固有的性质，在科学与逻辑中安家；最后是舞台道具与较早的地产庄园义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a boundary stone with a name on it, and the things inside the line that answer to that name.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块刻着名字的地界石，以及界线之内属于这个名字的一切。

branches.en: THINGS: belongings in general, and the objects a theatre company owns for a production.
branches.cn: 物：一般意义上的财物，以及剧团为某场演出所拥有的物件。

branches.en: LAND: the immovable core, houses and plots that cannot be carried off.
branches.cn: 土地：不可移动的内核，搬不走的房屋与地块。

branches.en: THE RIGHT: ownership as a legal power, extending to intangibles such as songs and marks.
branches.cn: 权利：作为法律权力的所有权，可延伸到歌曲与标记等无形之物。

branches.en: QUALITY: what belongs to a thing's nature, in the laboratory and in logic.
branches.cn: 性质：属于某物本性的东西，在实验室里也在逻辑中。

branches.en: ESTATE: the older landed domain, inherited rather than traded.
branches.cn: 庄园：较早的领地，承袭而来而非买卖所得。

intro.en: One Latin adjective for 'one's own' supplies the whole family, with noun and agent endings added; the sense splits between what is owned and what a thing is like.
intro.cn: 一个表示「自己的」的拉丁形容词提供了整个家族，随后加上名词与施事后缀；语义在「被拥有之物」与「某物像什么」之间分开。

latinIntro.en: The Latin forms below show the adjective, its abstract noun and the neuter form used as a noun.
latinIntro.cn: 下列拉丁形式展示了这个形容词、它的抽象名词，以及作名词用的中性形式。

items.example: The property passed to the eldest child.
items.exampleCN: 这份财产传给了长子。

items.example: The two properties share a fence.
items.exampleCN: 这两处房产共用一道篱笆。

items.example: That is the proper way to fold the cloth.
items.exampleCN: 那才是折这块布的正确方法。

items.example: The machine must be properly sealed.
items.exampleCN: 这台机器必须妥善密封。

items.example: The guests observed the proprieties of the house.
items.exampleCN: 客人们遵守这户人家的礼节。

items.meaning: the owner of a business or estate
items.example: The proprietor greeted us at the door.
items.exampleCN: 业主在门口迎接我们。

items.example: The software is proprietary and cannot be copied.
items.exampleCN: 该软件为专有软件，不得复制。

items.example: The business is under sole proprietorship.
items.exampleCN: 这家企业属独资所有。

items.meaning: to take as one's own; suitable
items.example: The council appropriated funds for the bridge.
items.exampleCN: 议会拨出款项用于这座桥。

latinEntries.meaning: a thing of one's own; a characteristic

derivatives.zh: 所有人；业主（表示「自己的」词根加表施事的名词后缀，指对某物享有所有权的人）
专有的；所有权的（名词加形容词后缀，指由某一所有人独占或与其所有权相关）
所有权；业主身份（名词加表身份或状态的名词后缀，指作为所有人的地位）
恰当的；本身的（由拉丁语中表示「自己的」形容词经法语传入，语义由「属于自己的」转为「合乎其本性的」）

definition_zh: 有法律责任的；负有义务的；易于遭受的；很可能发生的
definition_en: legally responsible for something, or likely to do or suffer something
core_image: 一根绳子把签了名的契约系在一只脚踝上，另一头连着一块写着「赔偿」的木牌
scene: 保险公司在条款中写明，运输途中货物受损时由承运人承担赔偿。 The policy states that the carrier is liable for damage to the goods while they are in transit.
sceneCN: 这里指「依法对某项损害承担赔偿」，对应第 1 个义项：因契约或法律而被绑定、必须负责；句意为条款规定运输途中货物受损由承运人负责。画面要点：签名的契约、系在脚踝上的绳、写着「赔偿」的木牌。

pos.zh: 有法律责任的；负有义务的；易于…的；很可能…的（多作表语，后接表示对象或方向的介词）

derivatives.zh: 责任；债务（形容词加表性质的名词后缀，由「可被约束的」转为「须承担的法律责任」）
各项债务（名词加复数词尾，指账面上须偿付的多项义务）
有限责任（形容词与名词构成的复合术语，指以出资额为限的责任形式）

senses.title: Legally answerable for damage
senses.titleCN: 对损害依法负有赔偿责任
senses.definition: bound by law or contract to pay for loss or injury one has caused
senses.definitionCN: 依法或依契约必须为自己造成的损失或伤害作出赔偿
senses.example: The policy states that the carrier is liable for damage to the goods while they are in transit.
senses.exampleCN: 条款规定，运输途中货物受损由承运人负责赔偿。
senses.why: The word began as 'able to be bound', and a contract is exactly the rope that binds a party to answer for a loss.
senses.whyCN: 这个词起初意为「可被绑住的」，而契约正是那根把一方绑住、使其对损失负责的绳子。

senses.title: Answerable for a debt
senses.definition: obliged to settle a debt or to perform an undertaking, often because one has guaranteed it
senses.definitionCN: 必须清偿债务或履行承诺，常因本人曾为之作保
senses.example: A guarantor is liable for the loan if the borrower defaults.
senses.exampleCN: 借款人违约时，担保人对该笔贷款负有责任。
senses.why: Money makes the bond visible: the rope now runs to a specific sum that must be paid.
senses.whyCN: 金钱让这根绳子看得见：它现在连着一个必须偿付的具体数额。

senses.title: Subject to a penalty or a charge
senses.definition: exposed by law to a fine, a tax or some other imposed charge
senses.definitionCN: 依法可能被课以罚款、税款或其他征收
senses.example: Income above that threshold is liable to tax.
senses.exampleCN: 超过该门槛的收入应纳税。
senses.why: The bond can run toward an authority rather than a victim, so the same word covers what the state may exact.
senses.whyCN: 这根绳子也可以通向权力机关而不是受害者，因此同一个词也覆盖国家可以征收的部分。

senses.title: Exposed to harm
senses.definition: open to a particular risk, such as injury, loss or damage, because of circumstances
senses.definitionCN: 因所处情况而暴露于某种风险，如受伤、损失或损坏
senses.example: Low-lying fields are liable to flooding in spring.
senses.exampleCN: 低洼的田地在春天容易遭水淹。
senses.why: From 'bound to answer' the word loosens into 'open to', a shift from a legal tie to a physical exposure.
senses.whyCN: 从「必须负责」松弛为「暴露于」，这是从法律束缚向身体处境的转移。

senses.title: Likely to happen
senses.definition: probable, especially of something unwelcome that may occur
senses.definitionCN: 很可能发生，尤指可能发生的不快之事
senses.example: The bridge is liable to close when the wind rises.
senses.exampleCN: 风一大，这座桥就可能关闭。
senses.why: If a thing is exposed to a risk, it will often meet it, so exposure slides into probability.
senses.whyCN: 如果一物暴露于某种风险，它往往会遇上，于是「暴露」滑向「概率」。

senses.title: Prone to do something
senses.definition: having a tendency to act in a certain way, often unintentionally or regrettably
senses.definitionCN: 有以某种方式行事的倾向，常指无意或令人遗憾的行为
senses.example: He is liable to forget names under pressure.
senses.exampleCN: 他在压力之下容易忘记名字。
senses.why: A person can be bound to an outcome by his own habits, so the word moves from outer obligation to inner tendency.
senses.whyCN: 人可能被自己的习惯绑向某个结果，因此这个词从外在义务移向内在倾向。

senses.title: Obliged to serve
senses.titleCN: 有义务服役或尽某项义务
senses.definition: required by law to perform a service, such as military duty or statutory work
senses.definitionCN: 依法须履行某项服务，如兵役或法定工作
senses.example: All men of that age were liable for military service.
senses.exampleCN: 那个年龄的所有男子都有服兵役的义务。
senses.why: The bond here is to the state and to a duty rather than to a creditor, but the grammar of being bound is unchanged.
senses.whyCN: 这里的绳子通向国家与一项义务，而不是通向债权人，但「被绑住」的语法没有变。

senses.title: Mildly probable in speech
senses.definition: used informally to mean that something may well happen, with less force than a prediction
senses.definitionCN: 口语中表示某事很可能发生，语气比预测更弱
senses.example: She is liable to be late if the traffic is bad.
senses.exampleCN: 如果交通不好，她可能会迟到。
senses.why: In everyday speech the legal weight drains away, leaving only a softened forecast that keeps a trace of the old 'bound to happen'.
senses.whyCN: 在日常口语中，法律分量被抽走，只剩一个软化的预测，仍留着「注定会发生」的一丝痕迹。

intro.en: Liable comes from Old French lier 'to bind', from Latin ligare, with the adjective ending -able. It first meant 'able to be bound', then 'bound by law to answer', and later widened to exposure and probability.
intro.cn: liable 出自古法语 lier「捆绑」，源头为拉丁语 ligare，加上形容词后缀 -able。它最初意为「可被绑住的」，继而指「依法须负责的」，后扩展到「暴露于」与「很可能」。

items.en: Ligare 'to bind' is the verb behind the word; the same root also produced alliance, obligation and ligament.
items.cn: ligare 意为「捆绑」，是这个词背后的动词；同一词根还产生了「联盟」「义务」与「韧带」。

items.en: Old French lier carried the verb into English, and its participle gave the sense of something or someone bound.
items.cn: 古法语 lier 把这个动词带入英语，其分词给出「被绑住的」这一意思。

items.en: The adjective formed with the ending for 'able' meant 'able to be bound', at first in the sense of being bound by law to answer for something.
items.cn: 加上表示「可…的」后缀构成的形容词，意为「可被绑住的」，最初指依法须对某事负责。

items.en: In medieval and early modern law the word described a person bound to pay or to answer, and fixed phrases named the object of the bond.
items.cn: 在中世纪与近代早期的法律中，这个词描述被绑定须付款或须作答的人，固定搭配则指明被绑向的对象。

items.en: The widening from 'bound to answer' to 'exposed to' and then to 'likely to' happened gradually, and the first date of the looser use is uncertain.
items.cn: 从「必须负责」扩展到「暴露于」再到「很可能」，这一过程是渐进的，较松弛用法首见的年代不确定。

note.en: The first group contains words that look or sound close but come from other sources or carry other senses; the second group gives near alternatives for responsibility and for proneness.
note.cn: 第一组是形音相近但来源不同或另有含义的词；第二组是「责任」与「易于」两个方向的近义替代。

entries.definition: A published false statement that damages a reputation; it comes from a Latin word for a small book, not from the verb to bind.
entries.definitionCN: 公开发表、损害名誉的不实陈述；它出自拉丁语中表示小册子的词，与「捆绑」无关。

entries.definition: Able to be trusted; it is formed from the verb rely plus the same ending, and has nothing to do with legal responsibility.
entries.definitionCN: 可信赖的；它由动词「依赖」加同一个后缀构成，与法律责任无关。

entries.definition: Unstable or easily changed, used in chemistry and psychology; its Latin source means 'sliding', not 'binding'.
entries.definitionCN: 不稳定、易变的，用于化学与心理学；它的拉丁来源意为「滑动」，而不是「捆绑」。

entries.definition: Having a duty to deal with something and being answerable for it; it is wider than the entry word and need not be legal.
entries.definitionCN: 有义务处理某事并须为之负责；它比本词宽，而且不必是法律上的。

entries.definition: Required to explain or justify one's actions to a person or body; it stresses reporting upward rather than paying for loss.
entries.definitionCN: 须向某人或机构解释、交代自己的行为；它强调向上报告，而不是赔偿损失。

entries.definition: Likely to suffer from or to do something, usually something bad; it covers the exposure sense but carries no legal duty.
entries.definitionCN: 易遭受或易做出某事，通常是不好的事；它覆盖「暴露」这一义，却不带法律义务。

entries.definition: Likely to do something, often in a neutral or habitual way; it lacks the sense of risk that the entry word usually carries.
entries.definitionCN: 有做某事的倾向，常为中性的或习惯性的；它缺少本词通常带的「风险」意味。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the Latin verb to bind, the adjective ending for 'able', real derived words and real legal phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：拉丁语中表示「捆绑」的动词、表示「可…的」形容词后缀、真实派生词与真实法律用语。

normal.en: The core is a rope: liable means able to be bound, and a contract is the rope.
normal.cn: 核心是一根绳子：本词意为「可被绑住的」，而契约就是那根绳。

normal.en: The family runs liability, liabilities and limited liability.
normal.cn: 同族词包括责任、各项债务与有限责任。

normal.en: The preposition sorts the senses: liable for a loss, liable to a penalty or a flood.
normal.cn: 介词把义项分开：对损失负责，应受处罚或易遭水淹。

normal.en: The same root appears in alliance, obligation and ligament, all forms of binding.
normal.cn: 同一词根出现在联盟、义务与韧带中，都是不同形式的「绑」。

normal.en: In speech the legal rope goes slack, and liable becomes a soft way of saying likely.
normal.cn: 在口语中法律之绳松脱，这个词变成「很可能」的软说法。

abstract.en: Picture a signed paper tied to an ankle, so that wherever the person walks the obligation follows.
abstract.cn: 想象一张签了名的纸系在脚踝上，人走到哪里，义务就跟到哪里。

abstract.en: Picture a field lying low beside a river, exposed each spring without anyone having agreed to it.
abstract.cn: 想象河边的低洼田地，每年春天都被淹，而没有任何人同意过这件事。

abstract.en: Picture a rope that slowly turns into a probability, still tied but no longer pulled by a court.
abstract.cn: 想象一根绳子慢慢变成一种概率，仍然系着，却不再被法庭拉动。

examples.en: The manufacturer is liable for defects found within two years.
examples.cn: 制造商对两年内发现的缺陷负有责任。

examples.en: Drivers are liable to heavy fines for using a phone at the wheel.
examples.cn: 司机开车时使用电话可能被重罚。

examples.en: The old roof is liable to leak after a long storm.
examples.cn: 旧屋顶在长时间暴雨之后容易漏水。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「赖不了的」——签了字就得赔，绳子系在脚上，赖也赖不掉，所以是有责任的。

root: 古法语 lier「捆绑」← 拉丁语 ligare「捆绑」→ 加表示「可…的」后缀构成 liable，字面为「可被绑住的」。ligare 的更深来源一般认为是印欧语中表示「系、缠」的词根，相关形式属重构形式；同根词包括 alliance、obligation、ligament。

sensesIntro.en: Eight readings unwind from one rope. Bound by a contract gives legal responsibility and debts; bound toward an authority gives penalties, taxes and service; loosening the rope gives exposure to harm, then likelihood and personal tendency; and in casual speech the rope nearly disappears, leaving only a soft forecast.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从同一根绳子解开。被契约绑住，产生法律责任与债务；被绑向权力机关，产生处罚、税款与服役义务；绳子一松，产生暴露于损害、可能性与个人倾向；到了口语里绳子几乎消失，只剩一个软化的预测。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a signed obligation tied to the ankle, following the person wherever he goes.
core.cn: 核心意象：系在脚踝上的签名义务，人走到哪里它就跟到哪里。

branches.en: BOUND: legal answerability for damage, and the duty to settle a debt.
branches.cn: 被绑住：对损害的依法负责，以及清偿债务的义务。

branches.en: OWED TO AUTHORITY: penalties and taxes on one side, service to the state on the other.
branches.cn: 欠向权力：一边是处罚与税款，一边是对国家的服役义务。

branches.en: EXPOSED: open to injury, loss or damage because of where one stands.
branches.cn: 暴露：因所处位置而易于受伤、受损或遭损失。

branches.en: LIKELY AND PRONE: what probably happens, and what a person tends to do.
branches.cn: 可能与倾向：很可能发生的事，以及一个人容易做出的举动。

branches.en: LOOSE FORECAST: the everyday weakening of the word into a mild 'may well'.
branches.cn: 松脱的预测：日常用法中弱化为轻微的「很可能」。

intro.en: One Latin verb for binding underlies the word and a large neighbouring family; the adjective ending adds the idea of capacity, and later endings build nouns and verbs for obligations.
intro.cn: 一个表示「捆绑」的拉丁动词支撑着这个词与一大片相邻词族；形容词后缀加上「能力」之意，后来的后缀又构成表示义务的名词与动词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin forms below show the verb of binding and its compounds; the English words built on them keep the same physical image of a tie.
latinIntro.cn: 下列拉丁形式展示表示「捆绑」的动词及其复合形式；由它们构成的英语词都保留同一种「系绑」的实体意象。

items.meaning: able to be bound, hence answerable
items.meaningCN: 可被绑住的，因而须负责的
items.example: The carrier is liable for the loss.
items.exampleCN: 承运人对该损失负有责任。

items.example: The firm accepted liability for the accident.
items.exampleCN: 公司承认对该事故负有责任。

items.meaning: debts shown on a balance sheet
items.meaningCN: 资产负债表上列出的各项债务
items.example: The company's liabilities exceeded its assets.
items.exampleCN: 公司的债务超过了资产。

items.example: The two states allied against the fleet.
items.exampleCN: 两国结盟对抗那支舰队。

items.meaningCN: 依协议形成的正式联合
items.example: The alliance held through the winter.
items.exampleCN: 这个联盟维持了整个冬天。

items.meaning: to bind someone by duty or favour
items.meaningCN: 以义务或恩惠约束某人
items.example: The contract obliges the seller to deliver.
items.exampleCN: 合同使卖方负有交付义务。

items.meaning: a duty one is bound to perform
items.example: The lease sets out the tenant's obligations.
items.exampleCN: 租约列明了租户的义务。

items.meaning: a band that binds bones together
items.meaningCN: 把骨骼系连起来的韧带
items.example: The runner tore a ligament in his knee.
items.exampleCN: 跑者撕裂了膝部的一条韧带。

items.meaning: a tie or band, also joined letters
items.example: The surgeon applied a ligature to the vessel.
items.exampleCN: 外科医生用系带结扎了那条血管。

latinEntries.meaning: to bind, to put under obligation

derivatives.zh: 责任；债务（形容词加表性质的名词后缀，由「可被约束的」转为「须承担的法律责任」）
各项债务（名词加复数词尾，指账面上须偿付的多项义务）
义务（由同根的「使受约束」动词加表行为的名词后缀构成，指必须履行的事）
联盟（由同根的「系到一处」动词加表行为的名词后缀构成，指依协议形成的联合）

definition_zh: 候鸟迁徙路线；季节性往返的路径；由停歇地串成的路线；人类迁徙路径；动物廊道与鱼类洄游路线；引申的既定航线
definition_en: the path followed by animals, people, aircraft or data when they move from one region or system to another, especially the seasonal path of migratory species
core_image: 一张铺在大陆上的虚线，从北方的繁殖地出发，绕过山脉，一连串小点串起湖泊与河口，最后落到南方的越冬地
scene: 湿地保护站里，研究者把一枚轻巧的定位器系在大雁背上，屏幕上随即出现一条跨越大陆的虚线。 Researchers fitted the geese with trackers to map the migration route they follow each autumn.
sceneCN: 这里 migration route 是「候鸟迁徙路线」（第 1 个义项：迁飞通道，即候鸟世代沿用的空中走廊）；句意为研究者给大雁装上追踪器，以绘制它们每年秋天沿用的迁徙路线。

pos.zh: 迁徙路线（多词短语，可数，复数 migration routes；作主语、宾语或介词宾语）

derivatives.zh: 迁徙；洄游；迁移
迁徙；移居
迁徙的；有迁居习惯的
路线；航线
改变路线；改道

senses.title: A Flyway for Migratory Birds
senses.definition: the broad corridor that migratory birds follow between breeding and wintering grounds
senses.definitionCN: 候鸟在繁殖地与越冬地之间循行的宽阔空中走廊
senses.example: The East Asian flyway is a migration route used by millions of waterbirds.
senses.exampleCN: 东亚迁飞通道是一条被数以百万计水鸟使用的迁徙路线。
senses.why: migration is the seasonal move and route is the line laid down for it, so the phrase names the corridor as a piece of geography.
senses.whyCN: migration 是季节性的移动，route 是为它铺下的线，这个短语因此把这条走廊当作一处地理事物来命名。

senses.title: The Specific Seasonal Path
senses.titleCN: 季节性往返的具体路径
senses.definition: the particular track a population takes in one season and reverses in the next
senses.definitionCN: 某一族群在一个季节走、下一季再反向走回的那条具体路径
senses.example: Satellite tags showed a migration route that turns north only in spring.
senses.exampleCN: 卫星标记显示出一条只在春季才折向北行的迁徙路线。
senses.why: the same line serves two journeys in opposite directions, so route stresses the fixed track rather than the movement.
senses.whyCN: 同一条线要服务两次方向相反的旅程，route 因此强调的是固定轨道，而不是移动本身。

senses.title: A Chain of Stopover Sites
senses.definition: the sequence of feeding and resting sites that together make the journey possible
senses.definitionCN: 由取食地与休息地依次串起、使整段旅程得以完成的序列
senses.example: Each wetland along the migration route is a link the birds cannot skip.
senses.exampleCN: 迁徙路线上的每一片湿地都是鸟群不能跳过的一环。
senses.why: a long flight is impossible without fuel stops, so the route is understood as a chain of places rather than a line on a map.
senses.whyCN: 长途飞行没有补给点就无从完成，于是这条路线被理解成一串地点，而不是地图上的一根线。

senses.title: The Path of Human Peoples
senses.titleCN: 人类迁徙路径（历史与人口学）
senses.definition: the corridor along which a human population spread from one region to another
senses.definitionCN: 某个人群从一地区扩散到另一地区时所经的走廊
senses.example: Linguists and geneticists traced the same migration route across the steppe.
senses.exampleCN: 语言学家与遗传学家在草原上追溯出同一条人类迁徙路径。
senses.why: people move the way birds do, only once, so the phrase transfers cleanly from season to prehistory.
senses.whyCN: 人像鸟一样移动，只是不再回头，这个短语于是从季节平移到了史前。

senses.title: A Wildlife Corridor
senses.definition: a strip of habitat that lets animals move between larger patches of suitable land
senses.definitionCN: 让动物在较大片适宜栖息地之间移动的一条带状生境
senses.example: The reserve protects a migration route for elk between summer and winter range.
senses.exampleCN: 保护区保护着一条麋鹿在夏季与冬季牧场之间往返的迁徙廊道。
senses.why: route here is a planning term: what matters is connectivity, not a single species or season.
senses.whyCN: 这里的 route 是规划术语：重要的是连通性，而不是某一个物种或某一个季节。

senses.title: The Course of Fish Migration
senses.definition: the path fish follow between spawning, feeding and overwintering waters
senses.definitionCN: 鱼类在产卵、索饵与越冬水域之间循行的路径
senses.example: Dams cut the migration route of salmon returning to their natal stream.
senses.exampleCN: 水坝截断了鲑鱼返回出生溪流的洄游路线。
senses.why: fish migrate in water as birds do in air, and English reuses the same phrase rather than coining a separate one.
senses.whyCN: 鱼在水里迁徙，正如鸟在空中迁徙，英语沿用同一短语，而不另造新词。

senses.title: An Established Air or Sea Lane
senses.titleCN: 既定航线（航空、航运引申）
senses.definition: a fixed air or sea lane assigned to regular traffic
senses.definitionCN: 分配给定期交通的固定空中或海上航道
senses.example: The airline shifted its migration route for the season to avoid storms.
senses.exampleCN: 这家航空公司为避开风暴而调整了当季的既定航线。
senses.why: once aircraft and ships move on schedules, they too follow set lines, and the phrase extends from birds to traffic.
senses.whyCN: 飞机与船只一旦按班期移动，也走固定的线，短语就从鸟群延伸到交通。

senses.title: The Path Data Takes in a Move
senses.titleCN: 数据迁移路径（信息技术引申）
senses.definition: the sequence of systems and transfers through which data moves during a platform change
senses.definitionCN: 平台更换期间数据所经的系统与转接序列
senses.example: The team documented every hop on the migration route from the old server.
senses.exampleCN: 团队记录了从旧服务器迁出时数据路径上的每一跳。
senses.why: data is imagined as a population leaving one home for another, so the same phrase covers a technical move.
senses.whyCN: 数据被想象成一群离开旧居、迁往新居的生物，同一个短语因此也覆盖技术层面的搬迁。

intro.en: Migration route joins two words of entirely different descent. Migration is Latin, from migratio and the verb migrare 'to move, change abode'. Route is French, from Old French rute, from Latin rupta (via) 'a broken-open way', built on rumpere 'to break'. The two halves share no root.
intro.cn: migration route 由两个来源完全不同的词拼成。migration 属拉丁系，来自 migratio 与动词 migrare「迁移、迁居」；route 属法语系，来自古法语 rute，更早是拉丁 rupta (via)「破开的路」，由 rumpere「破开」构成。两半不同源。

items.en: Migrare meant 'to move from one place to settle in another'; its own earlier origin is uncertain, with no settled Indo-European root.
items.cn: migrare 意为「从一处迁走、到另一处定居」；它自身更早的来源不确定，没有公认的印欧词根。

items.en: Migratio is the third-declension noun of that verb, naming the act of moving or a change of residence.
items.cn: migratio 是该动词的第三变格法名词，指迁移这一动作或住所的更换。

items.en: Rumpere meant 'to break, burst open'; its past participle ruptum supplies the element seen in rupture and interrupt.
items.cn: rumpere 意为「破开、冲破」；其过去分词 ruptum 提供了 rupture 与 interrupt 中可见的那个成分。

items.en: Rupta (via) meant a way cut or broken open through terrain, and it passed into everyday speech for any opened road.
items.cn: rupta (via) 指在地形中破开、开辟出来的一条路，后来泛指任何已开通的道路。

items.en: Old French shortened the Latin phrase to rute 'road, way', which English borrowed as route.
items.cn: 古法语把这一拉丁短语缩短为 rute「道路、路程」，英语借入后写作 route。

items.en: The compound migration route is modern English, formed once migration had become a technical term in zoology; the exact first date is uncertain.
items.cn: 复合词 migration route 属近代英语，是在 migration 成为动物学术语之后才组成的；确切首见年代不确定。

note.en: Group one separates the phrase from words that look close but stand in different relations to it; group two gives the specialist and general words that overlap with one sense or another.
note.cn: 第一组把这个短语与外形接近、但关系各不相同的词区分开；第二组给出在某个义项上与之重叠的专业词与一般词。

entries.definition: The single noun for the movement itself, without any route attached; it names the journey, not the line it follows.
entries.definitionCN: 单指出移动本身的那个名词，不含路线；它命名旅程，而不是旅程所循的线。

entries.definition: In- 'into' plus migrare: movement into a country, seen from the receiving side; the root is shared, the direction is not.
entries.definitionCN: in-「进入」加 migrare：从接收一方看的入境移居；词根相同，方向不同。

entries.definition: From Latin ratio 'reckoning', which has nothing to do with migrare; the resemblance is only in the ending, so the two are not kin.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 ratio「计算」，与 migrare 无关；相似只在词尾，二者并非同源。

entries.definition: French routine descends from route 'road', so it is kin to the second half of the phrase, not to migration.
entries.definitionCN: 法语 routine 源自 route「道路」，因此与短语的后半同源，而与 migration 无关。

entries.definition: The standard term for a bird migration route, usually a broad corridor; narrower and more technical than the phrase.
entries.definitionCN: 指鸟类迁徙路线的标准术语，通常是宽阔的走廊；比该短语更窄、更专业。

entries.definition: A strip of habitat linking two patches; it names the land itself, while migration route names the movement it serves.
entries.definitionCN: 指连接两片栖息地的带状地带；它命名土地本身，而 migration route 命名它所服务的移动。

entries.definition: A planned sequence of stops for a traveller; it is written for people, not inherited by animals.
entries.definitionCN: 指为旅行者事先排定的停留顺序；它是为人类书写的，而不是动物世代沿用的。

entries.definition: The act of going through or across; it stresses the crossing rather than the fixed line followed.
entries.definitionCN: 指穿过或横越的动作；强调穿越本身，而非所循的固定路线。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the two Latin and French halves, the real technical term flyway, and the real places that make a route work.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：拉丁与法语的两半、真实术语 flyway，以及真正让一条路线成立的那些地点。

normal.en: migrare 'to move' gives migration; rupta via 'a broken-open way' gives route: two roots, one phrase.
normal.cn: migrare「迁移」给出 migration；rupta via「破开的路」给出 route：两个词根，一个短语。

normal.en: Rupture and interrupt carry the same rupt- element as route, which is why route has nothing to do with migration's root.
normal.cn: rupture 与 interrupt 与 route 共用同一个 rupt- 成分，这正是 route 与 migration 词根无关的原因。

normal.en: Ornithologists say flyway for the same thing; the phrase is the plain-language version.
normal.cn: 鸟类学家把同一事物称作 flyway；这个短语是它的通俗说法。

normal.en: A route is only real if the stopover wetlands are still there, which is why conservation works site by site.
normal.cn: 只有中途湿地还在，路线才真正成立，所以保护工作要一处一处地做。

normal.en: The family runs migrate, migration, migratory, route, reroute.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 migrate、migration、migratory、route、reroute。

abstract.en: Picture a dotted line laid over a continent, each dot a lake where the flock rests.
abstract.cn: 想象一条铺在大陆上的虚线，每个点都是鸟群歇脚的湖泊。

abstract.en: Picture an old road cut through a mountain pass, opened by breaking the rock.
abstract.cn: 想象一条穿过山口的老路，是靠破开岩石才开通的。

abstract.en: Picture two arrows on the same line, one pointing south in autumn and one north in spring.
abstract.cn: 想象同一条线上的两支箭头，一支秋天指南，一支春天指北。

examples.en: The delta lies on a major migration route for shorebirds.
examples.cn: 这片三角洲位于水鸟的一条主要迁徙路线上。

examples.en: Historians disagree about the migration route taken into the valley.
examples.cn: 历史学家对进入该谷地所走的迁徙路径仍有分歧。

examples.en: Engineers mapped a migration route for the records before shutting the old system down.
examples.cn: 工程师在关停旧系统之前，为这些记录规划了一条迁移路径。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「迈格雷申 如特」——迈开步子（migra）沿着一条开出来的路（route）走 → 迁徙路线。

root: migration 来自拉丁 migratio，源自动词 migrare「迁移、迁居」，migrare 更早来源不确定；route 来自古法语 rute，源自拉丁 rupta (via)「破开的路」，出自 rumpere「破开」。两半不同源：migration 属 migrare 词族，route 属 rumpere 词族。

sensesIntro.en: The eight senses all describe one line between two places. Birds make it seasonal, stopovers make it a chain, people make it historical, corridors make it a planning unit, fish make it watery, aircraft make it scheduled, and data makes it digital.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项描述的都是两地之间的一条线。鸟把它变成季节性的，停歇地把它变成一串，人把它变成历史的，廊道把它变成规划单位，鱼把它带进水里，飞机把它变成班期，数据把它变成数字的。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a dotted line between a home and a far place, with resting points along it.
core.cn: 核心意象：家园与远方之间的一条虚线，线上分布着歇脚的点。

branches.en: THE CORRIDOR: a broad flyway, and the exact track a population reverses each season.
branches.cn: 走廊：一条宽阔的迁飞通道，以及某族群每季反向行走的确切轨迹。

branches.en: THE CHAIN: the route is only as good as the wetlands strung along it.
branches.cn: 链条：路线的好坏取决于串在它上面的湿地。

branches.en: LAND AND PEOPLE: the same line read as prehistory or as conservation planning.
branches.cn: 土地与人：同一条线，可读作史前史，也可读作保护规划。

branches.en: WATER: fish follow the same shape under the surface.
branches.cn: 水中：鱼在水面之下循着同一形状。

branches.en: TRANSFER: scheduled traffic and migrating data both inherit the phrase.
branches.cn: 转移：班期交通与迁移中的数据都继承了这个短语。

intro.en: The phrase splits into four morphemes: a Latin verb of moving, a Latin noun suffix, a French noun for a road, and the Latin participle hidden inside it.
intro.cn: 这个短语可拆成四个语素：一个表「迁移」的拉丁动词、一个拉丁名词后缀、一个表「道路」的法语名词，以及藏在它里面的拉丁分词。

latinIntro.en: Latin migrare yields migratio and English migration; Latin rumpere yields ruptum and ruptura, and the phrase rupta via passed through French into English route.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 migrare 衍生 migratio 与英语 migration；拉丁 rumpere 衍生 ruptum 与 ruptura，而短语 rupta via 经法语进入英语，成为 route。

items.meaning: to move, to change one's abode
items.example: The root supplies the movement before any line is drawn.
items.exampleCN: 词根提供的是画线之前的移动。

items.meaning: the act or process of doing something
items.example: Migration names the act of moving away.
items.exampleCN: migration 指迁离这一动作。

items.meaning: seasonal or permanent movement to a new region
items.meaningCN: 季节性或永久性的迁往新地区
items.example: Migration in birds is usually seasonal.
items.exampleCN: 鸟类的迁徙通常是季节性的。

items.meaning: to move from one region to another
items.meaningCN: 从一地区迁往另一地区
items.example: The geese migrate south before the frost.
items.exampleCN: 大雁在霜降前南迁。

items.example: Migratory species depend on intact stopover sites.
items.exampleCN: 迁徙物种依赖完好的中途停歇地。

items.structure: Old French rute, from Latin rupta (via) (noun, first declension)
items.example: Route names the line, not the moving.
items.exampleCN: route 命名的是线，而不是移动。

items.structure: rumpere, rupi, ruptum (Latin verb, third conjugation)
items.example: A road through wild ground is ground that was broken open.
items.exampleCN: 穿过荒野的路，就是被破开的土地。

items.meaning: the assigning of a path, or the path assigned
items.example: Routing decides which line the traffic takes.
items.exampleCN: 路径选择决定交通走哪一条线。

items.meaning: to send along a different path
items.example: Storms forced controllers to reroute the flight.
items.exampleCN: 风暴迫使管制员为航班改道。

items.meaning: the path followed by a migrating population
items.example: The phrase names a line plus the movement that uses it.
items.exampleCN: 这个短语同时命名一条线与使用它的移动。

latinEntries.meaning: a moving, a change of residence

latinEntries.structure: rupta, ruptae (f., first declension, past participle of rumpere)
latinEntries.meaning: broken open, as in rupta via 'an opened way'
latinEntries.meaningCN: 被破开的（如 rupta via「开出来的路」）

definition_zh: 因果关系；一个事件或变量引起另一个事件或变量的联系
definition_en: a link in which one event or variable brings about another
core_image: 一排多米诺骨牌，第一块倒下时推倒第二块，倒下的方向清楚可见
scene: 研究者发现，气温升高之后冰淇淋销量随之上升，但不敢直接说二者有因果联系。 The study tested whether a causal relationship exists between the two variables.
sceneCN: 这里指一个变量引起另一个变量的联系（第 1 个义项：引起与被引起的联系）；句意为这项研究检验两个变量之间是否存在因果关系。

pos.zh: 因果关系；因果联系

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁语「原因、案件」而来的动词，义为「引起；导致」
加形容词尾，义为「因果的」
加副词尾，义为「在因果上」
加行为名词尾，义为「因果作用；引起」
加形容词尾，义为「使然的；致因的」
由拉丁语「带回」而来的名词，义为「关系」
由「关系」加表示状态的名词尾构成，义为「联系；关系」

senses.title: One event bringing about another
senses.titleCN: 一个事件引起另一个事件
senses.definition: a link in which the occurrence of one event makes the other happen
senses.definitionCN: 一个事件的发生使另一事件得以发生的联系
senses.example: The court accepted a causal relationship between the leak and the illness.
senses.exampleCN: 法院认可了泄漏与疾病之间的因果关系。
senses.why: Cause is the active side and relationship is the link, so the phrase joins the pushing to the connecting.
senses.whyCN: 「原因」是主动的一面，「关系」是那条连接，这个词组把推与连接在一起。

senses.title: A directional link between variables
senses.titleCN: 变量之间的方向性联系
senses.definition: a connection in which a change in one variable produces a change in another
senses.definitionCN: 一个变量的变化引起另一变量变化的联系
senses.example: The model assumes a causal relationship running from income to health.
senses.exampleCN: 该模型假定存在从收入指向健康的因果关系。
senses.why: Direction is what separates causation from mere association, and the phrase always implies an arrow.
senses.whyCN: 方向正是因果与单纯关联的分界，这个词组总暗含一支箭头。

senses.title: A causal chain
senses.definition: a sequence in which each step brings about the next, so that the first reaches the last through intermediates
senses.definitionCN: 每一步引起下一步、最初一环经中间环节到达最后一环的序列
senses.example: A causal relationship between rainfall and crop failure runs through soil moisture.
senses.exampleCN: 降雨与歉收之间的因果关系经由土壤湿度这一环。
senses.why: Long causes act through middle steps, and the phrase can name the whole chain rather than a single jump.
senses.whyCN: 远因通过中间环节起作用，这个词组可以指整条链，而不只是单次跳跃。

senses.title: A claim tested by experiment
senses.titleCN: 由实验检验的因果主张
senses.definition: a statement that one condition causes another, which an intervention is designed to test
senses.definitionCN: 某条件引起另一条件的主张，并用干预来检验它
senses.example: Random assignment lets the trial test a causal relationship rather than describe one.
senses.exampleCN: 随机分配让试验得以检验因果关系，而不只是描述它。
senses.why: Only an intervention can show that changing the cause changes the effect, which is why experiments exist.
senses.whyCN: 只有干预才能显示改变原因会改变结果，这正是实验存在的理由。

senses.title: A legal causal link
senses.definition: the connection the law requires between an act and a harm before liability attaches
senses.definitionCN: 法律要求在行为与损害之间具备、责任才成立的联系
senses.example: The plaintiff had to prove a causal relationship between the defect and the injury.
senses.exampleCN: 原告必须证明缺陷与伤害之间的因果关系。
senses.why: Law asks whether the harm would have happened but for the act, a narrower test than scientific causation.
senses.whyCN: 法律问的是若没有该行为损害是否仍会发生，这比科学上的因果更窄。

senses.title: A risk factor linked to disease
senses.titleCN: 与疾病相连的风险因素
senses.definition: an association in medicine between an exposure and the later onset of a condition
senses.definitionCN: 医学中暴露因素与后来发病之间的关联
senses.example: Epidemiologists found a causal relationship between smoking and lung cancer.
senses.exampleCN: 流行病学家发现了吸烟与肺癌之间的因果关系。
senses.why: Medicine must act before mechanisms are fully known, so it often states the relationship before the process.
senses.whyCN: 医学必须在机制完全清楚之前行动，因此常先陈述关系，再谈过程。

senses.title: A link inferred from correlation
senses.definition: a causal reading that researchers draw from a strong association, subject to further checks
senses.definitionCN: 研究者从强关联中得出的因果解读，仍待进一步检验
senses.example: A causal relationship was inferred, but only after confounders were controlled.
senses.exampleCN: 因果关系是被推断出来的，而且是在控制混淆因素之后。
senses.why: Correlation suggests, and causal language converts the suggestion into a claim that must then be defended.
senses.whyCN: 相关只提示，因果措辞把提示变成需要辩护的主张。

senses.title: A two-way causal relationship
senses.definition: a link in which each side influences the other over time
senses.definitionCN: 双方随时间相互影响的联系
senses.example: Income and health show a causal relationship in both directions.
senses.exampleCN: 收入与健康呈现出双向的因果关系。
senses.why: Feedback loops are common in social systems, so the arrow sometimes has to be drawn twice.
senses.whyCN: 社会系统中反馈环很常见，所以箭头有时得画两次。

intro.en: Causal relationship joins the Latin word for cause to a Latin word for carrying back. The first half supplies the push, the second the link that carries the push to its result.
intro.cn: 这个词组把拉丁语中表示「原因」的词，与表示「带回」的词接在一起：前一半提供推力，后一半提供把推力带到结果的连接。

items.en: Causa meant cause, reason and also a legal case, since a case is a matter brought before a court.
items.cn: 这个词指原因、理由，也指案件，因为案件是被带到法庭前的事。

items.en: Late Latin formed the adjective for what belongs to a cause, and English causal came from it.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语为「属于原因的」造出形容词，英语的「因果的」由此而来。

items.en: Cause entered through French for both the reason of an event and the matter of a lawsuit.
items.cn: 这个词经法语进入英语，既指事件的原因，也指诉讼案件。

items.en: Ferre meant to carry, and with the prefix meaning back it produced referre, to bring back or relate.
items.cn: 这个词根意为「搬运」，加上表示「回」的前缀后构成「带回、关联」。

items.en: Relatio named a carrying back, hence a report or a connection between things.
items.cn: 这个词指「带回」，因而指报告或事物之间的联系。

items.en: Relation entered in the fourteenth century and relationship followed later; the exact first date of the compound is uncertain.
items.cn: 「关系」在十四世纪进入英语，「联系」随后出现；该复合词确切的最早年代不确定。

note.en: The first group belongs to the cause family or looks close; the second group names associations and links of different force.
note.cn: 第一组属于「原因」同族或形近；第二组指力度不同的关联与连接。

entries.definition: The event or condition that produces an effect.
entries.definitionCN: 指产生结果的事件或条件。

entries.definition: Relating to cause and effect.
entries.definitionCN: 指与因果有关的。

entries.definition: In terms of cause and effect.
entries.definitionCN: 指就因果关系而言。

entries.definition: The act or process of causing.
entries.definitionCN: 指引起的行为或过程。

entries.definition: Producing an effect, often used in grammar.
entries.definitionCN: 指致因的，常用于语法。

entries.definition: Relaxed or accidental; its root is falling, not causing.
entries.definitionCN: 指随意或偶然的；词根是「落下」，与致因无关。

entries.definition: A statistical association without a claim about direction or cause.
entries.definitionCN: 指统计上的关联，不主张方向或原因。

entries.definition: Any observed connection, weaker than a causal claim.
entries.definitionCN: 指任何观察到的连接，比因果主张弱。

entries.definition: The process through which the cause acts, which explains the relationship.
entries.definitionCN: 指原因起作用的过程，它解释这种关系。

entries.definition: The outcome produced by a cause.
entries.definitionCN: 指原因产生的结果。

entries.definition: A relation in which one thing relies on another, not necessarily causal.
entries.definitionCN: 指一物依赖另一物的关系，未必是因果。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the falling dominoes, the arrow of direction and the legal but-for test.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用倒下的多米诺、方向箭头与法律上的「若没有」检验。

normal.en: Causal means belonging to a cause, so a causal relationship is the link a cause travels along.
normal.cn: 「因果的」意为属于原因的，所以因果关系就是原因走过的连接。

normal.en: The fixed phrase is «a causal relationship between» two variables.
normal.cn: 固定说法是「两个变量之间的因果关系」。

normal.en: Dominoes are the clearest picture: each fall is both an effect and the next cause.
normal.cn: 多米诺是最清楚的画面：每一次倒下既是结果，也是下一次的原因。

normal.en: Law tests it with «but for»: would the harm have happened without the act?
normal.cn: 法律用「若没有」检验：没有该行为，损害还会发生吗？

normal.en: Correlation is an observation; causal relationship is a claim about direction.
normal.cn: 相关是观察，因果关系是关于方向的主张。

abstract.en: A causal relationship is a river with a direction; correlation is only a map of wet ground.
abstract.cn: 因果关系是有方向的河流，相关只是湿地的一张图。

abstract.en: Cause and effect can trade places over time, and then the phrase must be drawn with two arrows.
abstract.cn: 原因与结果会随时间互换位置，此时这个词组得画上两支箭头。

abstract.en: Naming a relationship causal is a promise to explain how the push travels.
abstract.cn: 把一种关系称为因果，就是承诺要解释这股推力如何传递。

examples.en: The data show a strong correlation but do not prove a causal relationship.
examples.cn: 数据显示出强相关，却未证明因果关系。

examples.en: Randomised trials are designed to establish a causal relationship.
examples.cn: 随机试验旨在确立因果关系。

examples.en: Researchers found a causal relationship between sleep and test scores.
examples.cn: 研究者发现睡眠与考试成绩之间存在因果关系。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「原因」是推手，「关系」是连线：推手通过连线把力量送到结果，就是因果关系

root: 「原因」来自拉丁语 causa「原因；案件」；「关系」来自拉丁语 relatio「带回」，其动词 ferre 意为「搬运」。「因果的」为晚期拉丁语形容词，英语十三世纪起用「原因」，十四世纪起用「关系」；复合词确切最早年代不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses run from a single push to a two-way loop: one event causing another, a directional variable link, a causal chain, an experimental claim, a legal link, a medical risk link, a link inferred from correlation, and a reciprocal relationship.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从单次推动延伸到双向回路：一事件引起另一事件、变量间的方向联系、因果链、实验主张、法律联系、医学风险联系、由相关推断的联系、双向关系。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a row of dominoes falls in one direction, each block both struck and striking.
core.cn: 核心意象：一排多米诺朝同一方向倒下，每一块既被撞倒也撞倒下一块。

branches.en: THE PUSH AND THE ARROW: one event making another happen, with a clear direction.
branches.cn: 推力与箭头：一个事件使另一事件发生，方向清楚。

branches.en: THE LONG CHAIN: the cause reaching its effect through intermediate steps.
branches.cn: 长链：原因经中间环节抵达结果。

branches.en: THE TESTED AND INFERRED CLAIM: a relationship tried by intervention or read from association.
branches.cn: 被检验与推断的主张：经干预检验或从关联读出的关系。

branches.en: THE APPLIED LINK: legal liability and medical risk.
branches.cn: 应用中的联系：法律责任与医学风险。

branches.en: THE TWO-WAY LOOP: mutual influence drawn with two arrows.
branches.cn: 双向回路：以两支箭头画出的相互影响。

intro.en: The phrase joins a Latin cause word to a Latin carrying word; direction is supplied by cause, connection by relation.
intro.cn: 这个词组把拉丁语的「原因」与「搬运」接起来：方向由原因提供，连接由关系提供。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplies causa and relatio; the modern compound is English, and its first record is uncertain.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语提供了「原因」与「关系」；现代复合词是英语构词，最早记录不确定。

definition_zh: 可靠性；可信度；可靠程度
definition_en: the quality of being dependable, or the degree to which a measurement, source or system performs consistently
core_image: 同一把尺子反复测量同一块板，刻度每次都落在同一位置
scene: 这里指「可靠性」。 The reliability of the sensor was tested by repeating the same measurement fifty times.
sceneCN: 这里 reliability 指「测量的可靠性」（第 2 个义项：重复测量结果的一致程度）；句意：传感器的可靠性通过重复同一测量五十次来检验。图中可辨识物件：传感器、重复测量曲线、刻度尺、记录表。

pos.zh: 可靠性；可信度；可靠程度（多作不可数，指不同方面时可用复数 reliabilities）

derivatives.zh: 可靠的；可信的
依赖；依靠
可靠地
