senses.title: Dependability of a person
senses.titleCN: 人的可靠：可以指望其说到做到
senses.definition: the quality of a person who can be trusted to do what is promised
senses.definitionCN: 一个人可以被信任履行承诺的品质
senses.example: Her reliability made her the obvious choice to hold the keys.
senses.exampleCN: 她的可靠使她成为保管钥匙的当然人选。
senses.why: The noun is reliable + -ity; reliable comes from rely, which originally meant 'to bind together', so reliability is the quality of being bound to one's word.
senses.whyCN: 该名词是 reliable 加 -ity；reliable 出自 rely，后者原意为「绑在一起」，因此 reliability 是「被绑定于自己承诺」的品质。

senses.title: Consistency of measurement
senses.titleCN: 测量的可靠性：重复得到相同结果
senses.definition: in research, the extent to which repeated measurements give the same result
senses.definitionCN: 研究中重复测量给出相同结果的程度
senses.example: The reliability of the sensor was tested fifty times.
senses.exampleCN: 传感器的可靠性被检验了五十次。
senses.why: Measurement theory separatedaccuracy from stability: a reading may be stable and still wrong, so reliability names only the stability.
senses.whyCN: 测量理论把准确与稳定分开：读数可以稳定却仍然错误，因此 reliability 只命名稳定性。

senses.title: Engineering reliability
senses.titleCN: 工程可靠性：设备在规定条件下不出故障
senses.definition: in engineering, the probability that a component or system performs its function without failure for a stated period
senses.definitionCN: 工程中部件或系统在规定时间内无故障执行功能的概率
senses.example: Engine reliability improved after the redesign of the cooling system.
senses.exampleCN: 冷却系统重新设计后，发动机可靠性提高了。
senses.why: Engineering made the word quantitative: failure rates and test hours turn dependability into a number.
senses.whyCN: 工程学把这个词量化：故障率与测试时长把「可依赖」变成一个数字。

senses.title: Credibility of a source
senses.titleCN: 信源可信：信息可被采信的程度
senses.definition: the degree to which a source of information can be trusted
senses.definitionCN: 信息来源可以被信任的程度
senses.example: The reliability of the witness was questioned in court.
senses.exampleCN: 证人的可信度在法庭上受到质疑。
senses.why: Here the instrument is a person's account: courts ask whether the report can be depended on, not whether a device repeats a reading.
senses.whyCN: 这里的仪器是一个人的陈述：法院追问这份报告能否被依赖，而不是装置能否重复读数。

senses.title: Inter-rater reliability
senses.titleCN: 评分者间信度：不同评分者结果一致
senses.definition: in assessment, the degree to which different raters give consistent scores
senses.definitionCN: 评估中不同评分者给出一致分数的程度
senses.example: Inter-rater reliability was high after the rubric was clarified.
senses.exampleCN: 评分标准明确后，评分者间信度很高。
senses.why: When judgement replaces a machine, consistency must be checked between people, and the word is applied to that agreement.
senses.whyCN: 当判断取代机器时，必须检查人与人之间的一致性，该词就被用于这种一致程度。

senses.title: Statistical reliability
senses.titleCN: 统计信度：结果可重复出现
senses.definition: in statistics, the consistency of a measure across samples or the repeatability of a finding
senses.definitionCN: 统计学中测量跨样本的一致性，或发现的可重复性
senses.example: The effect's reliability fell when the sample was split.
senses.exampleCN: 样本拆分后，该效应的可靠性下降了。
senses.why: Statistics asks whether the same result survives a new sample; if it does not, the measurement was stable only within one data set.
senses.whyCN: 统计学追问同一结果能否在新样本中存活；若不能，该测量的稳定只限于原数据集。

senses.title: System reliability
senses.titleCN: 系统可靠性：整体在压力下持续供电或运行
senses.definition: the ability of a whole system, such as a power grid, to keep operating under expected stress
senses.definitionCN: 整个系统（如电网）在预期压力下持续运行的能力
senses.example: Grid reliability depends on spare capacity and quick repairs.
senses.exampleCN: 电网可靠性取决于备用容量与快速修复。
senses.why: A grid is a chain of components, so the whole can fail where any link fails; system reliability counts the weakest link and the capacity held in reserve.
senses.whyCN: 电网是由部件连成的链条，任一环失效整体就可能失效；系统可靠性要计及最弱环节与储备容量。

senses.title: Reliability of memory
senses.titleCN: 记忆可靠性：回忆能否经得起核对
senses.definition: in psychology and law, the degree to which a memory or identification can be trusted
senses.definitionCN: 心理学与法律中，记忆或辨认可被信任的程度
senses.example: Eyewitness reliability decreases under stress.
senses.exampleCN: 压力之下，目击者记忆的可靠性会下降。
senses.why: The word moves inward: the measuring instrument is now a mind, and the question is whether its readings hold.
senses.whyCN: 词义向内移动：测量仪器现在是心智，问题变成它的读数是否站得住。

intro.en: Reliability is reliable plus -ity. Reliable comes from rely, which entered English through Old French relier, from Latin religare 'to bind fast' — the same root as religion, though the meanings divided.
intro.cn: reliability 是 reliable 加 -ity。reliable 出自 rely，后者经古法语 relier 进入英语，源于拉丁 religare「牢牢绑住」——与 religion 同根，但词义后来分道。

items.en: Ligare meant 'to bind, tie'. Its compounds include oblige, ligature, ally and religion, all built on binding.
items.cn: ligare 意为「绑、系」，其复合词包括 oblige、ligature、ally、religion，都建立在「绑定」意象上。

items.en: Religare strengthened ligare with re-, meaning 'to bind fast or back'. It could describe tying something securely or binding a person by obligation.
items.cn: religare 用 re- 加强 ligare，意为「牢牢绑住或绑回」，可指把某物系紧，或以义务约束某人。

items.en: Old French relier meant 'to bind, attach, depend on'. English rely first meant 'to gather together' and then 'to depend with confidence'.
items.cn: 古法语 relier 意为「绑、连接、依赖」。英语 rely 最初意为「聚拢」，后指「有把握地依赖」。

items.en: Reliable appeared in the seventeenth century, meaning 'that may be depended on'. The -able suffix marks capacity or fitness.
items.cn: reliable 于 17 世纪出现，意为「可被依赖的」；-able 后缀标记能力或适合性。

items.en: Reliability followed as the abstract noun, and twentieth-century statistics and engineering made it a measured property.
items.cn: reliability 随后作为抽象名词出现；20 世纪的统计学与工程学把它变成可测量的属性。

items.en: The exact first English citation is uncertain, and the semantic split between rely and religion is a later development rather than part of the original root meaning.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅首见年代）：英语最早书证确切年代存疑；rely 与 religion 的语义分化属于后来的发展，并非原始词根义的一部分。

note.en: The first group separates the rely family; the second gives near-synonyms for trustworthiness and consistency.
note.cn: 第一组区分 rely 词族；第二组给出关于可信与一致的近义词。

entries.definition: Describing someone or something that can be depended on; reliability is the noun.
entries.definitionCN: 形容可以依赖的人或物；reliability 是对应名词。

entries.definition: To depend on someone or something. It names the act of trusting, not the quality.
entries.definitionCN: 指依赖某人或某物；命名信任的行为，而非性质。

entries.definition: The condition of depending on something. It is the dependence, not the trustworthiness of the object.
entries.definitionCN: 指依赖的状态；是依赖本身，而非对象的可信程度。

entries.definition: From Latin religio, traditionally linked to religare 'bind fast'. It shares the root with rely but has followed a separate semantic path.
entries.definitionCN: 出自拉丁 religio，传统上与 religare「牢牢绑住」相关。它与 rely 同根，但走上了独立的语义路径。

entries.definition: The quality of being worthy of trust. It is close to sense 1 but more personal and moral.
entries.definitionCN: 指值得信任的品质；接近第 1 个义项，但更偏人格与道德。

entries.definition: The quality of being dependable in practice. It overlaps sense 1 but stresses performance over time.
entries.definitionCN: 指在实践中可被指望的品质；与第 1 个义项重叠，但强调长期表现。

entries.definition: The quality of giving the same results or behaving the same way. It is the core of measurement reliability.
entries.definitionCN: 指给出相同结果或行为一致的性质，是测量可靠性的核心。

entries.definition: In research, the degree to which a test measures what it claims to measure. Reliability is stability; validity is correctness of target.
entries.definitionCN: 研究中指测试测量其所声称之物的程度。reliability 是稳定，validity 是目标正确。

entries.definition: The quality of being believed. It concerns acceptance by an audience more than technical consistency.
entries.definitionCN: 指可被相信的品质，更关乎受众的接受，而非技术一致性。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: rely 'bind fast' + -able + -ity: the quality of being tied to one's word.
normal.cn: rely「牢牢绑住」+ -able + -ity：被绑定于承诺的品质。

normal.en: The family runs rely, reliable, reliably, reliance, unreliable.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 rely、reliable、reliably、reliance、unreliable。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the fields: test reliability, inter-rater reliability, system reliability, reliability engineering.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出领域：考试信度、评分者间信度、系统可靠性、可靠性工程。

normal.en: Reliability is stability; validity is measuring the right thing.
normal.cn: reliability 是稳定性；validity 是测对了东西。

normal.en: religion and rely share the root 'bind', but their meanings divided long ago.
normal.cn: religion 与 rely 共享「绑定」词根，但词义早已分化。

abstract.en: Picture the same ruler laid on the same board fifty times, each mark landing identically.
abstract.cn: 想象同一把尺子在同一块板上量五十次，每次刻度都落在同一处。

abstract.en: Picture a bridge cable that holds the same load year after year without slackening.
abstract.cn: 想象桥梁缆索年复一年承受同一荷载，从未松脱。

abstract.en: Picture two examiners scoring the same essay and arriving at the same number.
abstract.cn: 想象两位阅卷人给同一篇作文打分，得到相同数字。

examples.en: The reliability of the test was checked by repeating it with the same group.
examples.cn: 该测试的可靠性通过在同一组人身上重复测试来检验。

examples.en: Reliability engineering studies how often parts fail and why.
examples.cn: 可靠性工程研究部件多常失效以及原因。

examples.en: The court weighed the reliability of the identification against the lighting conditions.
examples.cn: 法院结合照明条件权衡了辨认结果的可靠性。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「rely（依赖）+ ability（能力）」——值得依赖的能力 → reliability 可靠性

root: 拉丁 ligare「绑」→ religare「牢牢绑住」→ 古法语 relier → 英语 rely；加 -able 与 -ity 成 reliability。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses test the same question in different instruments: a person's word, a sensor, an engine, a witness, a rubric, a statistic, a grid, a memory.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项在不同的「仪器」上检验同一个问题：人的承诺、传感器、发动机、证人、评分标准、统计结果、电网、记忆。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one ruler laid on one board fifty times, every mark aligned.
core.cn: 核心意象：同一把尺在同一块板上量五十次，每次刻度对齐。

branches.en: A PERSON: the promise is the thing that holds.
branches.cn: 人：被绑定的是承诺。

branches.en: MEASUREMENT: repeated readings and split samples test stability.
branches.cn: 测量：重复读数与拆分样本检验稳定性。

branches.en: MACHINES: components and whole grids are counted by failure and uptime.
branches.cn: 机器：部件与整个电网按故障与运行时间计量。

branches.en: JUDGEMENT: witnesses and raters are checked against one another.
branches.cn: 判断：证人与评分者被相互核对。

branches.en: MEMORY: the inward instrument may give a stable but wrong reading.
branches.cn: 记忆：内在仪器可能给出稳定却错误的读数。

intro.en: Reliability is an adjective of trust turned into a quality noun: rely, reliable, then -ity, with the root ligare 'bind' underneath.
intro.cn: reliability 是表示信任的形容词转为性质名词：rely、reliable，再加 -ity，底层词根是 ligare「绑」。

latinIntro.en: The ligare family includes rely, reliable, religion, oblige, ligature, ally and league; the shared image is something tied or bound.
latinIntro.cn: ligare 词族包括 rely、reliable、religion、oblige、ligature、ally、league，共同意象是被系住或绑住之物。

items.example: The reliability of the data was questioned.
items.exampleCN: 这些数据的可靠性受到质疑。

items.example: She is a reliable witness.
items.exampleCN: 她是一位可靠的证人。

items.example: We rely on the backup generator.
items.exampleCN: 我们依赖备用发电机。

items.meaning: the state of depending on something
items.example: Reliance on one supplier is risky.
items.exampleCN: 依赖单一供应商有风险。

items.meaning: a system of faith and worship
items.example: The region has two major religions.
items.exampleCN: 该地区有两大宗教。

items.meaning: to bind by duty or favour
items.example: The law obliges firms to report.
items.exampleCN: 法律要求公司报告。

items.example: The surgeon used a ligature to close the vessel.
items.exampleCN: 外科医生用结扎带闭合血管。

items.example: The two parties allied against the threat.
items.exampleCN: 两方结盟应对威胁。

definition_zh: 隐性的；隐性性状；后退的；不显眼的
definition_en: not expressed when a dominant allele is present; also tending to recede
core_image: 两个人并排站着，一个向前一步，另一个退进阴影里
scene: 两个携带者都表现正常，却在孩子身上看到了隐藏的特征。医生解释： The recessive allele only shows when both copies are the same.
sceneCN: 这里指「隐性的」（第 1 个义项：与显性等位基因同时存在时被掩盖、不表现）；句意为隐性等位基因只有在两份拷贝相同时才表现。

pos.zh: 隐性的；后退的；不显眼的
隐性性状；隐性等位基因

senses.title: Genetically recessive
senses.definition: not expressed in the phenotype when a dominant allele is also present
senses.definitionCN: 当显性等位基因同时存在时不在表型中表现
senses.example: The recessive allele only shows when both copies are the same.
senses.exampleCN: 隐性等位基因只有在两份拷贝相同时才表现。
senses.why: The word pictures stepping back: one version yields the foreground to the other and stays in the background.
senses.whyCN: 这个词描绘后退：一个版本把前景让给另一个，自己留在背景里。

senses.title: A recessive allele
senses.definition: an allele whose effect is masked by a dominant allele
senses.definitionCN: 效果被显性等位基因掩盖的等位基因
senses.example: She carries one recessive allele without showing the trait.
senses.exampleCN: 她携带一个隐性等位基因，却没有表现出该性状。
senses.why: As a noun the word names the version that loses the foreground, not the person who carries it.
senses.whyCN: 作名词时，这个词命名失去前景的那个版本，而不是携带它的人。

senses.title: A recessive trait
senses.definition: a trait that appears only when both alleles are recessive
senses.definitionCN: 只有在两个等位基因都为隐性时才出现的性状
senses.example: Blue eyes are often described as a recessive trait.
senses.exampleCN: 蓝眼常被描述为一种隐性性状。
senses.why: The adjective moves from the gene to the visible feature, naming the trait that waits for a matching copy.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词从基因移到可见特征，命名那种等待配对拷贝的性状。

senses.title: Recessive inheritance
senses.definition: a pattern in which the trait appears only in homozygotes
senses.definitionCN: 性状只在纯合个体中出现的遗传模式
senses.example: The disease follows a recessive pattern in this family.
senses.exampleCN: 这种病在这个家族中遵循隐性遗传模式。
senses.why: Genetics turns the adjective into a label for a transmission pattern, useful in counselling.
senses.whyCN: 遗传学把这个形容词变成一种传递模式的标签，在遗传咨询中很有用。

senses.title: Hidden or unexpressed generally
senses.titleCN: 被掩盖的；不表现的（广义）
senses.definition: present but not showing, in a general or figurative sense
senses.definitionCN: 存在却不显露，用于一般或比喻意义
senses.example: A recessive fear shaped her silence.
senses.exampleCN: 一种隐而不显的恐惧造成了她的沉默。
senses.why: The genetic picture of a hidden version is borrowed for anything present but out of sight.
senses.whyCN: 「隐藏版本」的遗传图像被借用来形容任何存在却看不见的事物。

senses.title: Receding or moving back
senses.definition: moving or tending to move backward
senses.definitionCN: 向后移动或有向后趋势的
senses.example: The recessive shoreline moved inland each year.
senses.exampleCN: 后退的海岸线每年都向内陆移动。
senses.why: The older spatial sense survives beside the genetic one: recede means to go back, and the adjective inherits that direction.
senses.whyCN: 较旧的空间义与遗传义并存：recede 意为后退，形容词继承了这个方向。

senses.title: Expressed only in homozygotes
senses.definition: showing its effect only when two identical recessive copies are present
senses.definitionCN: 只有两份相同的隐性拷贝存在时才表现效果
senses.example: The recessive form appears in one quarter of the offspring.
senses.exampleCN: 隐性类型出现在四分之一的后代中。
senses.why: The word describes a condition of expression, so it also names the rule that governs when the trait can be seen.
senses.whyCN: 这个词描述表现条件，因此也命名决定该性状何时可见的规则。

senses.title: A recessive mutation
senses.definition: a mutation whose effect is hidden unless no dominant version is present
senses.definitionCN: 除非没有显性版本存在、否则效果被隐藏的突变
senses.example: A recessive mutation can spread unnoticed for generations.
senses.exampleCN: 隐性突变可以在无人察觉的情况下传播数代。
senses.why: At the molecular level the adjective marks changes that do not alter the visible phenotype while a normal copy remains.
senses.whyCN: 在分子层面，这个形容词标记那些在正常拷贝仍存在时不改变可见表型的改变。

intro.en: Recessive comes from Latin recessus, the past participle of recedere 'to go back', built from re- 'back' and cedere 'to go'. The genetic sense arose around 1900. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: recessive 来自拉丁 recessus，即 recedere「后退」的过去分词，由 re-「向后」与 cedere「走」构成。遗传学义项约在 1900 年出现。年代均为约数。

items.en: Cedere meant 'to go, yield, withdraw'. It is the source of proceed, concede, precede and recede, and carries the idea of stepping.
items.cn: cedere 意为「走、让、退」，是 proceed、concede、precede 与 recede 的来源，带有「迈步」的意味。

items.en: Recedere combined re- 'back' with cedere 'to go': to go back, withdraw, retreat. Its past participle recessus gives English recess and recession as well as recessive.
items.cn: recedere 把 re-「向后」与 cedere「走」结合，意为后退、退出、撤退。其过去分词 recessus 衍生英语 recess、recession 与 recessive。

items.en: Recessive entered English in the seventeenth century with the spatial sense 'tending to recede'. That sense remains rare but survives.
items.cn: recessive 在 17 世纪进入英语，带空间义「有后退趋势」。这个义项虽少见，仍然存在。

items.en: Around 1900 genetics took the word for an allele that steps back when a dominant partner is present; the metaphor is one of yielding the foreground.
items.cn: 约 1900 年，遗传学用这个词指在显性伙伴存在时退让的等位基因；这个隐喻就是让出前景。

items.en: Modern English uses recessive mainly in genetics, with fixed phrases such as autosomal recessive and recessive inheritance.
items.cn: 现代英语中 recessive 主要用于遗传学，常见固定说法有常染色体隐性、隐性遗传。

items.en: Source uncertain (first dates): the earliest English use of recessive is dated only to the seventeenth century, and the exact adoption of the genetic sense around 1900 is not fixed.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：recessive 在英语中的最早使用只能定在 17 世纪；遗传义项在 1900 年前后的确切采用时间未有定论。

note.en: Group one holds words from the same recede-family that look similar; group two holds near meanings of hiddenness or withdrawal.
note.cn: 第一组是同出 recede 词族、外形相近的词；第二组是表示隐藏或退让的邻近词。

entries.definition: A pause in work, or a hollow space in a wall; it is a noun of withdrawal, not a genetic term.
entries.definitionCN: 指工作暂停，或墙上的凹处；是表示退缩的名词，并非遗传术语。

entries.definition: A period when the economy shrinks; it shares the going-back picture but belongs to economics.
entries.definitionCN: 指经济萎缩的时期；共享「后退」图像，但属经济领域。

entries.definition: To move back or become weaker; the adjective recessive describes what has that tendency.
entries.definitionCN: 指向后退或变弱；形容词 recessive 描述具有这种趋势的事物。

entries.definition: Relating to a departure, especially a hymn sung as clergy leave; the shape is similar but the use is ceremonial.
entries.definitionCN: 指与退场相关的，尤指神职人员退场时唱的赞美诗；外形相似，用途属礼仪。

entries.definition: Expressed even when paired with a different allele; recessive is its exact counterpart.
entries.definitionCN: 指即使与不同等位基因配对也表现；recessive 是其正相对概念。

entries.definition: Not visible or not known; it is broader and carries no genetic mechanism.
entries.definitionCN: 指不可见或未知；范围更广，不含遗传机制。

entries.definition: Existing but not yet active or expressed; disease and talent can be latent, but recessive is specific to alleles.
entries.definitionCN: 指存在但尚未活动或表现；疾病与才能都可以是潜在的，而 recessive 专指等位基因。

entries.definition: Lower in position or importance; it is social, while recessive is about expression.
entries.definitionCN: 指地位或重要性较低；属社会层面，而 recessive 关乎表现。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: re- 'back' + cedere 'go' + -ive: tending to go back.
normal.cn: re-「向后」+ cedere「走」+ -ive：有后退趋势的。

normal.en: The family runs recede, recession, recess, recessive, recessiveness.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 recede、recession、recess、recessive、recessiveness。

normal.en: The genetic pair is fixed: dominant versus recessive.
normal.cn: 遗传学中的配对是固定的：显性对隐性。

normal.en: A recessive allele steps back but is still inherited.
normal.cn: 隐性等位基因退到后面，却仍可被继承。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: recessive allele, recessive trait, autosomal recessive.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：隐性等位基因、隐性性状、常染色体隐性。

abstract.en: Picture one actor standing behind another, waiting for the same cue.
abstract.cn: 想象一个演员站在另一个身后，等同一个提示。

abstract.en: Picture a tide moving away from the shore.
abstract.cn: 想象潮水从岸边退走。

abstract.en: Picture a light dimmed by a brighter lamp beside it.
abstract.cn: 想象一盏灯被旁边更亮的灯压暗。

examples.en: Two carrier parents can have a child with the recessive disease.
examples.cn: 两个携带者亲代可能生出患隐性遗传病的孩子。

examples.en: The recessive allele remained hidden for three generations.
examples.cn: 这个隐性等位基因隐藏了三代。

examples.en: Recessive traits reappear when relatives marry.
examples.cn: 亲属通婚时隐性性状会重新出现。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「瑞塞西夫」——站在后面、把位置让出去的那一个 → 隐性的

root: 拉丁 recedere「后退」（re-「向后」+ cedere「走」）的过去分词 recessus + -ive；遗传学义项约始于 1900 年。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one step back: a version yields the foreground, and the same yielding picture extends to traits, inheritance, hidden things, shorelines and mutations.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项围绕一次后退展开：一个版本让出前景，同一幅退让图像再延伸到性状、遗传、隐藏事物、海岸线与突变。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one figure steps forward while the other steps into the shade.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人向前一步，另一个退进阴影。

branches.en: ALLELE AND NOUN: the basic masked version, and the same version named as a noun.
branches.cn: 等位基因与名词：基本的被掩盖版本，以及被名词化的同一版本。

branches.en: TRAIT AND TRANSMISSION: the visible trait, the family pattern, and the homozygote condition that releases it.
branches.cn: 性状与传递：可见性状、家族模式，以及让它显现的纯合条件。

branches.en: GENERAL MASKING: anything kept out of sight borrows the same image of a figure standing in shade.
branches.cn: 广义掩盖：任何被藏在视线之外的事物，都借用同一个人退进阴影的意象。

branches.en: MOLECULAR MUTATION: a change that stays unseen for generations, never showing on the surface.
branches.cn: 分子突变：一种可以数代不被看见、始终不显露于表面的改变。

branches.en: SPATIAL SURVIVAL: the old sense of moving backward still lives in the word.
branches.cn: 空间义的留存：向后移动的旧义仍活在这个词里。

intro.en: Recessive joins the Latin prefix re- 'back', the root ced- 'go', and the adjective suffix -ive: literally 'tending to go back'.
intro.cn: recessive 把拉丁前缀 re-「向后」、词根 ced-「走」与形容词后缀 -ive 结合，字面义为「有后退趋势的」。

latinIntro.en: Latin recedere and its participle recessus supply recede, recess, recession and recessive; the same cedere root also builds proceed, concede and precede.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 recedere 及其分词 recessus 提供 recede、recess、recession 与 recessive；同一 cedere 词根还构成 proceed、concede 与 precede。

items.example: The prefix turns going into going back.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把「走」变成「往回走」。

items.example: The root also appears in precede and concede.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根也出现在 precede 与 concede 中。

items.meaning: tending to; having the quality of
items.example: Recessive means tending to recede.
items.exampleCN: recessive 意为有后退倾向的。

items.example: The flood water receded at dawn.
items.exampleCN: 洪水在黎明时退去。

items.meaning: a withdrawal; a hollow; a break
items.example: The court took a short recess.
items.exampleCN: 法庭短暂休庭。

items.meaning: a going back; an economic decline
items.example: The recession lasted eighteen months.
items.exampleCN: 这次衰退持续了十八个月。

items.meaningCN: 有后退趋势的；遗传上隐性的
items.example: The recessive form stays in the background.
items.exampleCN: 隐性类型留在背景中。

items.example: Recessiveness depends on the partner allele.
items.exampleCN: 隐性状态取决于配对的等位基因。

items.example: The trait is recessively inherited.
items.exampleCN: 该性状以隐性方式遗传。

definition_zh: 流动性；移动能力；（人或资源在地方、职业、阶层之间的）流动
definition_en: the ability or tendency to move, or the movement of people between places, jobs or social positions
core_image: 同一个人分别拄着助行器挪向车站、拖着箱子搬到另一座城、从车间走进办公室，三条路线并排出现
scene: 雨后的车站里，一位拄拐的老人慢慢挪向站台边。 Mobility is the first thing a physiotherapist works to restore after a stroke.
sceneCN: 这里 mobility 指「身体活动的能力」（第 1 个义项：行动自如的能力）；句意为中风之后，康复师最先着手恢复的是活动能力。图中可辨识物件：拐杖、站台边沿、康复训练带、三条并行路线。

pos.zh: 流动性；移动能力（不可数；指具体某类流动时可作可数）

derivatives.zh: 可移动的 / 移动电话
动员；使流动
动员；调动
不能移动；静止状态
不能移动的

senses.title: Physical ability to move
senses.definition: the power of a person to move the body, especially to walk or shift position
senses.definitionCN: 一个人移动身体的能力，尤指行走或变换姿势
senses.example: Mobility is the first thing a physiotherapist works to restore after a stroke.
senses.exampleCN: 中风之后，康复师最先着手恢复的是活动能力。
senses.why: mobility comes from a Latin word for being movable, so the body is the most literal thing that can be mobile.
senses.whyCN: mobility 源自拉丁语中「可移动」的说法，因此身体是最字面意义上的可动之物。

senses.title: Ability to travel or be transported
senses.definition: the ease with which people or goods can reach places
senses.definitionCN: 人或货物抵达各地点的便利程度
senses.example: The new tram line gave the district a mobility it had never had.
senses.exampleCN: 新有轨电车线给了这个城区从未有过的出行便利。
senses.why: once movement is supplied by vehicles, the word shifts from the body to the journey.
senses.whyCN: 当移动由交通工具提供时，这个词便从身体转到旅程上。

senses.title: Movement between social positions
senses.definition: the movement of people between social classes or ranks
senses.definitionCN: 人们在社阶层之间或等级之间的移动
senses.example: Education is the strongest single lever of mobility in the survey.
senses.exampleCN: 在这项调查中，教育是撬动社会流动最强的一根杠杆。
senses.why: a society can be imagined as a ladder, and mobility is the traffic up and down it.
senses.whyCN: 社会可以被想象成一架梯子，流动就是上上下下的往来。

senses.title: Movement between jobs
senses.definition: the frequency with which workers change jobs, employers or trades
senses.definitionCN: 劳动者更换工作、雇主或行业的频繁程度
senses.example: Job mobility is high in hospitality, where contracts are short.
senses.exampleCN: 餐饮住宿业合同期短，职业流动很高。
senses.why: occupation is the everyday channel through which social movement is actually observed.
senses.whyCN: 职业是实际观察社会流动时最日常的通道。

senses.title: Movement between places
senses.definition: the movement of people from one place or region to another
senses.definitionCN: 人们从一个地方或地区移动到另一个
senses.example: Residential mobility falls sharply once families own their homes.
senses.exampleCN: 家庭一旦拥有自有住房，迁居流动就明显下降。
senses.why: migration is mobility written on a map, so the word covers changing address as well as changing class.
senses.whyCN: 迁移是画在地图上的流动，因此这个词既涵盖换阶层，也涵盖换住址。

senses.title: Movement of labour and capital
senses.definition: the freedom of workers, money or resources to move to where they are most useful
senses.definitionCN: 工人、资金或资源流向最有用处的自由程度
senses.example: Capital mobility lets savings cross borders in seconds.
senses.exampleCN: 资本流动让储蓄在几秒内跨越国境。
senses.why: economists generalized the idea from people to any input that can be shifted between uses.
senses.whyCN: 经济学家把这个概念从人推广到任何可在用途之间转移的投入。

senses.title: Charge-carrier mobility in physics
senses.titleCN: 物理学中的载流子迁移率
senses.definition: a measure of how quickly electrons or other charge carriers drift through a material under a field
senses.definitionCN: 在电场作用下，电子等载流子在材料中漂移快慢的量度
senses.example: Silicon has a lower electron mobility than gallium arsenide.
senses.exampleCN: 硅的电子迁移率比砷化镓低。
senses.why: the technical sense keeps the literal core: how easily the carriers can move through the lattice.
senses.whyCN: 这一技术义保留了字面核心：载流子在晶格中移动的容易程度。

senses.title: Tactical mobility in warfare
senses.definition: the ability of troops or equipment to move quickly into position
senses.definitionCN: 部队或装备快速进入位置的能力
senses.example: The brigade traded armour for mobility on the mountain roads.
senses.exampleCN: 该旅在山路上用装甲换取机动性。
senses.why: military planners want the same thing the word names everywhere: movement without delay.
senses.whyCN: 军事规划者想要的，正是这个词到处所指的东西：不受耽搁的移动。

intro.en: Mobility comes from Latin mobilitas 'movement, changeableness', formed on mobilis 'movable', which in turn rests on movere 'to move'. It entered English through Old French. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: mobility 来自拉丁 mobilitas「移动、易变」，由 mobilis「可移动」构成，而 mobilis 又出自 movere「移动」。它经古法语进入英语。年代均为约数。

items.en: Movere meant 'to move, set in motion'. Its deeper root is reconstructed rather than attested, and the form commonly quoted for it is a reconstruction.
items.cn: movere 意为「移动、使动」。其更深词根属重构形式而非直接记录，常被引用的那个印欧形式也只是重构。

items.en: Mobilis 'movable, flexible, changeable' was used of bodies, property and minds alike, already widening the sense beyond mere travel.
items.cn: mobilis 意为「可移动的、灵活的、易变的」，既用于身体，也用于财产与心思，其含义早已超出单纯的行走。

items.en: Mobilitas named both physical movement and the fickleness of fortune, a pairing that later made social rank a natural extension.
items.cn: mobilitas 既指身体的移动，也指命运的无常，这种并置后来使社会等级的引申显得自然。

items.en: Old French mobilite carried the noun into English in the fourteenth century, first as a word for movement and mutability.
items.cn: 古法语 mobilite 在 14 世纪把这个名词带入英语，最初指移动与无常。

items.en: Industrial and social change gave the word its familiar modern uses: movement of workers, of families and of classes, and later the drift of electrons in a solid.
items.cn: 工业与社会变迁赋予它熟悉的现代用法：工人、家庭与阶层的移动，后来又加上电子在固体中的漂移。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin): the Indo-European root behind movere is a reconstruction, and no attested earlier form of the word survives.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源）：movere 背后的印欧词根属重构形式，该词没有更早的有据可查形式流传下来。

note.en: Group one holds words built on the same root that look confusingly alike; group two holds words for movement with a narrower reach.
note.cn: 第一组是同出这一词根、外形极易混淆的词；第二组是表示移动但范围更窄的词。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning able to move, and a noun for a telephone that moves with its owner; it is not the abstract noun of movement.
entries.definitionCN: 作形容词指可移动的，作名词指随身携带的电话；它不是表示抽象流动的名词。

entries.definition: To set people or resources in motion for a purpose; the verb names the act, not the capacity.
entries.definitionCN: 为某个目的把人或资源调动起来；动词指动作，不指能力。

entries.definition: From mutare 'to change', not movere: it means susceptibility to change, often in biology or law.
entries.definitionCN: 出自 mutare「改变」而非 movere：指易受改变的性质，常用于生物学或法律。

entries.definition: The capacity for spontaneous movement in cells or organisms; a technical cousin, not the general social word.
entries.definitionCN: 细胞或生物自发运动的能力；是技术上的近亲，不是泛指的社会用语。

entries.definition: The everyday noun for changing position; it lacks the implication of capacity or rate that mobility carries.
entries.definitionCN: 表示位置改变的日常名词；不含 mobility 所带的「能力或比率」意味。

entries.definition: Movement produced by the organism itself, used of sperm, bacteria or gut muscle rather than of people in a society.
entries.definitionCN: 由生物自身产生的运动，用于精子、细菌或肠道肌肉，而非社会中的人。

entries.definition: The ability to bend or adapt to new conditions; it overlaps with mobility only when the change is one of position or job.
entries.definitionCN: 弯曲或适应新条件的能力；只有当变化涉及位置或工作时，才与 mobility 重叠。

entries.definition: Movement caused by something else pushing or removing; it usually implies loss of a former place.
entries.definitionCN: 由外力推走或移走造成的移动；通常意味着失去原来的位置。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real root, real fixed phrases and real relatives, not invented sound-alikes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的词根、真实的固定搭配与真实的同族词，而非编造的谐音。

normal.en: The root means move, so mobility is the capacity to be moved or to move.
normal.cn: 词根意为移动，因此 mobility 就是能被移动或自行移动的能力。

normal.en: Labour mobility, social mobility and geographic mobility mark the three main fields.
normal.cn: 劳动力流动、社会流动与地理流动标出三大领域。

normal.en: A mobility aid is literally a device that gives movement back.
normal.cn: 助行器具字面上就是一件把移动能力还给人的装置。

normal.en: Mobile, mobilize and mobilization all share the same root.
normal.cn: 同族的「移动的」「动员」「动员化」等形式共用同一个词根。

normal.en: In physics the word keeps the literal sense: how easily carriers move.
normal.cn: 在物理学中这个词保持字面义：载流子移动的容易程度。

abstract.en: Picture a door that opens in three directions: to the street, to another class and to another job.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇门朝三个方向打开：通向街道、通向另一个阶层、通向另一份工作。

abstract.en: Picture water that finds every gap in a wall, never staying where it was put.
abstract.cn: 想象水穿过墙上的每一道缝，从不停在被放置的地方。

abstract.en: Picture a ladder leaning against a building that is itself being rebuilt.
abstract.cn: 想象一架梯子靠在正在重建的建筑上。

examples.en: The study links residential mobility to the length of a daily commute.
examples.cn: 这项研究把迁居流动与每日通勤距离联系起来。

examples.en: Labour mobility across the border fell after the visa rules changed.
examples.cn: 签证规则改变后，跨境劳动力流动下降了。

examples.en: Improved mobility in the knee was the main goal of the treatment.
examples.cn: 治疗的主要目标是改善膝关节的活动度。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「摸吧·力」——一摸就能动起来的能力，就是移动能力与流动性

root: 拉丁 movere「移动」→ mobilis「可移动的」→ mobilitas「移动、易变」；经古法语进入英语为 mobility。movere 的更深词根属重构形式。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses radiate from one capacity: a body that can move, a person who can reach places, a worker who can change jobs, a class that can rise, capital that can cross borders, carriers that drift through a crystal, and troops that can reach the ridge.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从同一种能力辐射开来：能动的身体、能抵达各处的人、能换工作的劳动者、能上升的阶层、能跨越国境的资本、能在晶体中漂移的载流子，以及能抵达山脊的部队。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the same person moving along three routes at once, by foot, by train and up a job ladder.
core.cn: 核心意象：同一个人同时沿三条路线移动，靠双脚、靠列车，也沿职业阶梯向上。

branches.en: BODY: the most literal sense, the power to move one's own limbs.
branches.cn: 身体：最字面的义项，移动自己肢体的能力。

branches.en: VEHICLE: movement is handed over to transport, so the word comes to mean access to places.
branches.cn: 交通工具：移动交给交通工具完成，词义便转为抵达各地的便利。

branches.en: JOB AND ADDRESS: changing employer and changing town are the two everyday forms of movement.
branches.cn: 工作与住址：换雇主与换城市是移动最日常的两种形式。

branches.en: CLASS AND CAPITAL: people and money both move to where opportunity is higher.
branches.cn: 阶层与资本：人和钱都会流向机会更多的地方。

branches.en: PHYSICS AND WAR: the same capacity measured in a crystal or required on a ridge.
branches.cn: 物理与军事：同一种能力，或在晶体中被计量，或在山脊上被要求。

intro.en: Mobility is one Latin root plus two suffixes, and the whole family can be read from those pieces.
intro.cn: mobility 由一个拉丁词根加两个后缀构成，整个词族都可以按这些成分读出。

latinIntro.en: Latin movere supplies the root; the suffixes -ilis and -itas shape it first into an adjective and then into a noun of state.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 movere 提供词根；后缀 -ilis 与 -itas 先把它构成形容词，再构成表状态的名词。

items.example: The root is the seed of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根是整个词族的种子。

items.example: It builds the adjective of capacity.

items.example: A mobile clinic reaches the villages.
items.exampleCN: 流动诊所抵达各个村庄。

items.example: It converts the adjective into a state noun.
items.exampleCN: 它把形容词转成表状态的名词。

items.example: Mobility of labour is high in the coastal cities.
items.exampleCN: 沿海城市的劳动力流动性很高。

items.example: It turns the adjective into a verb of action.
items.exampleCN: 它把形容词变成表动作的动词。

items.example: They mobilized the volunteers within a day.
items.exampleCN: 他们在一天之内动员了志愿者。

items.example: Mobilization of the reserves began at dawn.
items.exampleCN: 预备役的调动在黎明开始。

items.example: The joint was immobile for six weeks.
items.exampleCN: 这个关节有六周不能活动。

items.example: Long immobility weakens the muscles.
items.exampleCN: 长期不动会使肌肉变弱。

definition_zh: 自由；自由权；擅自；获准行动的范围
definition_en: freedom to live and act as one chooses, especially as a condition protected by law or constitution
core_image: 一根被砸断的锁链落在石阶上，锁孔里还插着半截钥匙，人已经走远
scene: 城邦的公民在广场上宣读宪章，声称任何人不得未经审判而被拘押。 Citizens in the square read out the charter declaring that no one should be detained without trial, a guarantee of personal liberty.
sceneCN: 这里指「受法律保障、不受任意拘押的个人自由」，对应第 1 个义项：法律保护的、免于任意逮捕的自由；句意为公民宣读宪章，宣布未经审判不得拘押任何人。画面要点：广场、宪章、砸断的锁链。

pos.zh: 自由；自由权（不可数；表示各项具体自由时可用复数）

collocations.zh: 获准的；自由的；有空闲的

derivatives.zh: 自由的；宽容的；自由主义的（拉丁语中表示「自由人的、宽厚的」形容词经法语传入，语义由身份转向宽宏与开明）
解放；释放（表示「自由的」词根加动词后缀，指使某人脱离束缚）
解放；释放（动词加表行为的名词后缀，指使脱离束缚的过程）
自由意志论者（表示「自由」的名词加表主张或从事者的后缀，指主张个人自由最大化的人）

senses.title: Protection from arbitrary detention
senses.titleCN: 免于任意拘押的个人自由
senses.definition: the condition of a person who cannot be arrested or held except by lawful procedure
senses.definitionCN: 除依法定程序外不得被逮捕或拘押的个人状态
senses.example: Citizens in the square read out the charter declaring that no one should be detained without trial, a guarantee of personal liberty.
senses.exampleCN: 公民在广场宣读宪章，宣布未经审判不得拘押任何人，这是对个人自由的保障。
senses.why: In Roman law the free person's body could not be seized at will, so liberty begins as a legal status rather than a mood.
senses.whyCN: 在罗马法中，自由人的身体不能被随意捉拿，因此「自由」一开始是一种法律身份，而不是一种心情。

senses.title: Self-government of a community
senses.definition: the condition of a city or people that makes its own laws instead of receiving them from a ruler
senses.definitionCN: 城市或民族自行立法、而不是从统治者那里接受法律的状态
senses.example: The city kept its liberties against the duke for two generations.
senses.exampleCN: 这座城邦两代人以来一直保有对抗公爵的自由权。
senses.why: Medieval towns bought charters that listed their liberties, so the word came to name a body's collective self-rule.
senses.whyCN: 中世纪城镇买下特许状，状上逐条列出它们的自由权，于是这个词也命名一个群体的自治。

senses.title: Specific rights protected by law
senses.titleCN: 法律保护的各项具体自由权
senses.definition: the several freedoms, such as speech, worship and assembly, that a constitution or statute guarantees
senses.definitionCN: 宪法或法律所保障的若干项自由，如言论、礼拜与集会
senses.example: The bill lists the liberties that the state may not remove.
senses.exampleCN: 权利法案列出了国家不得取消的各项自由。
senses.why: The abstract condition becomes countable when each guarantee is written down separately, which is why the plural is so common in legal texts.
senses.whyCN: 当每一项保障被分别写下来，抽象状态就变得可数，这就是复数形式在法律文本中如此常见的原因。

senses.title: Overstepping what is allowed
senses.definition: the act of acting beyond one's permitted scope, especially in a way that is presumptuous
senses.definitionCN: 超出自己被允许的范围行事，尤指冒失无礼地这样做
senses.example: The visitor took liberties with the archive and rearranged the files.
senses.exampleCN: 那位访客擅自摆弄档案，把文件重新排列了。
senses.why: A granted latitude can be used too far, so the same noun turns ironic and names the abuse of a permission.
senses.whyCN: 获准的余地可能被用过了头，于是同一个名词转为反讽，命名对许可的滥用。

senses.title: Being permitted or free to act
senses.definition: the state of being allowed to do something, or of being free from obligation at a particular time
senses.definitionCN: 获准做某事、或在某一时刻没有义务在身的状态
senses.example: You are at liberty to inspect the records yourself.
senses.exampleCN: 你可以自行查阅这些记录。
senses.why: The phrase 'at liberty' keeps the old legal sense of a person not under restraint, and from it comes the polite formula for permission.
senses.whyCN: 「处于自由状态」这一短语保留了「人未受拘束」的旧法律义，礼貌的许可说法正是从这里来的。

senses.title: Freedom of conscience and worship
senses.definition: the right to hold and practise a faith without state pressure
senses.definitionCN: 不受国家压力地持有并实践信仰的权利
senses.example: Religious liberty was the first liberty to be argued for in print.
senses.exampleCN: 宗教自由是最早被以印刷文字论证的自由。
senses.why: Where the state and the church were the same body, the demand to worship otherwise was the sharpest test of a protected sphere.
senses.whyCN: 当国家与教会合为一体，要求以别的方式礼拜，就成了对「受保护领域」最尖锐的检验。

senses.title: Freedom of the will
senses.definition: the philosophical claim that a person can choose without being wholly determined by prior causes
senses.definitionCN: 人能够作出选择、而不完全被先在原因所决定的哲学主张
senses.example: The essay asks whether liberty of the will survives a strict causal account.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇文章追问，在严格的决定论解释下，意志自由是否还能成立。
senses.why: Once legal restraint is removed, the remaining question is whether anything else restrains the will, and the word follows the question inward.
senses.whyCN: 一旦法律约束被移除，剩下的问题就是是否有别的东西在约束意志，这个词便随问题向内走。

senses.title: The range of a granted freedom
senses.definition: the extent of a place or body of knowledge that a person is allowed to use
senses.definitionCN: 一个人被允许使用的场所或知识范围
senses.example: The scholar was given the liberty of the whole collection.
senses.exampleCN: 这位学者获准自由使用全部藏书。
senses.why: To have the liberty of a place is an old civic formula: not ownership, but the permitted run of it.
senses.whyCN: 「拥有某地的自由」是一个古老的市民说法：不是所有权，而是被允许在其中往来。

intro.en: Liberty comes from Latin libertas, the condition of a free person, built on liber 'free'. The deeper origin of liber is uncertain. English took the word through Old French, and its plural came to mean specific chartered privileges.
intro.cn: liberty 出自拉丁语 libertas，指自由人的身份，建立在 liber「自由的」之上。liber 的更深来源不确定。英语经古法语吸收此词，其复数后来指特许状上具体列明的特权。

items.en: Liber meant 'free, not a slave' and could also describe a person of noble or generous status. Its own origin is uncertain; a connection with a root meaning 'to grow' has been suggested but not established.
items.cn: liber 意为「自由的、非奴隶的」，也可形容出身高贵或气度宽厚的人。它本身的来源不确定；有人提出它与意为「生长」的词根相关，但未获确立。

items.en: Libertas named the condition of a free person and, in Roman public life, the status that law protected against arbitrary seizure.
items.cn: libertas 指自由人的身份；在罗马公共生活中，它指法律保护、免于任意捉拿的身份。

items.en: Old French liberte carried the noun into English, at first in religious and civic contexts rather than in philosophy.
items.cn: 古法语 liberte 把这个名词带入英语，最初用于宗教与市民语境，而不是哲学。

items.en: Towns and guilds listed their liberties in charters, and the plural became a name for specific privileges held by a body.
items.cn: 城镇与行会在特许状中逐条列出自己的自由权，其复数形式于是成为某个群体所持具体特权的名称。

items.en: From the seventeenth century the singular named a general political condition, and documents began to speak of civil liberty. The date is approximate.
items.cn: 自十七世纪起，单数形式指一般的政治状态，文书开始谈论公民自由。年代为约数。

items.en: The same noun was applied to the will, producing the long debate over liberty of the will that continues in philosophy.
items.cn: 同一个名词被用到意志上，产生了关于意志自由的长期争论，这一争论在哲学中延续至今。

note.en: The first group is built on the same Latin adjective or looks deceptively close to it, including one word whose Latin source is a different noun altogether; the second group gives near alternatives.
note.cn: 第一组由同一个拉丁形容词构成或与它形近得容易误认，其中还有一个词的拉丁来源是另一个名词；第二组是近义替代。

entries.definition: Generous or open-minded, and in politics favourable to reform; it began as 'of a free person' and moved toward generosity of attitude.
entries.definitionCN: 宽厚的、开明的，政治上倾向改革；它起初意为「自由人的」，后来转向态度上的宽宏。

entries.definition: To set a person or place free from control; it names the act that produces liberty rather than the condition.
entries.definitionCN: 使人或地方脱离控制；它命名产生自由的动作，而不是状态。

entries.definition: A place where books are kept; its Latin source is a word for a book or the bark used for writing, not the adjective for freedom.
entries.definitionCN: 藏书之所；它的拉丁来源是表示「书」或书写用树皮的词，而不是表示自由的形容词。

entries.definition: A published false statement that harms a reputation; it comes from a small Latin book or booklet, with no link to freedom.
entries.definitionCN: 公开发表的、损害名誉的不实陈述；它出自拉丁语中表示小册子的词，与自由无关。

entries.definition: The general condition of not being bound; it covers body, will and speech, while liberty more often names a legally protected status.
entries.definitionCN: 不受束缚的一般状态；它覆盖身体、意志与言论，而本词更常指受法律保护的身份。

entries.definition: The right of a person or region to govern itself; it stresses who makes the rules rather than what is forbidden.
entries.definitionCN: 个人或地区自行治理的权利；它强调由谁制定规则，而不是禁止什么。

entries.definition: The state of not being controlled or supported by another; it is common for nations and for self-supporting people.
entries.definitionCN: 不受他人控制或供养的状态；常用于国家与自食其力的人。

entries.definition: An official permission to do something; it is narrower than liberty because it is granted case by case and can be revoked.
entries.definitionCN: 做某事的官方许可；它比自由窄，因为逐案授予且可被撤回。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the Latin adjective for a free person, real derived words and real legal formulas, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：拉丁语中表示自由人的形容词、真实派生词与真实法律套语，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The core is a legal status: a free body that cannot be seized at will.
normal.cn: 核心是一种法律身份：一具不能被随意捉拿的自由身体。

normal.en: The family runs liberal, liberate, liberation and libertarian.
normal.cn: 同族词包括宽厚的、解放、解放过程与自由意志论者。

normal.en: Medieval towns kept their liberties in written charters, which is why the plural means specific privileges.
normal.cn: 中世纪城镇把自由权写进特许状，所以复数形式指具体特权。

normal.en: The phrase at liberty means both free from restraint and free to act.
normal.cn: 「处于自由状态」这一说法既指不受拘束，也指可以行动。

normal.en: Taking liberties is the ironic side: using a permission further than it was given.
normal.cn: 「擅自」是这个词的反讽一面：把许可用得比给予的更远。

abstract.en: Picture a broken chain on a step with the key still in the lock, and the person already out of sight.
abstract.cn: 想象石阶上一根断链，钥匙还插在锁里，人已经走远。

abstract.en: Picture a charter rolled open on a town table, each paragraph a named freedom.
abstract.cn: 想象城镇桌上一卷摊开的特许状，每一段都是一项有名字的自由。

abstract.en: Picture a door marked permission that opens only when the right name is spoken.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇标着「许可」的门，只有说出正确的名分才会打开。

examples.en: The court held that the detention violated his liberty.
examples.cn: 法院认定这次拘押侵犯了他的自由。

examples.en: You are at liberty to leave whenever you wish.
examples.cn: 你随时都可以离开。

examples.en: The reporter took liberties with the quotation and changed its sense.
examples.cn: 那名记者擅自改动引文，改变了它的意思。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「离不体」——身体离开束缚，就不必再贴着锁链过日子；自由就是能走开的那一步。

root: 拉丁语 liber「自由的、非奴隶的」→ libertas「自由人的身份」→ 经古法语 liberte 进入英语。liber 的更深来源不确定，与意为「生长」的词根相关的说法属假说；同族的 liberalis 意为「自由人的、宽厚的」，是另一条语义支线。

sensesIntro.en: Eight readings start from a free body that the law may not seize. From that status come self-rule for a community, the list of named guarantees, the permission formula, the ironic overstepping of permission, the freedom of worship, the philosophical liberty of the will, and the old civic right to move through a place.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从一具法律不得随意捉拿的自由身体开始。从这个身份分出共同体的自治、逐条列名的保障、许可的说法、对许可的反讽式越界、信仰的自由、哲学上的意志自由，以及古老的、可在某地往来的市民权利。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a chain broken at the link, with the key still turning in the lock.
core.cn: 核心意象：链环被砸断的锁链，钥匙还在锁里转动。

branches.en: UNBOUND BODY: protection from arbitrary arrest, and the polite formula that a person is free to act.
branches.cn: 不受束缚的身体：免于任意逮捕，以及「可以自由行动」的礼貌说法。

branches.en: SELF-RULE: a town or people that makes its own law.
branches.cn: 自治：自行立法的城镇或民族。

branches.en: NAMED GUARANTEES: the several liberties written in a charter, and the permitted run of a place.
branches.cn: 列名的保障：写进特许状的各项自由，以及在某地获准走动的范围。

branches.en: OVERSTEPPING: the same permission used beyond what was granted.
branches.cn: 越界：同一份许可被用得超出所给予的范围。

branches.en: CONSCIENCE AND WILL: worship without pressure, and the inner question of whether the will is determined.
branches.cn: 良心与意志：不受压力的礼拜，以及意志是否被决定的内在问题。

intro.en: The whole family rests on one Latin adjective for a free person, with noun, verb and agent endings added over time; the Germanic near synonym freedom belongs to a separate history.
intro.cn: 整个家族都依托一个表示自由人的拉丁形容词，随后加上名词、动词与施事后缀；日耳曼语的近义词「自由」属于另一段历史。

latinIntro.en: The Latin forms below show the adjective, its abstract noun and the derived adjective for generosity of character.
latinIntro.cn: 下列拉丁形式展示了这个形容词、它的抽象名词，以及由它派生、表示气度宽厚的形容词。

items.meaning: the condition of a free person
items.example: The charter guaranteed the liberty of every citizen.
items.exampleCN: 宪章保障每位公民的自由。

items.meaning: of a free person; generous, open-minded
items.meaningCN: 自由人的；宽厚的、开明的
items.example: A liberal education once meant the studies fit for a free person.
items.exampleCN: 「自由教育」原指适合自由人研习的科目。

items.meaningCN: 宽厚，尤指态度上的宽容
items.example: The host was praised for his liberality.
items.exampleCN: 主人因宽厚而受到称赞。

items.example: The troops liberated the occupied town.
items.exampleCN: 部队解放了被占领的城镇。

items.example: The museum marks the anniversary of the liberation.
items.exampleCN: 博物馆纪念解放周年。

items.example: The general was hailed as a liberator.
items.exampleCN: 那位将军被称颂为解放者。

items.meaning: one who holds personal freedom to be the highest value
items.meaningCN: 主张个人自由至上的人
items.example: The candidate described himself as a libertarian.
items.exampleCN: 这位候选人自称自由意志论者。

items.example: The measure was criticised as illiberal.
items.exampleCN: 这项措施被批评为不宽容。

items.example: The villagers gave thanks for their deliverance.
items.exampleCN: 村民们为获救而致谢。

latinEntries.meaning: freedom; the status of a free person
